OracleTier Anew · today systems
Oracle Unifier Solution Architect (Hands-On Configuration Lead)
United States · Posted: 2026-10-28
Comp: Not listed
Job description
We are seeking a highly technical, hands-on Oracle Unifier Solution Architect to lead the design, configuration, and implementation of our enterprise PMIS platform supporting a multi-billion-dollar capital projects program.

This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who operates at an architect level but remains deeply involved in system configuration and build. You will own the Unifier environment end-to-end—translating complex business requirements into scalable system solutions—while leading external consultants and aligning a broad set of stakeholders.

This role is ideal for someone who prefers building over managing but can still lead through expertise and influence.

Responsibilities:

System Architecture & Design

Define the overall Unifier system architecture, data structures, and configuration strategy

Design scalable solutions aligned to program needs across cost, change, contracts, and reporting

Establish standards for CBS, workflows, forms, and governance frameworks

 

Hands-On Configuration & Build

Personally configure and deploy Unifier business processes (BPs), workflows, and forms 

Build and optimize:
 

Cost management (budgets, commitments, actuals, accruals, EAC)

Change management workflows

Contract and invoice management processes

Funding and cashflow tracking

RFI and project workflows

Ensure system performance, usability, and data integrity

 

Implementation & Delivery

Own the end-to-end implementation lifecycle (design, build, test, deploy, iterate)

Drive rapid implementation with an MVP mindset, balancing speed with long-term scalability

Lead system testing, issue resolution, and continuous improvement

 

Stakeholder Leadership

Partner with Program Controls, Finance, Construction, and Technology teams to translate requirements into system solutions

Lead and coordinate external consultants and system integrators

Act as the central point of accountability for Unifier delivery

 

Integration & Data Strategy

Support integration with:
 

Scheduling platforms (e.g., Primavera Cloud)

ERP systems (e.g., Oracle Fusion)

Data lake / reporting environments

Ensure alignment of system data structures across platforms

 

Communication & Governance 

Provide clear, executive-level updates on system progress, risks, and decisions

Drive alignment across stakeholders in a fast-paced, evolving environment

Establish and enforce system governance and best practices

Sr. Director - Central Estimating & Planning - GFD
Indianapolis, Indiana, United States of America · Posted: 2026-10-06T16:18:01.016+0000
Comp: $163,500 - $239,800
Job description
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us. 
JOB POSITION OVERVIEW:
The Sr. Director, Central Estimating & Planning sits within the Capital Portfolio Operations (PortOps) team in Global Facilities Delivery (GFD), part of Manufacturing & Quality, and reports to the AVP, Capital Portfolio Operations. This role owns the capital estimate from initial concept through project closeout for GFD's capital portfolio of approximately $65 billion, and is accountable for establishing the estimating and planning strategy that delivers predictable and accurate cost outcomes across that portfolio. Scope includes basis of estimate, basis of schedule, estimate and schedule validation, contingency and allowance setting, and benchmarking. This role is accountable for developing the team’s structure, defining the hiring plan, hiring and onboarding estimators, and establishing the team’s operating processes for this function. The role works across a large number of senior stakeholders, including Network AVPs, program directors, Finance, and GPCO, and is expected to influence decisions through others where it does not hold direct authority. Estimating strategy is owned by this role and is aligned with the project controls framework and tools established by the Global Portfolio Controls Office (GPCO).
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Responsibilities are expressed as owned capability areas:
Owns the capital estimate from initial concept through project closeout, maintaining estimate continuity across each project phase and funding gate.
Establishes and maintains the estimating and planning strategy for the capital portfolio, with defined targets for estimate accuracy and cost predictability, and reports performance against those targets.
Owns basis of estimate, estimate plan, and estimate validation across the capital portfolio.
Owns basis of schedule, schedule design plan, and schedule validation across the capital portfolio.
Owns CSRA (contingency and allowance setting) for the capital portfolio.
Validates cost and schedule changes that escalate to the executive level.
Owns benchmarking of estimates and schedules against industry and internal data.
Builds the Central Estimating & Planning function: defines the hiring plan and recruits, hires, and onboards a team of estimators; plus, plans for surge capacity contract estimating support.
Establishes team structure, operating processes, and ways of working for a newly built team, consistent with methodology and tools established by GPCO.
Aligns estimating strategy and practice with the project controls framework and tools established by GPCO.
Manages estimate and schedule positions with multiple senior stakeholders who have competing priorities, including Network AVPs, program directors, and Finance, and defends those positions in governance forums (CPMO, PASC, SteerCos).
Pulls in subject matter experts from GPCO and other PortOps functions as needed to support estimate and schedule development.
BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:
This position requires a combination of technical or project management education, direct experience delivering capital projects, and strong analytical and communication skills.
Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field.
10+ years of experience in cost estimating on large capital projects, including estimating individual projects with a total installed cost greater than $1 billion, and experience managing a team with direct reports.
Qualified applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Lilly will not provide support for or sponsor work authorization or visas for this role, including but not limited to F-1 CPT, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, J-1, H-1B, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, or L-1.
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:
Experience estimating individual projects or programs with a total installed cost of $5 billion or greater.
Demonstrated ability to influence decisions through others and manage multiple senior stakeholders with competing demands.
Experience standing up or scaling an estimating or project controls function, including hiring and onboarding staff.
Previous experience in pharmaceutical manufacturing or pharmaceutical capital project delivery.
Proficient in cost estimating and scheduling methods and tools (e.g., AACE methodology, Primavera P6, Oracle Unifier).
Certified Cost Professional (CCP), Certified Estimating Professional (CEP), or PMP certification.
Proven ability to operate effectively within GMP-regulated pharmaceutical environments.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:
Position Location: 
Indianapolis, IN
Travel Percentage (%): 
~30%

Actual compensation will depend on a candidate’s education, experience, skills, and geographic location.  The anticipated wage for this position is
$163,500 - $239,800
Full-time equivalent employees also will be eligible for a company bonus (depending, in part, on company and individual performance). Senior Program C&Q Lead
Houston, Texas, United States of America · Posted: 2026-10-16T14:20:37.548+0000
Comp: $163,500 - $239,800
Job description
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us. 
The Global Facilities Delivery (GFD) Organization, part of Manufacturing & Quality, delivers new and renovated capital assets around the world. Our mission is accomplished through a highly leveraged organization of project management, engineering, construction, and qualification contractors. Many of the assets delivered focus on medical innovation and delivering innovative solutions to patients. Some of the assets delivered will expand the supply of existing medicines or strengthen the supply chain.
The Senior Program C&Q Lead owns commissioning and qualification (C&Q) for an assigned capital program or site – setting the C&Q strategy, driving field execution, and delivering systems that are validated, GMP-compliant, and ready for reliable startup and handover to Site Operations. This is a senior individual contributor role: the Senior Program C&Q Lead is Lilly's technical owner and single point of accountability for C&Q on the program.
Key Responsibilities
C&Q Strategy, Planning & Scheduling
Create, own, and implement the C&Q strategy, plans, and schedules for the assigned program, aligned to Lilly's CQV standards and to the relevant manufacturing platform and network requirements (API, LAPI, PDN, LMF).
Define system boundaries, system classification, and the commissioning and qualification scope and turnover package structure so testing is executed once, at the right level of rigor, with no gaps or duplication.
Build and maintain the integrated C&Q schedule, including critical path analysis, 2–4 week look-aheads, and resource loading; integrate C&Q sequencing with construction, automation, and startup milestones.
Forecast C&Q resource demand and partner with program leadership and service providers to secure the right contingent and contract resources at the right time.
C&Q Execution & Field Coordination
Direct day-to-day C&Q execution in the field through C&Q firms and contingent C&Q node leads; ensure adherence to C&Q procedures and program strategy in all activities.
Review and accept mechanical completion (MC) turnover from construction management and C&Q firms, and drive closeout of punch list items with C&Q firms and SWAT teams.
Coordinate pre-commissioning activities including utility priming, instrument calibration, automation downloads, installation of consumables (e.g., filter cartridges), and VFD setup.
Coordinate across nodes and with site utilities on demand for temporary power and utilities (e.g., steam, water) and on wastewater discharge and loading of drains and sumps.
Partner with the mechanical and construction teams on lock-out/tag-out (LOTO) and the transition of systems from construction control to commissioning control.
Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT)
Plan and lead FAT for the program – defining test strategy, reviewing and approving protocols, setting schedules, and coordinating with vendors, engineering, and construction so equipment and systems are verified ahead of shipment and startup.
Witness FAT at vendor sites, disposition findings and deviations, and confirm resolution before release to site.
Qualification, Documentation & Handover
Author, review, and approve commissioning and qualification protocols, test scripts, deviations, and summary reports; ensure right-first-time execution and audit-ready records.
Ensure structured capture and turnover of engineering and asset information through Project Information Management (PIM) – specifications, drawings, test records, as-builts, and handover data packages – so assets transition to Operations complete and audit-ready.
Lead or support system handover to the User team and Site Operations, including punch resolution, training support, and documentation turnover.
Quality, Compliance & Safety
Ensure C&Q activities meet regulatory, corporate, and site quality requirements; partner with Quality and support inspection readiness for the program.
Manage C&Q change and deviation processes, including impact assessment against the approved scope and escalation of compliance risk.
Enforce a strong safety culture by ensuring all commissioning and qualification activities comply with site safety standards and industry best practices, promoting a safe working environment for all team members.
Technical Expertise & Continuous Improvement
Serve as the program's C&Q subject matter expert, providing technical direction and coaching to contract and contingent C&Q resources without a direct reporting relationship.
Continuously identify opportunities to improve C&Q practices across the program, driving efficiency while maintaining compliance.
Feed lessons learned back into GFD CQV standards, methods, and templates so improvements are captured for future programs.
Reporting & Governance
Report progress, risks, and issues directly to program leadership and the Senior Director, Asset Delivery, providing clear visibility into C&Q status, quality, and compliance risk.
Report program C&Q metrics including change management against initial scope, progress and performance measurement, 2–4 week look-aheads, critical path analysis, and resourcing.
General
Collaborate across detailed design, project engineering, construction, automation, Quality, Site Operations, and program teams; take on priorities as they emerge.
Qualifications Required
Bachelor's in Engineering, Life Sciences, or a related field.
15+ years of commissioning, qualification, and validation (CQV) experience in GMP-regulated environments, including leading C&Q execution on capital projects.
Demonstrated hands-on experience across the validation lifecycle – commissioning, qualification, systems turnover, startup support, and handover to operations.
Experience planning and executing Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) with equipment vendors.
Ability to travel, both within and outside the US as required, approximately 35% expected; site-based program assignments may require extended field deployment.
Qualified applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Lilly will not provide support for or sponsor work authorization or visas for this role, including but not limited to F-1 CPT, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, J-1, H-1B, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, or L-1.
Preferred
Experience directing C&Q contractors and service providers and coordinating field execution alongside construction teams in an active construction environment.
Proven ability to influence and deliver results without direct authority in a complex, matrixed, contractor-leveraged organization.
Experience delivering C&Q on greenfield and/or GMP-regulated pharmaceutical or life-sciences facilities.
Experience on mega capital expansion projects ($100 million+ in total installed cost).
Experience with CQV in API, LAPI, sterile / parenteral, and/or biologics facilities.
Master's degree in engineering, science, or a related field.
Professional credentials such as ISPE CPIP, PE, or PMP.
Familiarity with tools such as validation / commissioning platforms (e.g., Kneat), Oracle Unifier, Smartsheet, and Power BI.

Actual compensation will depend on a candidate’s education, experience, skills, and geographic location.  The anticipated wage for this position is
$163,500 - $239,800
Full-time equivalent employees also will be eligible for a company bonus (depending, in part, on company and individual performance). In addition, Lilly offers a comprehensive benefit program to eligible employees, including eligibility to participate in a company-sponsored 401(k); pension; vacation benefits; eligibility for medical, dental, vision and prescription drug benefits; flexible benefits (e.g., healthcare and/or dependent day care flexible spending accounts); life insurance and death benefits; certain time off and leave of absence benefits; and well-being benefits (e.g., employee assistance program, fitness benefits, and employee clubs and activities).Lilly reserves the right to amend, modify, or terminate its compensation and benefit programs in its sole discretion and Lilly’s compensation practices and guidelines will apply regarding the details of any promotion or transfer of Lilly employees.

Report program C&Q metrics including change management against initial scope, progress and performance measurement, 2–4 week look-aheads, critical path analysis, and resourcing.
General
Collaborate across detailed design, project engineering, construction, automation, Quality, Site Operations, and program teams; take on priorities as they emerge.
Qualifications 
Required
Bachelor's in Engineering, Life Sciences, or a related field.
15+ years of commissioning, qualification, and validation (CQV) experience in GMP-regulated environments, including leading C&Q execution on capital projects.
Demonstrated hands-on experience across the validation lifecycle – commissioning, qualification, systems turnover, startup support, and handover to operations.
Experience planning and executing Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) with equipment vendors.
Ability to travel, both within and outside the US as required, approximately 35% expected; site-based program assignments may require extended field deployment.
Qualified applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Lilly will not provide support for or sponsor work authorization or visas for this role, including but not limited to F-1 CPT, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, J-1, H-1B, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, or L-1.
Preferred
Experience directing C&Q contractors and service providers and coordinating field execution alongside construction teams in an active construction environment.
Proven ability to influence and deliver results without direct authority in a complex, matrixed, contractor-leveraged organization.
Experience delivering C&Q on greenfield and/or GMP-regulated pharmaceutical or life-sciences facilities.
Experience on mega capital expansion projects ($100 million+ in total installed cost).
Experience with CQV in API, LAPI, sterile / parenteral, and/or biologics facilities.
Master's degree in engineering, science, or a related field.
Professional credentials such as ISPE CPIP, PE, or PMP.
Familiarity with tools such as validation / commissioning platforms (e.g., Kneat), Oracle Unifier, Smartsheet, and Power BI.

                        Position Summary
                    

Our Deloitte Strategy & Transactions team helps guide clients through their most critical moments and transformational initiatives. From strategy to execution, this team delivers integrated, end-to-end support and advisory services covering valuation modeling, cost optimization, restructuring, business design and transformation, infrastructure and real estate, mergers and acquisitions (M&A), and sustainability. Work alongside clients every step of the way, helping them navigate new challenges, avoid financial pitfalls, and provide practical solutions at every stage of their journey—before, during, and after any major transformational projects or transactions.
Do you want to help clients identify key business issues to drive meaningful change? Join our team of Infrastructure & Capital Projects professionals who bring industry experience, innovation, and specialized knowledge to help our clients make the best decision for their business. Are you interested in helping clients answer critical, mission-based questions such as ‘how do we complete major infrastructure projects on-time and within budget?’ and ‘how do we make use of new technologies to improve the construction process?’ If you are seeking a role that offers you the opportunity to create value and minimize risk for our clients, while allowing you to develop personally and professionally, consider a career at Deloitte!
Recruiting for this role ends on 10/27/2026.
Work you’ll do 
As a Senior Consultant 
on the Capital Projects team, you will be responsible for:
Advising clients on infrastructure and capital project decisions that align with organizational objectives
Designing and assessing structures, systems, controls, and construction management processes that support capital project delivery
Analyzing project cost and schedule data through construction auditing, schedule analysis, litigation support, and construction analytics
Evaluating capital project programs and project risks to improve accountability and transparency across the asset management lifecycle
Supporting client delivery through issue resolution, accurate work products, and proposal development
Providing financial advisory assistance in mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, and financial restructuring
Assessing capital project programs, construction management processes and controls, and project risk
Assist in proposal development, as requested
A successful candidate would possess these skills: 
Ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a team 
Effective written and verbal communication skills 
Meticulous attention to detail and quality of work product 
Ability to build and sustain professional relationships 
Ability to lead projects or workstreams 
Ability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced and dynamic environment 
Strong interpersonal skills and professional demeanor 
Ability to meet deadlines 
Ability to provide clear guidance to others
The team 
Deloitte’s Infrastructure and Real Estate team are trusted advisors to clients in managing physical assets throughout their lifecycle.  We help them unlock value from their real estate portfolios and functions by developing strategies, optimizing operating models and organizational design, and leveraging technology enablement.
  
Qualifications required: 
Bachelor’s degree in engineering or construction management 
4+ years of engineering/construction related experience 
MUST have experience administering or managing construction projects requiring Davis-Bacon Act compliance and regulations, including prevailing wage requirements, wage determinations, certified payroll reporting, related documentation, and Public Works Administration hiring practices
Experience analyzing project cost and schedule data using construction industry techniques and software applications
Proficiency with word processing, spreadsheet, presentation creation, and internet research tools 
Experience using artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled tools and digital technologies to improve efficiency, support analysis, and enhance the quality of work products
Ability to travel 30%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve.
Limited sponsorship may be available 
Preferred: 
Master’s degree in engineering or construction management, or MBA 
One or more of the following certifications: PE, ASA, PMP, CFA, CFE, CCE or CPA 
Proficiency in using Project Management tools, including Oracle Unifier, Procore, Hexagon Ecosys, Kahua, Primavera P6, and Power BI
Experience in a professional services firm 
International engagement experience 
Multi-lingual

A reasonable estimate of the current range is $110,700 to $218,300.
You may also be eligible to participate in a discretionary annual incentive program, subject to the rules governing the program, whereby an award, if any, depends on various factors, including, without limitation, individual and organizational performance.

 SCAM ALERT

Caution against fraudulent job offers!

We have been informed of instances where jobseekers are led to believe of fictitious job opportunities with Deloitte US (“Deloitte”). In one or more such cases, false promises of actual or potential selection, or initiation or completion of the recruitment formalities appear to have been or are being made. Some jobseekers appear to have been asked to pay money to specified bank accounts of individuals or entities as a condition of their selection for a ‘job’ with Deloitte. These individuals or entities are in no way connected with Deloitte and do not represent or otherwise act on behalf of Deloitte.

We would like to clarify that:

At Deloitte, ethics and integrity are fundamental and not negotiable.

We are against corruption and neither offer bribes nor accept them, nor induce or permit any other party to make or receive bribes on our behalf.

We have not authorized any party or person to collect any money from jobseekers in any form whatsoever for promises of getting jobs in Deloitte.

We consider candidates on merit and that we provide an equal opportunity to eligible applicants.

No one other than designated Deloitte personnel (e.g., a Deloitte recruiter or Deloitte hiring partner) is permitted to extend any job offer from Deloitte.

Anyone who at any time has made or makes any payment to any party in exchange for promises of job or selection for a job with Deloitte or any matter related to this (including those for ‘registration’, ‘verification’ or ‘security deposit’) or otherwise engages with any such person who has made or makes fraudulent promises or offers, does so (or has done so) entirely at their own risk. Deloitte takes no responsibility or liability for any such unauthorized or fraudulent actions or engagements. We encourage jobseekers to exercise caution.

 SCAM ALERT

Caution against fraudulent job offers!

We have been informed of instances where jobseekers are led to believe of fictitious job opportunities with Deloitte US (“Deloitte”). In one or more such cases, false promises of actual or potential selection, or initiation or completion of the recruitment formalities appear to have been or are being made. Some jobseekers appear to have been asked to pay money to specified bank accounts of individuals or entities as a condition of their selection for a ‘job’ with Deloitte. These individuals or entities are in no way connected with Deloitte and do not represent or otherwise act on behalf of Deloitte.

We would like to clarify that:

At Deloitte, ethics and integrity are fundamental and not negotiable.

We are against corruption and neither offer bribes nor accept them, nor induce or permit any other party to make or receive bribes on our behalf.

We have not authorized any party or person to collect any money from jobseekers in any form whatsoever for promises of getting jobs in Deloitte.

We consider candidates on merit and that we provide an equal opportunity to eligible applicants.

No one other than designated Deloitte personnel (e.g., a Deloitte recruiter or Deloitte hiring partner) is permitted to extend any job offer from Deloitte.

Anyone who at any time has made or makes any payment to any party in exchange for promises of job or selection for a job with Deloitte or any matter related to this (including those for ‘registration’, ‘verification’ or ‘security deposit’) or otherwise engages with any such person who has made or makes fraudulent promises or offers, does so (or has done so) entirely at their own risk. Deloitte takes no responsibility or liability for any such unauthorized or fraudulent actions or engagements. We encourage jobseekers to exercise caution.

Job description
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us. 
Position Brand Description
The Global Facilities Delivery (GFD) Organization, part of Corporate Engineering, delivers new and renovated capital assets around the world.  Our mission is accomplished through a highly leveraged organization of design, construction and qualification contractors.
Many of the assets delivered focus on manufacturing of medical innovations and delivering innovative solutions to patients.  Some of the assets delivered support an expansion in supply of existing medicines. 
Role Summary
The Advisor, Project Information Management & Document Control serves as the enterprise process owner for project information management, document control, and information governance within Global Facilities Delivery (GFD). The role establishes and governs the standards, processes, systems, and digital delivery requirements used to manage project information across the capital project lifecycle. The Advisor provides strategic leadership for information governance, project information systems, and digital delivery practices, ensuring information quality, consistency, traceability, compliance, and operational readiness across the global portfolio while driving continuous improvement and capability development.
Key Responsibilities
Serve as the enterprise Process Owner for Project Information Management and Document Control, defining governance, standards, procedures, and performance expectations across the global capital project portfolio.
Own and continuously improve Project Information Management processes governing project documentation, records management, metadata, information lifecycle management, retention requirements, and digital handover.
Author, maintain, and govern enterprise standards, SOPs, Project Delivery Work Instructions (PDWIs), templates, workflows, and guidance documents supporting consistent information management practices across all projects.
Establish and govern Owner Information Requirements (OIRs), Common Data Environment (CDE) standards, metadata structures, naming conventions, document classifications, and approval workflows to create a consistent digital ecosystem across internal and external delivery partners.
Provide governance, assurance, and compliance oversight of Project Information Management practices, conducting assessments, audits, performance reviews, and corrective action programs to ensure adherence to enterprise requirements.
Serve as business owner for Project Information Management systems and technologies, defining enterprise requirements, governance models, integration strategies, and data stewardship across digital delivery platforms.
Establish standards and requirements for engineering deliverables, contractor documentation, construction records, commissioning and qualification records, turnover packages, and operational handover information throughout the project lifecycle.
Define information management requirements for external delivery partners, including A/E, EPCM, Construction Management, and Contractor organizations, ensuring consistent information exchange, document control, digital handover, and compliance with enterprise standards.
Lead capability-building initiatives for the Project Information Management and Document Control community, providing training, mentoring, guidance, and subject matter expertise to strengthen organizational capability and process adoption. This responsibility aligns with the JD's governance and enterprise ownership focus.
Drive continuous improvement, digital transformation, and innovation in Project Information Management, evaluating emerging technologies, advancing digital delivery strategies, and implementing improvements that enhance information quality, accessibility, traceability, and lifecycle management.
Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, construction management, or related field, or equivalent experience.
At least 8 years of experience in engineering, project engineering, information and document control, or similar field.
Qualified applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Lilly will not provide support for or sponsor work authorization or visas for this role, including but not limited to F-1 CPT, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, J-1, H-1B, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, or L-1
Preferred Qualifications
Professional certification in Information Management, Records Management, Project Management, or Digital Delivery (e.g., CRM, IGP, PMP, PMI-CP, AIIM, BuildingSMART, Autodesk Certified Professional).
Proficiency with Project Information Management and Document Control platforms such as Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC), Oracle Unifier, Procore, Aconex, SharePoint, and related systems.
Strong knowledge of information governance, document control, records management, Common Data Environments (CDEs), metadata standards, and digital handover practices.
Familiarity with industry standards and frameworks, including ISO 19650 and information lifecycle management principles.
Strong analytical, communication, stakeholder management, and organizational skills, with the ability to drive adoption of enterprise standards and digital transformation initiatives.
Additional Information
Travel is required up to 25%

Capital Cost Estimator – Mechanical, Electrical and Plumbing (MEP)
Indianapolis, Indiana, United States of America · Posted: 2026-10-14T14:20:36.192+0000
Comp: $130,500 - $211,200
Job description
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us. 
Position Brand Description:
The Global Facilities Delivery (GFD) Organization, part of Corporate Engineering, delivers new and renovated capital assets around the world.  Our mission is accomplished through a highly leveraged organization of design, construction and qualification contractors.
Many of the assets delivered focus on manufacturing medical innovations and delivering innovative solutions to patients.  Some of the assets delivered support an expansion in supply of existing medicines. 
Role Summary:
The MEP Capital Cost Estimator develops owner-side Class 5 through Class 1 estimates for the mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, building controls, and utility distribution systems supporting complex pharmaceutical manufacturing and infrastructure projects. The role converts evolving engineering scope, design information, execution strategies, market data, and benchmarks into complete, traceable, and decision-ready estimates. The role will assess installation labor, equipment setting, supports, testing, commissioning interfaces, temporary services, and MEP trade indirect costs.
Key Objectives/Deliverables:
Develop capital cost estimates from Class 5 through Class 1 using methods appropriate to the maturity of project definition, including capacity-factored, parametric, assembly-level, unit-rate, and detailed quantity takeoff methods.
Prepare estimate plans, estimate workbooks, quantity takeoffs, pricing build-ups, bases of estimate, assumptions, exclusions, qualifications, and supporting documentation for assigned scopes.
Interpret business requirements, basis-of-design information, drawings, specifications, equipment lists, process flow diagrams, P&IDs, layouts, schedules, contracting strategies, and construction execution plans to define estimate scope and cost.
Build labor, material, equipment, subcontract, construction management, temporary facilities, logistics, indirect cost, escalation, and contingency inputs appropriate to the assigned discipline and estimate class.
Obtain and normalize vendor budget quotes, contractor pricing, market rates, productivity factors, location factors, escalation inputs, and historical cost data.
Identify scope gaps, overlaps, ambiguities, estimate risks, cost drivers, and missing inputs; document their treatment in the estimate and Basis of Estimate.
Perform cost benchmarking using historical project data, comparable facilities, market intelligence, and normalized unit-cost metrics to validate estimate reasonableness, identify cost drivers, and explain variances. Develop and maintain internal benchmarking databases using actual costs from completed and active projects, and maintain current insights into relevant external benchmarks. Complete estimate reconciliation, variance analysis, and estimate-to-estimate bridging as scope and design mature.
Support multidisciplinary estimate reviews and page-turns with project teams, engineering partners, construction partners, procurement, and project controls.
Prepare estimate summaries and clear cost narratives for project reviews, funding decisions, value engineering, option analysis, bid evaluation, and change assessment.
Maintain estimates in Oracle Unifier PMIS to provide a complete and auditable estimate trail.
Minimum Requirements:
Bachelor's degree in engineering, construction management, quantity surveying, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience. 
At least 5 years of direct capital cost estimating experience for industrial, manufacturing, life sciences, or similarly complex capital projects. 
Demonstrated experience personally developing estimates across multiple levels of project definition, including conceptual and detailed estimates.
Qualified applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Lilly will not provide support for or sponsor work authorization or visas for this role, including but not limited to F-1 CPT, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, J-1, H-1B, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, or L-1
Additional Preferences:
Experience estimating pharmaceutical, biotechnology, chemical, food, semiconductor, advanced manufacturing, or other process-intensive facilities. 
Experience with both owner and contractor estimating environments. 
Professional certification such as AACE Certified Estimating Professional (CEP), Certified Cost Professional (CCP), or an equivalent credential. 
Experience with benchmarking, estimate reconciliation, value engineering, bid leveling, and change estimate development. 
Familiarity with CSI MasterFormat, Uniformat, equipment-based process estimating, and owner work breakdown structures. 
Ability to work independently, manage multiple estimate assignments, and clearly communicate limitations and uncertainty.
 
Additional Information:
Must reside in or relocate to Indianapolis, Indiana, with onsite presence at Lilly Technology Center-South
Ability to travel up to 25% including domestic and international project locations

Capital Cost Estimator – Industrial Process and Pharmaceutical Equipment
Indianapolis, Indiana, United States of America · Posted: 2026-10-14T14:20:36.198+0000
Comp: $130,500 - $211,200
Job description
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us. 
Position Brand Description:
The Global Facilities Delivery (GFD) Organization, part of Corporate Engineering, delivers new and renovated capital assets around the world.  Our mission is accomplished through a highly leveraged organization of design, construction and qualification contractors.
Many of the assets delivered focus on manufacturing medical innovations and delivering innovative solutions to patients.  Some of the assets delivered support an expansion in supply of existing medicines. 
Role Summary:
The Industrial Process Capital Cost Estimator develops owner-side Class 5 through Class 1 estimates for major pharmaceutical process equipment, packaged systems, process piping, hygienic systems, process utilities, equipment installation, and related construction scopes. The role converts evolving process and engineering scope, equipment data, vendor information, execution strategies, market data, and benchmarks into complete, traceable, and decision-ready estimates. The role will assess equipment freight, rigging, setting, modularization, fabrication, specialty welding, testing, passivation, validation support, spare parts, and vendor field services.
Key Objectives/Deliverables:
Develop capital cost estimates from Class 5 through Class 1 using methods appropriate to the maturity of project definition, including capacity-factored, parametric, assembly-level, unit-rate, and detailed quantity takeoff methods.
Prepare estimate plans, estimate workbooks, quantity takeoffs, pricing build-ups, bases of estimate, assumptions, exclusions, qualifications, and supporting documentation for assigned scopes.
Interpret business requirements, basis-of-design information, drawings, specifications, equipment lists, process flow diagrams, P&IDs, layouts, schedules, contracting strategies, and construction execution plans to define estimate scope and cost.
Build labor, material, equipment, subcontract, construction management, temporary facilities, logistics, indirect cost, escalation, and contingency inputs appropriate to the assigned discipline and estimate class.
Obtain and normalize vendor budget quotes, contractor pricing, market rates, productivity factors, location factors, escalation inputs, and historical cost data.
Identify scope gaps, overlaps, ambiguities, estimate risks, cost drivers, and missing inputs; document their treatment in the estimate and Basis of Estimate.
Perform cost benchmarking using historical project data, comparable facilities, market intelligence, and normalized unit-cost metrics to validate estimate reasonableness, identify cost drivers, and explain variances. Develop and maintain internal benchmarking databases using actual costs from completed and active projects and maintain current insights into relevant external benchmarks. Complete estimate reconciliation, variance analysis, and estimate-to-estimate bridging as scope and design mature.
Support multidisciplinary estimate reviews and page-turns with project teams, engineering partners, construction partners, procurement, and project controls.
Prepare estimate summaries and clear cost narratives for project reviews, funding decisions, value engineering, option analysis, bid evaluation, and change assessment.
Maintain estimates in Oracle Unifier PMIS to provide a complete and auditable estimate trail.
Minimum Requirements:
Bachelor's degree in engineering, construction management, quantity surveying, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience. 
At least 5 years of direct capital cost estimating experience for industrial, manufacturing, life sciences, or similarly complex capital projects. 
Demonstrated experience personally developing estimates across multiple levels of project definition, including conceptual and detailed estimates.
Qualified applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Lilly will not provide support for or sponsor work authorization or visas for this role, including but not limited to F-1 CPT, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, J-1, H-1B, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, or L-1
 
Additional Preferences:
Experience estimating pharmaceutical, biotechnology, chemical, food, semiconductor, advanced manufacturing, or other process-intensive facilities. 
Experience with both owner and contractor estimating environments. 
Professional certification such as AACE Certified Estimating Professional (CEP), Certified Cost Professional (CCP), or an equivalent credential. 
Experience with benchmarking, estimate reconciliation, value engineering, bid leveling, and change estimate development. 
Familiarity with CSI MasterFormat, Uniformat, equipment-based process estimating, and owner work breakdown structures. 
Ability to work independently, manage multiple estimate assignments, and clearly communicate limitations and uncertainty.
Additional Information:
Must reside in or relocate to Indianapolis, Indiana with onsite presence at Lilly Technology Center-South
Ability to travel up to 25%, including domestic and international project locations

Advisor/Sr Advisor - Program Governance and Operations - GFD
Richmond, Virginia, United States of America · Posted: 2026-10-20T20:27:00.520+0000
Comp: $130,500 - $211,200
Job description
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us. 
The Global Facilities Delivery (GFD) Organization, part of Manufacturing & Quality, delivers new and renovated capital assets around the world. Our mission is accomplished through a highly leveraged organization of project management, engineering, construction, and qualification contractors. Many of the assets delivered focus on medical innovation and delivering innovative solutions to patients. Some of the assets delivered will expand the supply of existing medicines or strengthen the supply chain.
The Advisor/Sr Advisor of Program Governance and Operations is embedded within a single large-scale capital program and serves as the strategic integrator and trusted advisor to the program's senior leader. The role exists to extend leadership capacity: it converts leadership intent into clear operating norms, execution plans, and communications, and it protects leadership focus by resolving friction before it requires escalation.
The role is accountable for the program's leadership operating rhythm, executive communications, program office operations, and organizational health. It works alongside the Program PMO Lead, who owns the program's PMO framework and delivery governance; this position operates the leadership forum layer that sits above that framework and ensures decisions are made when they need to be made.
The role partners with the Global Portfolio Operations organization and Project Integrators so that leadership reporting, communications, and executive briefings are consistent with enterprise standards and reconcile with wider portfolio messaging. Success is defined by a leadership team that is prepared, aligned, and able to focus on high-value priorities, and by a program community that operates with clarity, structure, and accountability.
Key Responsibilities
Strategic Advisory & Decision Support
Act as a trusted thought partner to the program's senior leader, supporting prioritization, escalation, and decision readiness across program initiatives.
Translate leadership direction into clear operating norms, execution plans, and communication artifacts.
Proactively identify risks, misalignments, and execution gaps, and surface recommendations with options and implications.
Ensure information from across the program and the wider organization reaches leadership in time to inform decisions.
Leadership Operating Rhythm
Own the program's leadership meeting cadence, including agendas, pre-reads, action tracking, documentation, and follow-through across leadership forums.
Facilitate leadership office hours, staff meetings, and administrative huddles, ensuring time is used effectively and outcomes are captured.
Prepare leadership for stage-gate reviews, funding decisions, and governance forums in partnership with the Program PMO Lead, who owns the underlying governance framework and delivery reporting.
Serve as steward of meeting and artifact quality, ensuring alignment with Lilly and GFD expectations.
Executive Communications & Stakeholder Alignment
Partner with Project Integrators to author and deliver executive-level communications on behalf of program leadership, including steering committee talking points, organizational announcements, event remarks, and external-facing messages.
Maintain consistent messaging across collaboration, email, and intranet channels as well as formal governance forums.
Provide clarity during ambiguity by distilling complex inputs into clear, actionable communication.
Program Office Operations & Workplace Readiness
Lead program office operations, including workspace readiness, site and office access, logistics, and change communications.
Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to ensure a seamless employee and partner experience at the program location.
Establish and maintain the program office as a functioning working environment for the integrated program team.
External Partner Interface
Act as a central coordination point between Lilly program leadership and external partners, including engineering, construction, staffing, and service providers.
Support onboarding and integration of new partners by clarifying roles, interfaces, and communication norms, working from the governance expectations set by the Program PMO Lead.
Ensure partner interactions reflect Lilly's standards for professionalism, alignment, and decision clarity.
Culture, Team Enablement & Organizational Health
Foster a high-trust, low-friction operating culture by resolving miscommunications, reducing unnecessary escalation, and protecting leadership focus.
Support mentoring and talent continuity programs as an active participant in building organizational relationships.
Champion collaboration, psychological safety, and continuous improvement across the program community.
Compliance & Records
Maintain program leadership documentation, decision records, and communications in compliance with applicable Lilly quality, records management, and regulatory standards.
Key Interfaces
Program senior leader (AVP or equivalent) — primary partner; the role exists to extend this leader's capacity and decision bandwidth.
Program workstream leads (engineering, construction, commissioning and qualification, quality) — coordination and information flow into leadership forums.
Global Portfolio Operations — alignment of leadership reporting and communications with enterprise standards and portfolio messaging.
External delivery and service partners — relationship management at the leadership interface.
Qualifications
Minimum
Bachelor's in Business, Engineering, Construction Management, Communications, or a related field.
10+ years of experience in program operations, business operations or senior program management roles within a large, complex organization.
Qualified applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Lilly will not provide support for or sponsor work authorization or visas for this role, including but not limited to F-1 CPT, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, J-1, H-1B, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, or L-1.
Preferred
Experience supporting greenfield and/or GMP-regulated pharmaceutical or life-sciences capital programs.
Experience on projects or programs of >$500M in total installed cost.
Demonstrated experience authoring executive-level written communications on behalf of senior leadership.
Demonstrated ability to operate effectively at both strategic and tactical levels without loss of quality, and to manage multiple concurrent workstreams under deadline pressure.
Experience working within large, matrixed organizations and alongside external partners and contractors.
Familiarity with capital delivery stage-gate and governance frameworks.
Experience preparing and supporting executive or board-level governance forums.
High emotional intelligence with mature stakeholder management and relationship-building capability.
Lean Six Sigma or continuous improvement experience.
Familiarity with tools such as Smartsheet, Power BI, SharePoint, and Microsoft Teams; exposure to Oracle Unifier or Primavera P6 is a plus.
Additional Information
Ability to travel, both within and outside the US as required, approximately 10% expected.

Project Controls / Cost Engineer - Huntsville
Huntsville, Alabama, United States of America · Posted: 2026-10-02T20:24:18.446+0000
Comp: $67,500 - $173,800
Job description
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us. 
Role Summary
 
The Advisor, Project Controls/Cost Engineer is the central steward for project controls functions within Global Facilities Delivery (GFD). This role ensures best-in-class practices in budgeting, cost control, earned value management, change and risk management, forecasting, and planning. The Project Controls Engineer provides strategic governance, leadership, and mentorship to project controls teams across a diverse portfolio of capital projects, with a strong focus on cost management and business value. The incumbent drives continuous improvement, compliance, and capability development, enabling successful project delivery and organizational growth. 
Key Responsibilities
 
Own and continuously improve project controls processes, standards, and systems to ensure alignment with industry best practices and organizational objectives. 
Conduct reviews of project controls across the portfolio, identifying gaps and driving corrective actions. 
Author and update standards, work instructions, and playbooks to establish and maintain best practices. 
Provide governance, mentoring, and training to project controls teams, fostering a culture of excellence and continuous learning. 
Lead organizational change initiatives to adopt advanced project management and controls methodologies. 
Advise project teams and contractors on effective project management systems for scope, cost, and schedule performance. 
Collaborate in developing project estimates, budgets, and value engineering strategies. 
Analyze contractor spend and invoices to ensure accuracy and prevent financial loss. 
Establish and maintain comprehensive risk management processes, including risk registers and probabilistic assessments. 
Implement robust change control processes in alignment with standard operating procedures. 
Ensure consistent and proper use of project controls systems, processes, and resources across all projects. 
Ensure proper application of company finance policies on capital projects, safeguarding compliance and financial integrity. 
Identify opportunities for process improvement and innovation in project controls, driving adoption of new tools and techniques. 
Minimum Qualifications
 
Bachelor’s degree in business management, finance, engineering, construction, or related field, or equivalent experience. 
At least 8 years of experience in project control, quantity surveying, or similar field. 
Qualified applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Lilly will not provide support for or sponsor work authorization or visas for this role, including but not limited to F-1 CPT, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, J-1, H-1B, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, or L-1.
Preferred Qualifications

Indianapolis, Indiana, United States of America · Posted: 2026-10-06T16:18:01.043+0000

Job description
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us. 
JOB POSITION OVERVIEW:
The Network Performance & Assurance Lead sits within the Capital Portfolio Operations (PortOps) team in Global Facilities Delivery (GFD), part of Manufacturing & Quality, and reports to the AVP, Capital Portfolio Operations. This role supports an assigned network portfolio within GFD's capital delivery footprint (e.g., the API Dry Network, the Parenteral & Device Network, or another network as assigned by PortOps leadership) and is responsible for portfolio performance metrics, audit coordination, after-action reviews, and performance governance for that network's capital projects. The role coordinates GPCO controls standards, PMO resourcing, Operational Excellence & Governance processes, and Portfolio Comms support across the network's project teams. The role also confirms that projects in the assigned network are executing to GPCO-defined Project Controls standards, forecasts where Project Controls capacity is needed, conducts delivery assurance reviews, and reviews contractor and Managed Service Provider (MSP) cost data on the Owner's behalf. Network assignment is set by PortOps leadership and may change as GFD's network structure evolves. The role will be competent in each GFD standard process as it is introduced or revised, define what compliant execution looks like for project teams, and maintain process discipline across multiple senior stakeholders, influencing through others where it does not hold direct authority.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Responsibilities are expressed as owned capability areas, applied to the network portfolio this role is assigned to support:
Owns portfolio performance metrics for the assigned network's capital portfolio, including the reporting that feeds Project Unify dashboards for cost, schedule, and delivery performance across active projects in the network.
Coordinates process audits and compliance reviews for the network's projects, including scheduling and follow-up on findings, in partnership with the function that executes the audit.
Leads after-action reviews at project checkpoints and closeout and documents lessons learned for incorporation into GFD standard ways of working, in partnership with Operational Excellence & Governance.
Coordinates support to network project teams across GPCO controls standards, PMO resourcing, Operational Excellence & Governance processes, and Portfolio Comms.
Confirms that projects in the assigned network are executing to GPCO-defined Project Controls standards for cost, schedule, risk, and change management, and escalates deviations from those standards to GPCO.
Forecasts Project Controls capacity needs across the network's portfolio and identifies coverage gaps before projects reach critical phases.
Conducts delivery assurance reviews across the network's portfolio to identify where project controls processes are not being followed or where data is unreliable, and tracks corrective actions to closure.
Reviews Managed Service Provider (contractor) cost data, invoices, and forecasts on the Owner's behalf before they are incorporated into network portfolio reporting.
Owns performance governance for the network, including recurring portfolio performance reporting, participation in the network AVP's staff meetings (PALs), and continued development of Project Unify dashboards for the network AVP.
Owns contract exhibit coordination for the network's capital projects.
Establishes competency in each new or revised GFD standard process (PDWIs, SOPs, playbooks) ahead of network rollout, and serves as the network's reference point for correct application of that process.
Trains and coaches network project teams on GFD standard processes, and provides feedback to Operational Excellence & Governance on process gaps identified during application.
Maintains adherence to GFD standard processes across network projects, including with senior stakeholders, and escalates unresolved deviations to the AVP, Capital Portfolio Operations and the network AVP.
BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:
This position requires a combination of technical or project management education, direct experience delivering capital projects, and strong analytical and communication skills.
Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related field.
10+ years of experience in capital project delivery within industrial or manufacturing facilities, with experience in both project controls (cost, schedule, risk, or change management) and project management, and experience managing multiple senior stakeholders.
Qualified applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Lilly will not provide support for or sponsor work authorization or visas for this role, including but not limited to F-1 CPT, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, J-1, H-1B, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, or L-1
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:
Previous experience in pharmaceutical manufacturing or pharmaceutical capital project delivery.
Demonstrated ability to influence decisions through others and maintain process discipline with senior stakeholders.
Experience learning, applying, and training others on new processes or standards during organizational change.
Proficient in portfolio performance reporting, audit coordination, governance forums, or continuous improvement work.
Prior work with tools such as Smartsheet, Power BI, Oracle Unifier (PMIS), and Veeva Vault.
Experience embedded with or supporting a Network AVP and staff, without daily on-site support from GPCO or PMO.
Proven ability to operate effectively within GMP-regulated pharmaceutical environments.
Lean Six Sigma or PMP certification.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:
Position Location: 
Indianapolis, IN
Travel Percentage (%): 
~30-50%

Own the configuration and continuous improvement of Procore's Project Management tools — RFIs, Submittals, Drawings and Specifications, Meetings, Correspondence, Action Plans Inspections, observations and Tasks

Author standard operating procedures, job aids and facilitate training, and serve as the global partner concern point for workflow and system issues raised by project teams and external partners.

Job description
The Global Program Controls organization provides governance, reporting, controls processes, cost management support, and portfolio visibility to help Oracle Cloud Infrastructure deliver global data center programs with greater consistency, transparency, and execution discipline.  

We are seeking a hands-on technical leader to build and deploy the dashboards, reports, and AI-enabled analytics that help senior leadership understand operational performance, identify risks, and make informed decisions.

We have an established database foundation supported by data entry and governance processes. This role will build on that foundation by turning trusted data into reliable reporting products that people use in their daily work. The position will integrate information from Oracle Primavera Cloud (OPC), our scheduling platform, Oracle Primavera Unifier, and Oracle APEX applications and their underlying data sources.

 

The successful candidate will personally write queries, develop reporting models, build dashboards, connect systems, and deploy solutions into production. They will also establish reporting priorities and technical standards, working closely with business leaders, system owners, and technical teams. The role carries substantial technical ownership and can operate as a senior individual contributor leading cross-functional delivery.

Strong technical execution must be paired with analytical judgment and clear communication. This person should be able to investigate a discrepancy in the underlying data, explain its business significance, and deliver an accurate, concise view for executives.

 

Key Responsibilities

 

Dashboard and Reporting Development

 

Design, build, and deploy executive and operational dashboards that provide consistent views of schedules, milestones, delivery progress, dependencies, and emerging risks.

Translate business questions into defined metrics, data requirements, reporting logic, and intuitive visualizations with useful filters and drill-down capabilities.

Develop reusable datasets, SQL queries, and reporting models that support multiple dashboards and reduce manual report preparation.

Own reporting solutions through requirements, development, testing, deployment, user adoption, and ongoing maintenance.

 

Oracle Systems and Data Integration

 

Connect OPC, Unifier, and APEX-related data through supported APIs, database views, approved extracts, or existing integration pipelines, working with system owners to determine the appropriate approach.

Reconcile project identifiers, reporting periods, status definitions, and data granularity across 
systems
 so combined reports remain accurate and meaningful.

Build or extend automated data transformations and refresh workflows; investigate failed loads, stale data, and integration issues with the appropriate technical teams.

 

AI Models and Analytical Automation

 

Apply AI models, including large language models where appropriate, to practical reporting needs such as summarizing operational updates, explaining variances, and helping users explore approved data.

Use Python, model APIs, and other appropriate tools to prototype, evaluate, and deploy repeatable analytical workflows

Ground AI-generated insights in verifiable source data, test output quality against representative examples, and establish human review where needed.

Assess model accuracy, reliability, cost, and business usefulness before expanding a solution; protect confidential information through approved tools and access controls.

Use AI-assisted development effectively while independently reviewing and testing generated code, queries, calculations, and conclusions.

 

Reporting Reliability and Data Integrity

 

Build on existing governance processes to maintain documented metric definitions, calculation rules, source mappings, ownership, and data lineage.

Validate dashboard results against source systems and approved business definitions before release; make refresh timing and data limitations visible to users.

Implement appropriate access controls, version control, release documentation, and monitoring so reporting products remain secure and supportable.

Optimize query and dashboard performance, resolve defects, and work with data owners to address recurring quality issues at their source.

 

Executive Partnership and Technical Leadership

 

Work with executives and operational leaders to identify the decisions reporting must support and prioritize a practical delivery roadmap.

Present the few insights, risks, and actions that matter most, with enough supporting detail to answer follow-up questions.

Develop working fluency in data center operations, infrastructure deployment, hardware testing, commissioning, and server turn-up to interpret operational information accurately.

Lead cross-functional delivery with clear owners, milestones, and follow-through; provide technical direction to internal partners or vendors as needed.

Train users, gather feedback, and improve reporting products based on actual use and changing business needs.

Job description
Technical Integration Lead – Oracle Primavera Integrations and Data Migration

U.S. Citizenship Required:
 This position supports projects with specific access and/or contractual requirements. As a result, U.S. citizenship is required for consideration for this role.
About the Role

Oracle’s Construction and Engineering Global Business Unit (CEGBU) provides enterprise project and portfolio management solutions, including Primavera Unifier, P6 EPPM, Oracle Primavera Cloud, and Aconex.

We are seeking a 
Technical Integration Lead with proven, hands-on experience designing and developing integrations and data migrations using REST APIs through integration tools or middleware
, such as Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) or Project Integration Framework (PIF).

This role combines client-facing technical leadership with direct development responsibility. You will own delivery from requirements gathering and data mapping through solution design, development, unit testing, UAT support, and production deployment.

Direct integration development experience is essential. Experience limited to functional consulting, project coordination, or QA/testing on integration projects does not meet this requirement. Prior Oracle Primavera integration experience is an added advantage, but is not required.
Key Responsibilities

Lead client workshops to gather, clarify, and document integration and data migration requirements.

Translate business requirements into technical specifications, source-to-target data mappings, transformation rules, and validation criteria.

Assess and establish source and target system connectivity, including API access, authentication, authorization, and connectivity troubleshooting.

Design integration and data migration solutions for Oracle Primavera applications and external enterprise systems.

Personally build and configure integrations and migration workflows in OIC or PIF using REST API calls
, including request and response handling, data transformations, orchestration, and error handling.

Develop migration processes covering data extraction, transformation, loading, validation, and reconciliation.

Create and execute unit tests, troubleshoot defects, and verify data accuracy and integration behavior.

Support system integration testing and client UAT, including issue analysis and resolution.

Prepare deployment plans, support migration cutover activities, and deploy solutions to production.

Provide post-deployment support, technical documentation, and knowledge transfer.

Lead technical discussions, review development work, and guide team members while remaining actively involved in implementation.

Required Qualifications and Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field.

10+ years of relevant technical delivery, software development, or consulting experience, including client-facing responsibilities.

10+ years of integration architecture and development experience using enterprise integration tools or middleware.

Demonstrated hands-on experience personally developing and delivering REST API integrations and data migrations through middleware
, such as OIC, or PIF

Strong practical knowledge of REST APIs, HTTP methods and status codes, JSON/XML payloads, authentication, pagination, and API troubleshooting.

Experience implementing data mappings, transformations, orchestration, logging, error handling, retry mechanisms, and reconciliation.

Experience delivering solutions across the full lifecycle: requirements gathering, technical design, development, unit testing, UAT support, and production deployment.

Ability to independently translate client requirements into implementable technical solutions and resolve development and connectivity issues.

Strong communication, technical documentation, stakeholder management, and coaching skills.

Candidates must be able to explain integrations they personally developed, including the middleware used, REST API interactions, data mappings, technical challenges, and deployment approach.
Preferred Qualifications

Hands-on development experience with OIC or PIF.

Experience leading technical delivery for enterprise integration and data migration projects.

Good to have: Experience integrating or migrating data for Primavera Unifier, P6 EPPM, Oracle Primavera Cloud, or Aconex.

Good to have: Experience integrating Oracle applications with external enterprise systems such as SAP or Oracle E-Business Suite.

Oracle Primavera product or integration experience is preferred, not required. Candidates with strong hands-on middleware and REST API development experience in other enterprise application environments are encouraged to apply.

Job description
STV is seeking a 
Senior Project Controls Manager
 to join our growing Project Controls team in multiple client office locations across the United States. This leadership role will support some of the nation's most complex and high-profile aviation programs, including airport expansions, terminal developments, airside improvements, baggage handling systems, landside infrastructure, maintenance facilities, and capital improvement programs.
 
The Senior Project Controls Manager will serve as a trusted advisor to project teams and clients, providing strategic leadership for all aspects of project controls, including cost management, scheduling, forecasting, risk management, change management, performance reporting, and project analytics. This individual will play a critical role in helping clients successfully deliver major aviation infrastructure investments while supporting the continued growth of STV's national aviation practice.
 
The ideal candidate combines strong technical project controls expertise with exceptional leadership, client relationship management, and business development capabilities.
 
Responsibilities
Strategic Project Controls Leadership
Lead project controls functions across large-scale aviation programs from planning and design through construction, commissioning, and closeout.
Establish and implement project controls governance frameworks, procedures, standards, and best practices.
Serve as the primary project controls advisor to project managers, program executives, clients, and stakeholders.
Develop integrated project controls strategies encompassing cost, schedule, risk, forecasting, and performance management.
Identify and proactively mitigate project risks, opportunities, and performance challenges.
Cost Management & Financial Controls
Direct the development and management of project budgets, forecasts, cash flow analyses, and cost reports.
Perform cost trending, earned value analysis, variance analysis, and estimate-at-completion forecasting.
Review contractor payment applications, change orders, estimates, and cost proposals.
Support contingency planning, financial reporting, and executive decision-making.
Evaluate project performance and recommend corrective actions when necessary.
Scheduling & Performance Management
Oversee development, maintenance, and analysis of complex CPM schedules utilizing Primavera P6 and related tools.
Review contractor schedules and monitor compliance with project requirements.
Analyze critical path activities, schedule risks, float consumption, and recovery plans.
Develop and maintain integrated master schedules for major aviation programs.
Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) and project controls dashboards.
Risk & Change Management
Lead project risk identification, assessment, mitigation planning, and monitoring activities.
Facilitate risk workshops and maintain comprehensive risk registers.
Evaluate schedule and cost impacts associated with proposed project changes.
Support claims avoidance, dispute resolution, and change management processes.
Collaborate with project teams to implement effective corrective action strategies.
Client & Stakeholder Management
Develop and maintain strong relationships with airport authorities, airlines, program management teams, contractors, and design partners.
Deliver executive-level project controls reporting and presentations.
Support governance meetings, executive briefings, and client reviews.
Serve as a trusted advisor for project performance, program controls strategy, and delivery excellence.
Team Leadership & Business Development
Mentor and develop project controls professionals, schedulers, cost engineers, and analysts.
Support recruitment, workforce planning, and professional development initiatives.
Contribute to proposal development, interviews, and strategic pursuits within the aviation market.
Collaborate with aviation and infrastructure leaders to expand STV's project controls services and client relationships.
Support implementation of digital project delivery tools and advanced reporting platforms.
 
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Project Management, Architecture, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field.
15+ years of progressive project controls experience supporting large capital programs.
8+ years of experience managing project controls teams on aviation, transportation, or major infrastructure projects.
Demonstrated experience supporting complex aviation projects including:
Airport terminal expansions
Airfield and runway improvement programs
Baggage handling systems
Landside transportation facilities
Airline support facilities
Airport modernization programs
Extensive knowledge of:
Cost Engineering
CPM Scheduling
Risk Management
Change Management
Forecasting
Earned Value Management (EVM)
Program Controls Governance
Performance Reporting
Advanced proficiency with Primavera P6 and Microsoft Office Suite.
Strong leadership, communication, presentation, and client-facing skills.
Proven ability to manage multiple concurrent projects and priorities.
 
Preferred Qualifications
Experience supporting aviation capital programs exceeding $500M.
Experience working directly with major airport authorities, airlines, and aviation stakeholders.
Professional certifications such as:
Project Management Professional (PMP)
Certified Cost Professional (CCP)
Planning & Scheduling Professional (PSP)
Certified Construction Manager (CCM)
PMI-RMP
Experience with Primavera Risk Analysis, Acumen Fuse, Unifier, e-Builder, Kahua, Procore, Power BI, or similar project management platforms.
Master's degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Business Administration, or related discipline.
