The ideal candidate combines strong technical project controls expertise with exceptional leadership, client relationship management, and business development capabilities.
 
Responsibilities
Strategic Project Controls Leadership
Lead project controls functions across large-scale aviation programs from planning and design through construction, commissioning, and closeout.
Establish and implement project controls governance frameworks, procedures, standards, and best practices.

Develop integrated project controls strategies encompassing cost, schedule, risk, forecasting, and performance management.
Identify and proactively mitigate project risks, opportunities, and performance challenges.
Cost Management & Financial Controls
Direct the development and management of project budgets, forecasts, cash flow analyses, and cost reports.
Perform cost trending, earned value analysis, variance analysis, and estimate-at-completion forecasting.
Review contractor payment applications, change orders, estimates, and cost proposals.

Evaluate project performance and recommend corrective actions when necessary.
Scheduling & Performance Management
Oversee development, maintenance, and analysis of complex CPM schedules utilizing Primavera P6 and related tools.
Review contractor schedules and monitor compliance with project requirements.

Lead project risk identification, assessment, mitigation planning, and monitoring activities.

Project Overview:
 
The selected candidate will initially be placed on one of our four Liquefied Natural Gas Plant Projects in the US Gulf Coast Region for our Energy Global Business Unit, but we may also require the selected candidate to have future mobility to one of our other Global Business Units in a different location. The ideal candidate will have market sector/ sub sector construction industry experience in 
energy
 (liquefied natural gas), 
manufacturing and technology
 (semiconductor, chemical, pharmaceutical, data centers, fire power generation),
 infrastructure
 (aviation, rail, roads/bridges),  
mining and minerals
 (water treatment plant, mineral extraction, metal refining), & 
nuclear, security, and environmental
 (nuclear power epc, power distribution, combined cycle, defense and space, environmental cleanup). As needs arise in our growing business, there will be expectation for the candidate to be fully mobile.
Job Summary:
 
In this role, you will provide automation support to project teams, including setup, training, application use in work-process, software quality assurance and control, reporting, database administration, and close-out of all construction automation software and applications. Your technical knowledge will help ensure applications and software meet user requirements and are compliant with work processes.
 #LI-BH1
Major Responsibilities:
 
The Construction Automation Engineer is responsible for establishing and administering the suite of Construction Automation applications. This includes, but is not limited to, the following applications: Unifier, PowerApps, AI – enabled solutions, TEAMWorks, SetRoute, WITS (Weld and Welder tracking system), Smart Completions, SSRS, Bechtel Productivity Services (BPS) (Xfighters), AWP Tools and DCS/ MAP.
Maintain existing and create new Unifier and Power Apps Workflows.
Work with the Project Team to establish the requirements for Construction Automation Systems to support construction work processes.
Coordinate with design engineering, supply chain, project controls, and other departments to establish automated data transfer between applications.
Configure BSAPs and other applications to meet project requirements.
Understand reporting requirements for each application and configure reports accordingly. Ensure reports are accurate and functioning as intended.
Review/trouble-shoot data for accuracy and completeness. Identify and address anomalies.
Provide ongoing administration to each BSAP.
Provide training and technical support to end users, including field engineering, supervision, administration, project controls, and other site personnel.
Interface with corporate BSAP administrators to change functionality or configuration of applications to meet project specific requirements.
Education and Experience Requirements:
 
Requires a University Hire with 1-2 years of experience or 5-6 years of relevant work experience
Required Knowledge and Skills:
 
Knowledge of engineering and construction methods and processes customarily acquired over time through specialized instruction and practical experience is required.
Extensive knowledge of Unifier and linking Unifier to Bechtel BSAPs and other applications is required.
Extensive knowledge of Power Apps and linking Power Apps to Bechtel BSAPs and other applications is required.
Extensive knowledge of TEAMWorks and associated applications used for data integrity and reporting is required.
Experience with other Bechtel Standard applications, including but not limited to SETROUTE and DSCS/EBS required.
A good understanding of Bechtel standard construction work processes and procedures required.
Advanced level capability of databases is required.
Bechtel Direct Hire Construction experience is preferred.
Excellent communication and problem-solving ability.
Additional Information:
Work requires the physical ability to conduct field inspections including but not limited to: extensive walking in and around a construction site often in high heat and high humidity conditions, climbing ladders, climbing scaffolding, working on elevated platforms, working on uneven surfaces, and working in small or confined spaces. Some lifting may be required. Must have the ability to walk into and out of the project (enter/egress). Must be able to use appropriate standard issued Personal Protection Equipment (PPE) required for each assigned task (i.e. harness, life vest, lift buckets, etc.).

Project Overview:
 
Bechtel is partnering with NextDecade to support their vision to provide the world access to lower carbon intensive energy with their Rio Grande LNG (RGLNG) project in Brownsville, Texas. RGLNG is a natural gas liquefaction and export terminal situated on a 984-acre site on the banks of the Brownsville ship channel. The first phase of the RGLNG project consists of three liquefaction trains, two storage tanks and one marine berth. At full capacity, the five-train facility will have a production capacity of 27 million tonnes per annum (MTPA). Brownsville, Texas is a city known for its diverse history, tradition, and rich culture. Located in the southernmost region in the beautiful state of Texas, lays Brownsville a rich, tropical oasis bordering the Rio Grande River and near the shores of the Gulf of Mexico. Brownsville embraces innovation, looks forward to the future and beyond! 
Job Summary:
 
As part of the System Turnover team, members interface with other teams across the project, to drive System completion per the established schedule. Analyzing System readiness, tracking restraints and open items and identifying potential roadblocks or pitfalls. Proactively considers continuous learning, developing firm understanding of system and area scoping and drawings while embracing zero accident and zero rework philosophies. The team provides a pivotal interface between other team members and requires excellent interpersonal and organizational skills.
 #LI-BH1

Track pending issues and actions impacting system turnover.
Coordinate system walkdowns.
Impress upon Construction, Field Engineering and Pre-Commissioning the sense of urgency for meeting commitments.

Utilize multiple databases and BSAPs for reviewing and checking dossiers including Teamworks, Setroute and Aconex.
Maintain and administrate Completions tracking databases.
Prepare and complete quality documents and data audits.
Support the implementation of the records retention and turnover plans.
Manage installation work packages and test packages.
Update Teamworks database.
Perform / assist with other general administrative or clerical duties as assigned.
Coordinate and track open punchlist items.
Proactively consider continuous learning or show interest in pursuing learning activities.
Develops firm understanding of work packaging, test packaging, and system and area scoping and drawings required for package development.
Support development and provide operational training to other team members as required.

Requires bachelor's degree (or international equivalent) and 5-8 years of relevant experience or 9-12 years of relevant work experience
Required Knowledge and Skills:
 
Experience on an LNG construction site especially along the U.S. Gulf Coast preferred.
Good communication skills, both verbal and written.
Computer literate in word processing, spreadsheets, and database applications.
Some understanding of and experience with Smart Completions and Unifier is preferred.

Digital Commercial SME
Houston, Texas, US · Posted: 2026-10-09T23:26:50.791Z
Comp: Not listed
Job description
Turner & Townsend is a global professional services company with over 22,000 people in more than 60 countries.
Working with our clients across real estate, infrastructure, energy and natural resources, we transform together delivering outcomes that improve people’s lives. Working in partnership makes it possible to deliver the world’s most impactful projects and programmes as we turn challenge into opportunity and complexity into success.

Our capabilities include programme, project, cost, asset and commercial management, controls and performance, procurement and supply chain, net zero and digital solutions.
We are majority-owned by CBRE Group, Inc., the world’s largest commercial real estate services and investment firm, with our partners holding a significant minority interest. Turner & Townsend and CBRE work together to provide clients with the premier programme, project and cost management offering in markets around the world.
 

We are seeking a strong 
Senior Digital Consultant
 with a strong focus on systems implementation, data, analytics, and information management to support major capital programs and portfolios across all sectors.
This role bridges project controls systems, information management, data analytics, and digital strategy, helping clients unlock value from data, improve delivery performance, and align ways of working with modern digital tools. You will lead a PMIS implementation and data strategy from requirements through configuration, implementation, adoption, and continuous improvement.
The role is client-facing, consultative, and delivery-oriented, with opportunities to shape strategy, lead technical delivery, support business development, and champion leading digital practices.
 
Key Responsibilities
Lead the development, validation, and translation of business and system requirements into practical digital solutions
Lead the configuration, implementation, and optimization of a PMIS systems for a large PMO focusing on cost, risk, schedule, and portfolio tools
Develop system configuration approaches, technical documentation, and implementation plans aligned to program objectives
Influence client ways of working to align operational processes with system capabilities and data models
Champion leading practice in digital systems configuration and integration across major capital programs
Capture and analyses client requirements to design digital strategies, data frameworks, and analytics approaches aligned to business outcomes
Support integration of project, cost, schedule, and asset data across the PMO into a series of reports
Design and implement dashboarding and reporting solutions (e.g. Power BI, Tableau) to enable insight-led decision-making
Provide technical training, coaching, and user adoption support to client teams
Contribute to high-quality documentation, presentations, and stakeholder communications
Provide technical input to business development, bid responses, and winning work
Support the continuous improvement of digital, data, and analytics capability across the business
Act as an ambassador for digital services, championing value-led digitization and innovation
Actively engage with emerging industry trends and technologies and embed learning into delivery
Technical Knowledge
Data and Information Management standards
Understanding of PMIS  Environments (e.g. Procore, Kahua, Unifier etc)
Dashboarding and analytics tools (e.g. Power BI, Tableau)
Understanding of PMIS systems, cost, schedule, and portfolio management tools
Experience setting up and managing SharePoint, PowerApps, Power Automate and Power Query along with other collaborative digital workspaces

Skills & Experience
Strong understanding of digital systems and data-driven delivery within capital projects and asset management
Proven experience delivering client-facing digital or data-enabled change, from engagement start-up through implementation
Ability to clearly link digital solutions to client value, including cost, efficiency, assurance, and performance outcomes
Strong understanding of PMO / PMIS tools, methodologies, and governance
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, able to explain complex technical concepts clearly
High emotional intelligence with the confidence to challenge constructively and implement change
Qualifications
Degree or Masters in a STEM discipline (or equivalent)
Chartered or equivalent professional qualification with a professional institution or recognized body

The salary range for this full-time role is 
$130K-$180K
 per year. Ranges are determined by role and level and represent a good faith effort to provide a fair and equitable salary. This range is a reflection of base salary only, not of a total compensation package.  Please note Turner & Townsend reserves the right to pay more or less than the posted range, depending on candidate’s experience and qualifications. *On-site presence and requirements may change depending on our client's needs*

About Us:
At Broadpin, we specialize in transforming businesses by putting our clients at the center of everything we do. With deep expertise in Oracle ERP, Oracle Cloud, and industry-specific solutions, we deliver customer-focused consulting, strategic implementation, and exceptional service.
Our tailored Oracle solutions are designed to not only meet but exceed the unique needs of each client. We empower organizations to confidently navigate digital transformation, optimize operations, and achieve sustainable growth. Our commitment to excellence, innovation, and long-term partnerships ensures that our clients are equipped for success in today’s fast-paced digital landscape.
At Broadpin, we don’t just implement technology — we enable transformation.
Job Summary:
Project Partners (now Broadpin) is seeking an experienced Oracle Primavera Unifier Consultant for a remote position. The ideal candidate will have 10+ years of experience in project-centric industries such as Engineering, Construction, Manufacturing, or Infrastructure. This role is responsible for designing, implementing, configuring, and optimizing Oracle Primavera Unifier solutions, ensuring seamless integration with client project management and business processes.

Interface Manager
San Francisco, California, United States · Posted: 2026-09-17T21:59:28-04:00
Comp: Salary: $190k-$260k/year ($91-$125/hour)
Job description
About the Position

We’re seeking an experienced 
Interface Manager
 to support a large, complex, heavy-civil rail infrastructure program. This role is responsible for establishing, implementing, and managing a formal Interface Management Plan, including the governance, processes, and tools required to identify, track, and resolve all technical and organizational interfaces across engineering, procurement, and construction activities. This position operates within multi-contract programs involving significant discipline integration and high-risk interface environments (e.g., tunneling, major utility coordination, or systems integration), requiring coordination across contractors, stakeholders, and technical teams to ensure alignment, minimize risk, and support efficient project execution.

This is a long-term, full-time, hybrid position (three days per week in office) position located in the greater San Francisco Bay Area, CA.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Develop, maintain, and implement the project interface management plan, including the interface register, interface control documents, and the process for identifying, assigning, and closing interface points.

Identify technical and organizational interfaces across engineering, procurement, and construction activities, and coordinate resolution across design contracts, construction packages, and disciplines.

Chair interface coordination meetings, track open interface items to closure, and escalate unresolved items with a recommended path forward.

Review design submittals and deliverables for interface conformance, including spatial coordination, structural envelope, equipment clearance, access, and maintainability, and verify that the design supports long-term operations and maintenance rather than the minimum equipment footprint.

Coordinate interfaces between civil and structural work and the systems it houses, including tunnel and station ventilation, mechanical and electrical rooms, traction power, trackwork, fire life safety, and communications.

Evaluate change proposals, design change notices, and requests for information for interface impact, and document the cost, schedule, and scope consequences across affected contracts.

Coordinate with third parties, utility owners, adjacent contracts, and permitting and operating stakeholders on interfaces that cross the contract boundary.

Support the program risk process by translating unresolved interfaces into identified risks with assigned owners, mitigation actions, and closure dates.

Maintain interface traceability from design criteria through construction verification, and confirm that interface requirements are carried into testing, commissioning, and turnover.

Support schedule coordination by identifying interface-driven dependencies between concurrent design and construction contracts and confirming they are reflected in the program schedule.

Prepare interface status reporting and briefings for program leadership, and support decisions with analysis, documentation, and recommendations.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, or systems engineering, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

10+ years' experience with interface management roles in large, complex rail infrastructure programs.

Experience developing and implementing an interface management plan, interface register, or equivalent structured process on a program with concurrent contracts.

Experience performing interdisciplinary design review across civil, structural, mechanical, and electrical scopes, including spatial coordination, clearance, access, and maintainability.

Experience with underground and tunneled construction, including the interfaces between tunnel and station structures and the mechanical, electrical, and ventilation systems they house.

Experience coordinating concurrent design and construction contracts, including interface-driven change, schedule, and risk impacts.

Working knowledge of how civil and structural work interfaces with supporting systems on transit, rail, or other complex infrastructure, including ventilation, power, trackwork, fire life safety, and communications.

Experience with industry standard project / construction management software (e.g., Primavera P6, MS Project, Unifier, Kahua, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in civil engineering, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, or systems engineering.

Professional Engineer (PE) license, Certified Systems Engineering Professional (CSEP) (International Council on Systems Engineering), or Project Management Professional (PMP) certification (Project Management Institute).

Experience carrying interface requirements through testing, commissioning, and turnover to verified closure.

Experience coordinating interfaces with operating agencies, utility owners, and third parties in a dense urban environment.

Experience with interface, requirements, or issue management platforms (e.g., IBM DOORS, Jama Connect, Coordinate, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Compensation Details

Expected Salary: $190k-$260k/year ($91-$125/hour). Job description
About the Positions

We’re seeking 
Project Managers
 of various skill levels to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. We hire project managers who run delivery on programs where a single package can exceed $100M in construction value. You’ll carry scope, budget, schedule, and risk on your assigned projects, hold delivery teams to what they committed to, and provide a clear read on where the work actually stands.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. 
We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Note: We are seeking candidates of various skill levels, and the following responsibilities represent the core of these roles. Scope and complexity increase with experience level.

May lead delivery of assigned projects or task orders, from planning and design through construction and closeout.

Oversee scope, budget, schedule, and risk, and give program leadership an early and honest read when any of the four starts to move.

Oversee designers and contractors against their scope, design criteria, and schedule commitments, and escalate deviations while they are still cheap to fix.

Administer construction contracts, including submittals, requests for information, progress payments, and time extension requests.

Evaluate change proposals and claims for entitlement, cost impact, and schedule impact, and recommend a position to program leadership.

Coordinate with program controls staff to develop and validate cost forecasts, CPM schedule updates, and earned value reporting.

Coordinate across agencies, utility owners, railroads, adjacent contracts, and other third parties so decisions inside the package account for work outside it.

Oversee construction staging and phasing that keeps existing operations running.

Oversee quality and safety compliance, verifying that contractor programs are being followed and that installed work matches approved documents.

Oversee commissioning, operations readiness, and transition to maintenance for completed facilities.

Report project status, risk, and forecast to program leadership so funding and delivery decisions rest on current information.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in construction management, civil engineering, construction engineering, or engineering management, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

10+ years of project management experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Experience managing scope, budget, schedule, and risk on capital projects from design through construction and closeout.

Working knowledge of construction contract administration, including submittals, requests for information, change management, and progress payments.

Experience coordinating designers, contractors, agencies, utility owners, and other third parties across the life of a project.

Experience with industry standard project / construction management software (e.g., Primavera P6, MS Project, Unifier, Kahua, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in construction management, civil engineering, construction engineering, or engineering management.

Active professional certifications and licenses such as PMP (PMI), CCM (CMAA), and/or PE.

Experience serving as the owner’s project manager on a contract package exceeding $100M in construction value.

Experience managing multiple concurrent task orders or contract packages on a program exceeding $1B in construction value.

Experience negotiating change and claim resolution with contractors on the owner’s behalf, including entitlement and impact analysis.

Experience supervising or mentoring project managers, engineers, and controls staff in a program office setting.

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Compensation Details

Expected Salary: $115k-$210k/year ($55-$101/hour). Project Controls Manager
New York, New York, United States · Posted: 2026-10-16T19:11:26-04:00
Comp: Salary: $130k-$205k/year ($63-$99/hour)
Job description
About the Positions

We’re seeking 
Project Controls Managers
 to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. These roles sit where cost, schedule, risk, and change come together, so the baseline, the forecast, and the performance a program reports all tell the same story. We are looking for people who can defend a number in front of a contractor and in front of program leadership on the same day.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. 
We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Oversee the program’s integrated controls system, including the work breakdown and cost breakdown structures, coding standards, and baseline change procedures, so cost and schedule data reconcile to the same source.

Review and validate contractor cost and schedule submittals, including baseline schedules, monthly updates, progress payments, and contingency drawdown requests, against contract requirements and verified field progress.

Analyze earned value, cost and schedule performance indices, and productivity trends, and surface the variances that will move the forecast before they show up in a monthly report.

Evaluate change proposals, delay claims, and time impact analyses for cost and schedule merit, and recommend a position to program leadership.

Oversee the program forecast, cash flow projection, and contingency and reserve position, and test the assumptions behind each of them.

Coordinate the risk register with the cost and schedule baselines so quantified exposure carries into the forecast and into contingency decisions.

May lead the monthly controls cycle, presenting cost and schedule status, trends, and recommended corrective action to program leadership.

Coordinate controls across adjacent contracts and program interfaces so impacts that cross package boundaries are captured before they land in a claim.

Coordinate that work across roadway and structures packages, systems and trackwork contracts, airfield phasing, and water and utility relocation work.

Coordinate across estimating, scheduling, engineering, contracts, document control, and finance so one set of numbers supports program decisions.

Oversee the controls data in the program’s management information systems and verify that cost, schedule, and change records are complete, correctly coded, and traceable for funding agency reporting and external audit.

May lead and mentor controls analysts and specialists, setting expectations for analysis quality, turnaround, and how findings get escalated.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in construction management, engineering, finance, business, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

10+ years of project controls experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Experience integrating cost and schedule data on a common work breakdown and cost breakdown structure, including baseline management and change control.

Experience applying earned value methods and critical path schedule analysis to evaluate program performance and forecast outcomes.

Experience reviewing contractor cost and schedule submittals against contract requirements and verified progress.

Experience leading or directing project controls staff on a capital program.

Proficiency with industry standard scheduling and program cost controls software (e.g., Primavera P6, Microsoft Project, Oracle Unifier, EcoSys, e-Builder, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in construction management, engineering, finance, or business.

Active professional certifications such as CCP, PSP, or EVP (AACE), and/or PMP (PMI).

Experience leading the owner’s project controls function on a highway, bridge, transit and rail, aviation, or water and wastewater capital program exceeding $1B in construction value.

Experience standing up a project controls function on a new program, including procedures, coding structures, reporting cycle, and staffing plan.

Experience integrating a quantitative cost or schedule risk model with the program baselines to set and defend a contingency position.

Experience supporting claims, delay analysis, or dispute resolution with time-phased cost and schedule records on a program exceeding $1B in construction value.

Experience configuring or administering the controls modules of a program management information system rather than only working inside one.

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Compensation Details

Expected Salary: $130k-$205k/year ($63-$99/hour). Change Manager
New York, New York, United States · Posted: 2026-10-16T17:16:48-04:00
Comp: Salary: $125k-$200k/year ($60-$96/hour)
Job description
About the Positions

We’re seeking 
Change Managers
 to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. You’ll support the change control process, develop the independent analysis that tests submitted entitlement, cost, and time, keep the scope, cost, schedule, and technical baselines accurate and traceable, and give program leadership a defensible position before money moves, on assignments ranging from a single contract package to a program-level change function.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. 
We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Note: We are seeking candidates of various skill levels, and the following responsibilities represent the core of these roles. Scope and complexity increase with experience level.

Support the program’s change control process from early identification through entitlement determination, pricing, negotiation, and executed change order.

Track every change notice and open change item in the log to a documented decision within the timeframes the contract allows.

Evaluate change proposals, requests for equitable adjustment, and claims for contractual entitlement, and recommend a position supported by the contract language and the factual record.

Develop and review independent cost estimates and time impact analyses that test contractor-submitted pricing and delay claims rather than accepting the submitted numbers.

Coordinate with the estimators, schedulers, and analysts supporting change evaluation, and apply a consistent approach to how changes are analyzed, priced, and documented.

Prepare change board packages that carry the recommendation, the independent analysis, the funding source, and the consequence of not acting, and present them to program decision-makers.

Support negotiation of change order value and time extensions alongside the contracting officer or contract administrator, and document what was agreed and what was released.

Process approved change orders through the contract, and confirm each one is reflected in the contract value, the baseline schedule, the budget, and the affected drawings and specifications.

Coordinate change evaluation with the program’s engineering, inspection, right of way, and operations groups.

Evaluate impacts to active operations and existing facilities before a change is approved.

Analyze differing site conditions, design changes, and third-party-driven changes on bridges, underground work, and systems, and separate what the contract already covers from what it does not.

Report change trends, open change exposure, and pending time extensions to executive program leadership so cost and schedule risk is visible before it lands.

Maintain configuration control of the change record and the affected technical documentation, including version control, revision history, and audit trails.

Keep entitlement decisions, pricing basis, and correspondence retrievable for internal and external audit, funding review, and dispute resolution.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in construction management, civil engineering, construction engineering, or business administration, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

10+ years of construction change control, change order, or claims experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Experience leading the change control process on a construction contract package, including change identification, entitlement determination, pricing, executed change order, and coordination of the estimators, schedulers, and analysts who support change evaluation.

Experience evaluating change proposals, requests for equitable adjustment, or claims for entitlement, cost, and schedule impact, and recommending a position to the owner.

Experience developing or reviewing independent cost estimates and time impact analyses that test contractor-submitted pricing and delay claims.

Experience preparing change board or governance packages and presenting recommendations to owner decision-makers.

Working knowledge of public works contract provisions governing changes, differing site conditions, delays, and notice and claim requirements.

Experience with industry standard PMIS, document management, and CPM scheduling software (e.g., MS Project, Unifier, Kahua, e-Builder, Primavera P6, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in construction management, civil engineering, construction engineering, or business administration.

Active professional certifications such as CCM (CMAA), PMP (PMI), and/or CCP or CFCC (AACE).

Experience managing a program-level change control function across multiple contract packages, including supervising change analysts and standardizing how packages are evaluated.

Experience negotiating individual change orders exceeding $10M in value.

Experience leading the owner’s position on a claim through a dispute resolution board, mediation, or a formal claims process.

Experience analyzing delay and schedule impact on a CPM schedule, including concurrency and the difference between excusable and compensable delay.

Experience with industry standard estimating, cost analysis, and document markup software (e.g., HCSS HeavyBid, RSMeans, Bluebeam Revu, ProjectWise, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Compensation Details

Expected Salary: $125k-$200k/year ($60-$96/hour). Luster provides the salary range that the company in good faith believes it might offer for this position based on the successful candidate’s level and years of experience, knowledge, skills, abilities, education, certifications, licenses, geographic location, etc. Luster reserves the right to ultimately pay more or less than the posted range depending on circumstances not related to any status protected by local, state, and/or federal law.

Cost Controls Manager
Los Angeles, California, United States · Posted: 2026-10-14T19:44:46-04:00

Job description
About the Positions

We’re seeking 
Cost Controls Managers
 to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. You’ll hold the cost position on an assigned program: what the work was budgeted at, what it is forecast to cost now, and what the gap between those two numbers means for funding and delivery decisions. This bank spans managers running cost control on a single program through leaders running the cost function across a portfolio.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. 
We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Develop and maintain the cost baseline for an assigned program, including budget structure, work breakdown and cost coding, and the change control workflow that keeps the baseline current.

Produce monthly cost forecasts, estimates at completion, and cash flow projections, and explain the variance against the approved budget in terms the program can act on.

Review payment applications, cost reports, and invoices against contract terms, verified progress, and the approved schedule of values, then recommend approval or adjustment.

Evaluate change order and claim pricing for cost reasonableness, and track the cost exposure of pending changes so the program sees the number before it is committed.

Monitor contingency and management reserve, track drawdown against the program’s remaining risk, and recommend when contingency is released, held, or replenished.

Analyze earned value and cost performance data across contracts, and flag adverse trends early enough that corrective action is still available.

May lead monthly cost reviews with program leadership, including cost reports, trend analysis, and scenario models that support funding and delivery decisions.

Coordinate with finance and accounting groups and with the scheduling, estimating, risk, and contract administration teams so budget, commitment, and expenditure data reconcile across systems.

Prepare cost reporting and audit documentation for local, regional, state, and federal funding agencies, and maintain the audit trail behind every reported number.

May lead and develop cost control analysts and specialists, including review of their work products and consistency of method from one contract to the next.

Coordinate with construction management and discipline leads on the cost drivers behind each contract’s forecast.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in construction management, civil engineering, accounting, or finance, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

10+ years of cost control experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Experience developing and maintaining program budgets, cost baselines, work breakdown structures, and cost coding on active construction programs.

Experience producing cost forecasts, estimates at completion, cash flow projections, and earned value and variance analysis.

Experience reviewing contractor payment applications, cost reports, and change order pricing against contract terms and verified progress.

Experience leading, supervising, or coordinating cost control staff, including review of their work products and consistency of method between them.

Experience with industry standard program cost management and cost modeling software (e.g., Oracle Unifier, e-Builder, Kahua, Microsoft Excel, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in construction management, civil engineering, accounting, or finance.

Active professional certifications such as CCP or EVP (AACE), CCM (CMAA), and/or PMP (PMI).

Experience leading the owner’s cost control function on a program exceeding $1B in construction value.

Experience supporting owner’s representative, program management, or construction management assignments on transportation, transit, aviation, or water and wastewater programs.

Experience setting contingency and management reserve policy on a multi-year capital program, including drawdown tracking and replenishment decisions.

Experience defending program cost reporting in grant, funding agency, or oversight reviews, including reconciliation against the owner’s enterprise financial systems.

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Fresno, California, United States; Los Angeles, California, United States; Sacramento, California, United States; San Francisco, California, United States · Posted: 2026-10-16T17:14:53-04:00
Comp: Salary: $125k-$200k/year ($60-$96/hour)
Job description
About the Positions

We’re seeking 
Change Managers
 to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. You’ll support the change control process, develop the independent analysis that tests submitted entitlement, cost, and time, keep the scope, cost, schedule, and technical baselines accurate and traceable, and give program leadership a defensible position before money moves, on assignments ranging from a single contract package to a program-level change function.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. 
We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Note: We are seeking candidates of various skill levels, and the following responsibilities represent the core of these roles. Scope and complexity increase with experience level.

Support the program’s change control process from early identification through entitlement determination, pricing, negotiation, and executed change order.

Track every change notice and open change item in the log to a documented decision within the timeframes the contract allows.

Evaluate change proposals, requests for equitable adjustment, and claims for contractual entitlement, and recommend a position supported by the contract language and the factual record.

Develop and review independent cost estimates and time impact analyses that test contractor-submitted pricing and delay claims rather than accepting the submitted numbers.

Coordinate with the estimators, schedulers, and analysts supporting change evaluation, and apply a consistent approach to how changes are analyzed, priced, and documented.

Prepare change board packages that carry the recommendation, the independent analysis, the funding source, and the consequence of not acting, and present them to program decision-makers.

Support negotiation of change order value and time extensions alongside the contracting officer or contract administrator, and document what was agreed and what was released.

Process approved change orders through the contract, and confirm each one is reflected in the contract value, the baseline schedule, the budget, and the affected drawings and specifications.

Coordinate change evaluation with the program’s engineering, inspection, right of way, and operations groups.

Evaluate impacts to active operations and existing facilities before a change is approved.

Analyze differing site conditions, design changes, and third-party-driven changes on bridges, underground work, and systems, and separate what the contract already covers from what it does not.

Report change trends, open change exposure, and pending time extensions to executive program leadership so cost and schedule risk is visible before it lands.

Maintain configuration control of the change record and the affected technical documentation, including version control, revision history, and audit trails.

Keep entitlement decisions, pricing basis, and correspondence retrievable for internal and external audit, funding review, and dispute resolution.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in construction management, civil engineering, construction engineering, or business administration, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

10+ years of construction change control, change order, or claims experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Experience leading the change control process on a construction contract package, including change identification, entitlement determination, pricing, executed change order, and coordination of the estimators, schedulers, and analysts who support change evaluation.

Experience evaluating change proposals, requests for equitable adjustment, or claims for entitlement, cost, and schedule impact, and recommending a position to the owner.

Experience developing or reviewing independent cost estimates and time impact analyses that test contractor-submitted pricing and delay claims.

Experience preparing change board or governance packages and presenting recommendations to owner decision-makers.

Working knowledge of public works contract provisions governing changes, differing site conditions, delays, and notice and claim requirements.

Experience with industry standard PMIS, document management, and CPM scheduling software (e.g., MS Project, Unifier, Kahua, e-Builder, Primavera P6, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in construction management, civil engineering, construction engineering, or business administration.

Active professional certifications such as CCM (CMAA), PMP (PMI), and/or CCP or CFCC (AACE).

Experience managing a program-level change control function across multiple contract packages, including supervising change analysts and standardizing how packages are evaluated.

Experience negotiating individual change orders exceeding $10M in value.

Experience leading the owner’s position on a claim through a dispute resolution board, mediation, or a formal claims process.

Experience analyzing delay and schedule impact on a CPM schedule, including concurrency and the difference between excusable and compensable delay.

Experience with industry standard estimating, cost analysis, and document markup software (e.g., HCSS HeavyBid, RSMeans, Bluebeam Revu, ProjectWise, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Job description
About the Positions

We’re seeking 
Contract Administrators
 to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. These roles carry contracts and task orders through the full life cycle, from solicitation and proposal through award, administration, modification, and closeout, on transit and transportation capital programs. We are looking for people who know how to build a clean solicitation, who can work across a range of contract and agreement types, and who keep contract files defensible from the first draft to final payment.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Support each assigned contract and task order through its full life cycle, from solicitation and proposal through award, administration, modification, and closeout, on transit and transportation capital programs.

Develop and review solicitation packages, including requests for proposals, invitations for bid, requests for quotes, scopes of work, specifications, and evaluation criteria, for completeness and conformance with program and agency procurement requirements.

Coordinate pre-proposal and pre-bid meetings, respond to bidder and proposer questions, and prepare addenda and amendments before proposals are due.

Support proposal and bid evaluation, including coordinating selection committees, documenting evaluation results, and preparing award recommendations and approval packages for executive concurrence.

Coordinate collection and verification of bonds, insurance certificates, and other documents needed to execute contracts and task orders and issue notice to proceed.

Administer assigned contracts and task orders after award, including tracking deliverables, funding, periods of performance, option exercises, and compliance with contract terms.

Evaluate change proposals, requests for equitable adjustment, and claims for merit, coordinate independent cost estimates and schedule analysis, and support negotiation and preparation of contract modification packages.

Verify solicitations and contract actions against federal and agency procurement requirements, including FTA procurement rules, Buy America provisions, and DBE participation goals.

Maintain contract files, correspondence, logs, and records in the program’s contract management system so every action is documented and audit-ready.

Coordinate with project managers, legal, finance, risk, and compliance staff to resolve contract issues and keep procurement schedules on track.

Support contract and task order closeout, including final acceptance, release of claims, final payment, and records retention.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Sound judgment and discretion when handling confidential procurement and negotiation information.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in business administration, engineering, construction management, or public administration, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

5+ years of transit and transportation contract administration or procurement experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Experience developing and administering requests for proposals, invitations for bid, requests for quotes, scopes of work, and specifications.

Working knowledge of a range of contract and agreement types (e.g., firm fixed price, cost reimbursable, time and materials, indefinite delivery/indefinite quantity, task order, and intergovernmental agreements) and the solicitation methods used to award them.

Experience administering task orders from proposal through closeout on multiple task order contracts.

Experience with industry standard contract management, procurement, or ERP systems (e.g., Unifier, PeopleSoft, SAP Ariba, e-Builder, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in business administration, engineering, construction management, or public administration.

Certified Professional Contract Manager (CPCM) or Certified Federal Contract Manager (CFCM) certification (National Contract Management Association), or Certified Public Procurement Officer (CPPO) certification (Universal Public Procurement Certification Council).

Experience administering construction, professional services, and task order contracts on a transit or transportation capital program exceeding $1B in total value.

Experience evaluating and negotiating change orders, requests for equitable adjustment, and claims on construction contracts exceeding $100M in value.

Working knowledge of the federal procurement requirements that apply to federally funded transit and transportation programs, including FTA Circular 4220.1F, Buy America, Brooks Act qualifications-based selection, and DBE program requirements.

Experience working in a public agency procurement environment, including agency procurement manuals, board approval thresholds, protest procedures, and public records requirements.

Experience supporting an owner’s representative, program management, or construction management team on a public infrastructure program.

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Document Control Manager
Baltimore, Maryland, United States; New York, New York, United States · Posted: 2026-10-16T17:43:57-04:00
Comp: Salary: $110k-$175k/year ($53-$84/hour)
Job description
About the Positions

We’re seeking 
Document Control Managers
 to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. These positions own the program record: the systems, procedures, and controls that keep every drawing, submittal, RFI, and piece of correspondence current, traceable, and defensible. When an audit, a claim, or a funding review lands two years after the fact, what you built is what the program stands on.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. 
We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Note: We are seeking candidates of various skill levels, and the following responsibilities represent the core of these roles. Scope and complexity increase with experience level.

May lead the document control function across the program, including direction of assigned document control staff and allocation of that workload across contracts, phases, and field offices.

Develop and maintain the program’s document control procedures, numbering and naming conventions, revision control, and retention schedules, and hold contractors, designers, and internal teams to them.

Administer the enterprise document management system, including permissions, workflow configuration, metadata structure, and issue resolution, so the system stays the single authoritative record.

Oversee the intake, logging, distribution, and closeout of submittals, RFIs, correspondence, and design deliverables in the system of record.

Keep the register accurate enough that turnaround can be measured and defended.

Verify that the current approved revision of drawings, specifications, and other controlled documents is the version in use across the program team, the field offices, and any shared platform.

Coordinate document flow across active work areas and the contract packages they support.

Monitor and report document control metrics, including submittal turnaround, RFI aging, overdue reviews, and open action items, and escalate what is at risk before it affects schedule or payment.

About the Positions

Assistant Project Managers
 to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. If you have run a scope component end to end on a transit or transportation program and can defend a position on a change or a delay with the record behind it, this is the seat.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. may include, but are not limited to, the following:

May lead assigned task orders on behalf of the owner through all phases of the project, from task order scoping and budgeting through design, construction, and closeout, coordinating the contractors and design consultants performing the work.

Track cost performance against the approved budget, review contractor and consultant invoices and payment applications, and develop forecasts the program can act on.

Monitor schedule updates against milestone and contract commitments, analyze critical path movement, and press for recovery where the assigned scope is slipping.

Evaluate change requests, requests for information, and submittals for technical merit, cost impact, and schedule impact, and recommend a position to program leadership.

Monitor contractor and consultant performance against quality, safety, and contract requirements, and document nonconformance so it gets corrected.

Maintain the risk register for the assigned scope, evaluate mitigation options, and escalate program-level risks to the Project Manager while there is still time to act.

Coordinate design and construction submittal reviews across disciplines, including roadway, structures, and water and wastewater elements, and track comments through to documented closure.

Coordinate construction phasing and access on active facilities, including traffic staging, service windows, and operational constraints.

Coordinate interfaces with adjacent contracts, utility owners, railroads, and other third parties so the assigned scope stays aligned with the rest of the program.

May lead client and stakeholder meetings and deliver progress reporting on scope, cost, schedule, and risk, with the supporting documentation behind every number.

Administer contract documents and program controls procedures, and maintain the correspondence, decision, and action item record so program positions hold up under audit and claim review.

Project controls experience on a capital program, including cost and schedule performance tracking, budget forecasting, and review of contractor or consultant invoices.

Working knowledge of construction contract documents and of the submittal, request for information, and change order processes.

Experience coordinating project meetings and maintaining action item, decision, and correspondence records on a public agency capital program.

Experience with industry standard project / construction management software (e.g., Primavera P6, MS Project, Unifier, Kahua, etc.).

PMIS Configuration Consultant
Fresno, California, United States; Los Angeles, California, United States; Phoenix, Arizona, United States; Sacramento, California, United States; San Francisco, California, United States · Posted: 2026-09-22T15:32:59-04:00
Comp: Salary: $130k-$160k/year ($63-$77/hour)
Job description
About the Positions

We’re seeking 
PMIS Configuration Consultants
 to configure, implement, and support project management information systems on large-scale, heavy-civil infrastructure programs across highways, roads and bridges, transit (rail and bus), aviation, and water sectors. You’ll build out PMIS modules for budget, cost, schedule, risk, and reporting, and partner with project controls teams to keep program data structured, accurate, and audit ready.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. 
We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.
 While we are currently targeting the greater San Francisco Bay area, we welcome and will consider qualified candidates from anywhere in the continental United States. These positions require up to 50% travel.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Note: We are seeking candidates of various skill levels, and the following responsibilities represent the core of these roles. Scope and complexity increase with experience level.

Configure PMIS processes for budget, cost, change orders, payments, risk, issues, cash flow, and earned value to support project controls, project management, and program management functions.

Configure security roles, user access, and integrations between PMIS platforms, scheduling systems, document management systems, and ERP systems.

Configure cash flow, earned value, and other modules within the PMIS solution.

Identify and correct inconsistencies in data structures, coding, and hierarchy across project controls systems.

Develop and maintain data models that support integrated reporting across cost, schedule, and performance metrics, and drive continuous improvement of data structures, reporting processes, and data quality across the program.

Develop project reports and dashboards aligned with client and program reporting requirements.

Automate data extraction, transformation, and reconciliation across PMIS and integrated systems using SQL and/or Python.

Reconcile and validate data across multiple reporting systems to maintain accuracy and consistency.

Collaborate with project controls managers, cost engineers, and schedulers to ensure data structures support program controls requirements.

Support end-user training and knowledge transfer on deployed PMIS configurations, workflows, and reporting tools.

Attributes

Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical project data into clear reporting for program leadership and stakeholders.

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret complex datasets and identify meaningful insights.

High attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy.

Ability to manage multiple data sources and competing reporting deadlines across large, complex programs.

Collaborative mindset that supports project controls managers, cost engineers, and schedulers in achieving shared reporting goals.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, computer science, construction management, business administration (management information systems), data analytics, statistics, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

3+ years’ experience implementing, integrating, and configuring software systems, preferably Unifier, P6, Kahua, or Procore.

Experience configuring business processes, workflows, security roles, and user access within an enterprise software platform.

Experience building and maintaining integrations between enterprise systems, including work with APIs, authentication, and structured data formats such as JSON, XML, and CSV.

Proficiency with SQL and Python, including the use of Python to automate data extraction, transformation, reconciliation, and system-to-system integration.

Experience performing advanced data manipulation, transformation, and structuring of large datasets, beyond basic reporting or dashboarding.

Experience working with hierarchical data structures such as work breakdown structures (WBS), cost breakdown structures (CBS), chart of accounts, or similar multi-level coding frameworks.

Experience integrating, reconciling, and normalizing data across multiple systems, such as scheduling, cost, and financial systems.

Experience improving data quality, hierarchy, and alignment across systems when working with incomplete, inconsistent, or poorly structured datasets.

Experience developing reports and dashboards aligned with stakeholder and organizational reporting requirements.

Proficiency with Microsoft Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in engineering, computer science, construction management, business administration (management information systems), data analytics, or statistics.

PMP (PMI), CCM (CMAA), MRICS/FRICS (RICS), or CCA (AACE).

Experience supporting project controls, data, or reporting functions on large, complex infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (rail or bus), aviation, or water/wastewater projects, typically involving multi-contract delivery and integrated reporting requirements.

Understanding of project controls processes and their relationships to budget, schedule, risk, and governance on large capital programs.

Experience integrating PMIS or enterprise platforms via API with analytics platforms or AI-assisted reporting tools, including familiarity with applicable cybersecurity governance requirements.

Experience developing Python-based integrations in a production environment, including scheduled execution, error handling, logging, and documentation.

Experience operating within a Center of Excellence model, including development of templates, processes, and governance that support efficient configuration and delivery.

Experience supporting integrated cost and schedule reporting, including earned value or similar performance frameworks.

Experience supporting project controls or program management on infrastructure programs exceeding $500M in value.

Familiarity or proficiency with Microsoft Power BI.

Compensation Details

Expected Salary: $130k-$160k/year ($63-$77/hour). Contracts and Claims Specialist
New York, New York, United States · Posted: 2026-10-16T17:36:58-04:00
Comp: Salary: $90k-$155k/year ($43-$75/hour)
Job description
About the Positions

We’re seeking 
Contracts and Claims Specialists
 of various skill levels to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. These are construction claims and disputes roles, meaning contract claims rather than insurance adjusting. You’ll evaluate claims and requests for equitable adjustment for entitlement and quantum, test claimed cost and time against the contract and the contemporaneous record, and develop a position that holds up in negotiation, in front of a dispute review board, and in whatever comes after that. Contract administration is part of the job, but the center of it is what happens when the parties stop agreeing.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. 
We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Note: We are seeking candidates of various skill levels, and the following responsibilities represent the core of these roles. Scope and complexity increase with experience level.

Analyze claims and notices of potential claim and lost productivity, and evaluate entitlement against the contract provisions that govern each one.

Evaluate requests for equitable adjustment and disputed change proposals for entitlement, merit, and cost reasonableness, and recommend a position supported by the record.

Review claimed costs, including labor, equipment, materials, extended field and home office overhead, and markup, against contract provisions, force account records, and submitted cost backup.

Identify unsupported, duplicated, or misclassified amounts.

Coordinate with scheduling staff to evaluate time impact analyses and time extension requests against the accepted baseline and the contemporaneous progress schedules.

Assemble the contemporaneous record behind each claim, pulling daily reports, correspondence, requests for information, submittals, inspection records, and meeting minutes into a package that supports the program’s position.

Verify that notices meet the timing and content requirements of the contract, and track responses so contractual response periods are met and the program’s defenses stay intact.

Develop independent cost estimates and quantity checks on roadway, structures, and utility work to test contractor pricing on disputed changes and claims.

Prepare claim position papers, findings of fact, and recommendations for program decision-makers, dispute review boards, and mediation or arbitration panels.

Support negotiation and settlement of disputed changes and claims by developing entitlement and quantum summaries, cost comparisons, and a documented basis of settlement.

Evaluate claims arising in active operating environments, including restricted service windows, access limits, and facility shutdowns.

Coordinate with counsel, claims consultants, project controls, and finance staff on claim strategy, document production, and responses to formal demands.

Track open claims and disputed exposure by contract for program leadership.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in construction management, civil engineering, quantity surveying, or finance, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

5+ years of contract administration and construction claims experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Experience analyzing or supporting claims, requests for equitable adjustment, or disputed change proposals for entitlement, cost, and schedule impact.

Working knowledge of standard construction contract terms and public agency contracting requirements, including notice, changes, differing site conditions, delay, and disputes provisions.

Ability to interpret construction contract documents, plans, specifications, and cost and schedule records, and to build an entitlement narrative from the contemporaneous record.

Experience with industry standard contract administration, document management, and CPM scheduling software (e.g., Unifier, Aconex, e-Builder, Primavera P6, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in construction management, civil engineering, quantity surveying, or finance.

Active professional certifications such as CPCM (NCMA), CCM (CMAA), and/or CCP or CFCC (AACE).

Experience serving as the owner’s lead analyst on a claim exceeding $10M in disputed value.

Experience supporting contract administration and claims on a package exceeding $100M in construction value.

Experience carrying a claim beyond the project level through a dispute review board, mediation, arbitration, or litigation, including document production and support to counsel.

Experience preparing or reviewing time impact analyses, as-planned versus as-built comparisons, or windows analyses supporting delay claims, including the treatment of concurrent delay.

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Compensation Details

Expected Salary: $90k-$155k/year ($43-$75/hour). Luster provides the salary range that the company in good faith believes it might offer for this position based on the successful candidate’s level and years of experience, knowledge, skills, abilities, education, certifications, licenses, geographic location, etc. Luster reserves the right to ultimately pay more or less than the posted range depending on circumstances not related to any status protected by local, state, and/or federal law.
