Job description
About the Position

We’re seeking a 
Claims and Change Specialist
 to support large, heavy-civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (both rail and bus), international airports, and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative methods. Your primary focus will be supporting claims analysis, contract administration, and change management activities associated with complex infrastructure construction projects, including contract research, change control, commercial management support, and coordination with project controls and construction management teams.

This is a long-term, full-time, on-site position located in New York, NY.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Support the review of contractor notices, change requests, contract modifications, and related documentation through contract research and claims analysis.

Assist in evaluating entitlement considerations by reviewing contract requirements, technical documentation, project records, and applicable procedures.

Draft correspondence related to contract changes, requests for clarification, and change management activities for management review.

Prepare written summaries, analyses, and supporting documentation outlining contractual considerations, findings, and key project issues.

Support administration of the change control process in accordance with contract requirements, project procedures, and established change management practices.

Review and track change requests to help ensure compliance with contractual requirements, documentation standards, and established timelines.

Compile, maintain, and organize supporting documentation associated with change requests, including cost, schedule, technical, and project controls information.

Maintain accurate records of change orders, approvals, correspondence, negotiations, and supporting documentation within project tracking systems and change logs.

Coordinate with estimators, schedulers, project controls teams, construction management staff, contractors, and stakeholders to facilitate the collection and organization of information related to proposed changes.

Schedule and coordinate change management meetings, prepare meeting materials, and document action items, decisions, and follow-up activities.

Assist in the preparation and review of change proposal requests and related documentation.

Support change order negotiations by coordinating meetings, preparing materials, documenting discussions, and tracking outcomes.

Assist in ensuring change management activities comply with applicable contract requirements, procurement guidelines, project procedures, and audit requirements.

Organize and maintain project records to support internal and external audits related to contract compliance and change management activities.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent organizational and analytical skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a passion for continuous improvement.

Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced project environment.

Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality, accountability, and professionalism.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, construction management, business, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

2-5 years of experience supporting claims analysis, contract administration, change management, project controls, commercial management, or construction management activities on large infrastructure, transportation, transit, rail, aviation, or heavy civil construction projects.

Experience reviewing and interpreting construction contracts, specifications, change orders, contract modifications, notices, and other project documentation.

Experience supporting change management, contract administration, project controls, commercial management, or claims-related activities on design-build and/or alternative delivery projects.

Experience coordinating with estimators, schedulers, project controls teams, construction management teams, contractors, and project stakeholders.

Demonstrated experience in technical writing and project documentation.

Experience maintaining detailed project records, logs, correspondence, and supporting documentation.

Experience using Oracle Primavera Unifier or similar project controls, contract management, or change management software (Unifier preferred).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in construction management, engineering, or business.

Experience supporting claims analysis, contract administration, change management, or commercial management on major transit, rail, tunnel, underground, or heavy civil infrastructure programs.

Experience supporting owner's representative, PMCM, program management, or construction management assignments.

Experience supporting design-build contracts exceeding $100M in construction value.

Experience supporting contract change negotiations and commercial management activities.

NYC agency, public transportation, or major capital infrastructure program experience.

Reporting Specialist
New York, New York, United States · Posted: 2026-10-16T18:20:18-04:00
Comp: Salary: $80k-$145k/year ($38-$70/hour)
Job description
About the Positions

We’re seeking 
Reporting Specialists
 of various skill levels to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. These roles produce the recurring reporting a program publishes, the monthly, quarterly, and annual packages that reach program leadership, funding agencies, and oversight bodies, along with the input collection, verification, and version control standing behind every figure in them. You’ll run the reporting cycle and get a defensible package out on the date it was promised. If your work is weighted toward building data models, queries, and dashboards, our data analyst bank is the better fit, and if it is weighted toward authoring plans, procedures, and controlled documents, look at our technical writer bank.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. 
We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Note: We are seeking candidates of various skill levels, and the following responsibilities represent the core of these roles. Scope and complexity increase with experience level.

Prepare the recurring monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting packages the program publishes, assembling progress, cost, schedule, change, and milestone content into the program’s approved format.

May lead the reporting cycle from data cutoff through review and distribution, tracking who owes what and chasing late or missing inputs so the publication date holds.

Collect reporting inputs from project teams, consultants, and contractors, and verify each figure and status statement against the source records held in the program’s PMIS, cost, and schedule systems.

Review contractor and consultant reporting submissions for completeness and conformance with the reporting requirements in their contracts, and return submissions that do not meet the standard.

Reconcile differences between what a contractor reports, what the PMIS holds, and what program records show, and escalate what cannot be settled before publication.

Develop the exhibits behind the reporting, including milestone and progress charts, dashboard extracts, maps, and photo logs, and confirm each one matches the data it was drawn from.

Apply the program’s reporting templates, data definitions, and format standards across projects and contracts so figures carry the same meaning at the program level.

Maintain reporting trackers, logs, distribution lists, and the repositories where published reporting and its backup live, under version control, so any published figure can be traced back to its source.

Coordinate with cost, schedule, change management, risk, quality, and document control teams to settle conflicting figures before they reach leadership.

Assemble the documentation supporting funding, grant, and oversight agency reporting, researching project records, correspondence, and submittal and change logs to close the gaps.

Prepare ad hoc status summaries and briefing materials for program leadership and project staff across all contract packages.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in construction management, engineering, business administration, or public administration, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

5+ years of program or project reporting experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Experience producing recurring reporting deliverables on a fixed cycle, including assembling content from multiple contributors and meeting a published distribution date.

Experience verifying reported figures and status against source records, and resolving discrepancies with the team or organization that submitted them.

Working knowledge of program controls and construction management reporting content, including progress, cost, schedule, and change status, and where each of those figures originates.

Experience with industry standard program reporting and document management software (e.g., Kahua, Unifier, e-Builder, SharePoint, ProjectWise, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in construction management, engineering, business administration, or public administration.

Active professional certifications such as CCM (CMAA), and/or PMP or CAPM (PMI).

Experience serving as the lead producer of a program’s recurring reporting package on a program exceeding $1B in construction value.

Experience producing board, committee, or oversight body reporting deliverables on a publicly funded capital program.

Experience assembling federal or state grant reporting, funding drawdown packages, or external audit responses, including the documentation trail behind them.

Experience consolidating reporting across a portfolio of concurrent projects and contracts into a single program-level package.

Experience developing reporting templates, data definitions, or format standards that other teams then produced reporting to.

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Compensation Details

Expected Salary: $80k-$145k/year ($38-$70/hour). We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Note: We are seeking candidates of various skill levels, and the following responsibilities represent the core of these roles. Scope and complexity increase with experience level.

Prepare the recurring monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting packages the program publishes, assembling progress, cost, schedule, change, and milestone content into the program’s approved format.

May lead the reporting cycle from data cutoff through review and distribution, tracking who owes what and chasing late or missing inputs so the publication date holds.

Collect reporting inputs from project teams, consultants, and contractors, and verify each figure and status statement against the source records held in the program’s PMIS, cost, and schedule systems.

Review contractor and consultant reporting submissions for completeness and conformance with the reporting requirements in their contracts, and return submissions that do not meet the standard.

Reconcile differences between what a contractor reports, what the PMIS holds, and what program records show, and escalate what cannot be settled before publication.

Develop the exhibits behind the reporting, including milestone and progress charts, dashboard extracts, maps, and photo logs, and confirm each one matches the data it was drawn from.

Apply the program’s reporting templates, data definitions, and format standards across projects and contracts so figures carry the same meaning at the program level.

Maintain reporting trackers, logs, distribution lists, and the repositories where published reporting and its backup live, under version control, so any published figure can be traced back to its source.

Coordinate with cost, schedule, change management, risk, quality, and document control teams to settle conflicting figures before they reach leadership.

Assemble the documentation supporting funding, grant, and oversight agency reporting, researching project records, correspondence, and submittal and change logs to close the gaps.

Prepare ad hoc status summaries and briefing materials for program leadership and project staff across all contract packages.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in construction management, engineering, business administration, or public administration, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

5+ years of program or project reporting experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Experience producing recurring reporting deliverables on a fixed cycle, including assembling content from multiple contributors and meeting a published distribution date.

Experience verifying reported figures and status against source records, and resolving discrepancies with the team or organization that submitted them.

Working knowledge of program controls and construction management reporting content, including progress, cost, schedule, and change status, and where each of those figures originates.

Experience with industry standard program reporting and document management software (e.g., Kahua, Unifier, e-Builder, SharePoint, ProjectWise, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in construction management, engineering, business administration, or public administration.

Active professional certifications such as CCM (CMAA), and/or PMP or CAPM (PMI).

Experience serving as the lead producer of a program’s recurring reporting package on a program exceeding $1B in construction value.

Experience producing board, committee, or oversight body reporting deliverables on a publicly funded capital program.

Experience assembling federal or state grant reporting, funding drawdown packages, or external audit responses, including the documentation trail behind them.

Experience consolidating reporting across a portfolio of concurrent projects and contracts into a single program-level package.

Experience developing reporting templates, data definitions, or format standards that other teams then produced reporting to.

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Document Control Specialist
New York, New York, United States · Posted: 2026-10-16T17:55:30-04:00
Comp: Salary: $80k-$140k/year ($38-$67/hour)
Job description
About the Positions

We’re seeking 
Document Control Specialists
 of various skill levels to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. These positions own the integrity of the project record: which revision is current, who holds it, where it lives, and whether it will still stand up when someone pulls it years from now. Luster’s quality management system is ISO 9001:2015 certified, so controlled document practice on our programs is a standard we are audited against rather than a preference.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. 
We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Note: We are seeking candidates of various skill levels, and the following responsibilities represent the core of these roles. Scope and complexity increase with experience level.

Maintain the controlled document register in the program’s electronic document management system, so the current approved revision is the only one in circulation.

Apply the program’s numbering, naming, metadata, and revision conventions to incoming and outgoing records, including drawings, specifications, submittals, and correspondence, so any document can be retrieved years later.

Control the distribution of controlled documents against the program’s distribution matrix, and issue transmittals that record who received which revision and when.

Verify that superseded revisions are withdrawn from circulation and archived, and that the record set in the field offices matches the record set in the system.

Administer user access, permissions, and confidentiality handling in the document management system, including restricted handling of procurement, legal, and security sensitive records.

Audit the document register for missing, misfiled, or unindexed records, and correct discrepancies before they surface in an audit or a claim.

Prepare records for internal and external audits, including ISO 9001:2015 quality audits, agency reviews, and funding reviews, and produce the requested evidence within the time the auditor allows.

Coordinate document flow across program technical staff, designers, contractors, and agency reviewers on assigned packages.

Train program staff, consultants, and contractors on the document control procedure, and correct misuse of the system before it corrupts the record.

Report register status to the project management team, including revision status, overdue transmittals, and records outstanding against the procedure.

Compile and turn over the closeout record set, including as-built documentation, warranties, and archival against the program’s retention schedule.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in construction management, project management, engineering, or information management, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

5+ years of document control experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Experience controlling construction and program records through a full revision lifecycle, including drawings, specifications, submittals, requests for information, and correspondence.

Working knowledge of ISO-based document control practice, including numbering and metadata conventions, control of documented information, distribution control, and records retention.

Experience with industry standard document management and project / construction management software (e.g., SharePoint, Oracle Aconex, e-Builder, Unifier, Kahua, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in construction management, project management, engineering, or information management.

Active professional certifications such as CRM (ICRM), IGP (ARMA), and/or CDT (CSI).

Experience serving as the lead document control resource for the owner on a program exceeding $1B in construction value.

Experience standing up a document control function at the start of a program, including the numbering convention, metadata schema, workflow configuration, and the written document control procedure.

Experience supporting external quality audits under ISO 9001:2015 and producing objective evidence on request.

Experience controlling records across multiple concurrent contracts or work packages on the same program, including highway, bridge, transit, airport, and water and wastewater work.

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Compensation Details

Expected Salary: $80k-$140k/year ($38-$67/hour). Luster provides the salary range that the company in good faith believes it might offer for this position based on the successful candidate’s level and years of experience, knowledge, skills, abilities, education, certifications, licenses, geographic location, etc. Luster reserves the right to ultimately pay more or less than the posted range depending on circumstances not related to any status protected by local, state, and/or federal law.

Project Scheduler
San Jose, California, United States · Posted: 2026-07-13T17:27:30-04:00
Comp: Salary: $105k-$135k/year ($50-$65/hour)
Job description
About the Position

We’re seeking a 
Project Scheduler
 to support a portfolio of major transit capital improvement projects. Your primary focus will be developing, maintaining, and analyzing project schedules for the owner's Project Controls team, supporting projects from planning and design through construction and closeout while helping ensure successful project delivery.

This is a long-term, full-time, on-site position located in San Jose, CA.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Develop, maintain, and update master schedules, detailed project schedules, schedule forecasts, recovery schedules, and schedule reports for a portfolio of transportation capital projects.

Manage and regularly update schedules for approximately 80 to 100 active projects throughout planning, design, procurement, and construction.

Analyze project schedules to identify critical path activities, schedule risks, constraints, and opportunities for schedule improvement.

Review contractor baseline schedules, monthly schedule updates, recovery schedules, and schedule narratives for compliance with contract requirements.

Perform Time Impact Analysis (TIA) to evaluate schedule impacts associated with contract changes, delays, and change orders.

Coordinate closely with project managers, project controls staff, consultants, contractors, and stakeholders to maintain accurate project schedules and resolve schedule-related issues.

Integrate individual project schedules into larger program or master schedules to support program-level reporting and decision-making.

Support project controls activities involving schedule performance, cost controls, funding, earned value concepts, and project reporting.

Prepare schedule analyses, progress reports, executive dashboards, and other management reports that communicate project status, schedule performance, and forecasted outcomes.

Provide scheduling requirements and schedule specifications for inclusion in procurement and construction contract documents.

Evaluate contractor work sequencing, construction methods, productivity assumptions, and schedule logic to verify schedule reasonableness.

Support contract administration activities involving schedule analysis, change management, claims avoidance, and schedule documentation.

Coordinate with internal departments and external agencies to support project planning, delivery, and reporting requirements.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent organizational and analytical skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a passion for continuous improvement.

Ability to communicate schedule status, risks, and recommendations to both technical and executive stakeholders.

Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality, accountability, and professionalism.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, construction management, architecture, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

5+ years of experience developing, maintaining, and analyzing schedules for transit or other similar heavy civil infrastructure capital projects.

Strong knowledge of Critical Path Method (CPM) scheduling principles, schedule development, schedule analysis, and schedule forecasting.

Experience developing and reviewing contractor baseline schedules and monthly schedule updates.

Experience performing Time Impact Analysis (TIA) and evaluating schedule impacts associated with contract changes and delays.

Knowledge of earned value concepts and their application to project controls and schedule performance measurement.

Understanding of construction sequencing, construction means and methods, contract administration, and change management.

Experience coordinating with project managers, contractors, consultants, and owner representatives throughout project delivery.

Experience preparing schedule analyses, progress reports, executive reporting, and schedule performance metrics.

Proficiency with Oracle Primavera P6, Oracle Primavera Unifier, Microsoft Project, and other project controls software.

Proficiency with Microsoft Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, construction management, or architecture.

Planning & Scheduling Professional (PSP), Project Management Professional (PMP), Certified Cost Professional (CCP), or equivalent certification.

Experience supporting owner’s representative, program management, or construction management assignments.

Experience supporting design-build, CM/GC, or progressive design-build delivery methods.

Experience evaluating construction claims and schedule entitlement.

Experience integrating multiple project schedules into program-level master schedules.

Familiarity with Microsoft Power BI or similar dashboard KPI reporting software.

Compensation Details

Expected Salary: $105k-$135k/year ($50-$65/hour). Project Coordinator
Washington, District of Columbia, United States · Posted: 2026-10-15T21:25:10-04:00

Job description
About the Positions

We’re seeking 
Project Coordinators
 to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. These positions keep the project office running: submittals and requests for information moving inside contractual time frames, action items closed, cost and progress reporting current, and a project record that holds up long after the people who built it have moved on. We place coordinators into program offices, field offices, and construction management teams, so we are looking for people who have carried the day to day coordination load on a program of real size.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Coordinate the daily operations of the project office, including meeting agendas, minutes, and action item tracking, and drive open items to closure with the parties who own them.

Track submittals, requests for information, and change documentation through the program’s management information system, and keep contractor and reviewer turnaround inside the contractual time frames.

Maintain the project record, including correspondence, transmittals, contract documents, and supporting files, so decisions stay traceable through audit, claim review, and funding review.

Review contractor and consultant deliverables for completeness and conformance with the contract’s documentation requirements before they reach the program’s technical reviewers.

Monitor progress reporting and field activity against the accepted schedule, and report deviations, operational impacts, and discrepancies to the project manager.

Develop project status reports, progress summaries, and staffing plans for program and funding agency audiences, drawn from schedule, cost, and document control data.

Support program cost tracking by maintaining budget, accrual, invoice, and cash flow records, and reconciling pay applications and change documentation against the program’s cost record.

Coordinate site access, badging, escorts, and work windows on active facilities so field work happens only inside the periods the operator approves.

Coordinate information flow across program disciplines, agency stakeholders, third parties, and adjacent contracts so questions reach the right reviewer and the answers get recorded.

Coordinate contract closeout, including punch list tracking, final inspection scheduling, as-built and warranty submittals, and record retention.

Guide project staff on the program’s documentation standards and the proper use of project systems and procedures.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Bachelor’s degree in construction management, civil engineering, construction engineering, or project management, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

5+ years of project coordination experience on multiple task order contracts for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Experience tracking submittals, requests for information, and change documentation through a project or construction management information system on transit and transportation projects.

Working knowledge of construction contract administration, including submittal and request for information workflows, change documentation, and project recordkeeping.

Thorough knowledge of general office practices and procedures, including business correspondence standards and the arithmetic behind quantity, invoice, and budget records.

Experience with industry standard project / construction management software (e.g., Primavera P6, MS Project, Unifier, Kahua, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in construction management, civil engineering, construction engineering, or project management.

Active professional certifications such as CAPM or PMP (PMI), and/or CCM (CMAA).

Experience coordinating the owner’s project office on a program exceeding $1B in construction value.

Experience coordinating documentation, reporting, and correspondence across multiple concurrent contracts or work packages on the same program.

Experience supporting contract administration on a package exceeding $100M in construction value, including change documentation, pay applications, and closeout.

Experience coordinating submittal and shop drawing tracking on bridge or structures packages.

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Job description
About the Position

We’re seeking a 
Senior Document Control Specialist 
to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. This position is the technical lead for document control on a major rail capital program, serving as the subject matter expert for the enterprise document control system and the standards behind it. You’ll keep controlled record sets accurate, traceable, and audit-ready while supporting system rollout, adoption, and continuous improvement across projects and functional groups.

This is a long-term, full-time, hybrid (3-4 days per week on-site) position based in Sacramento, CA.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Serve as the technical subject matter expert for document control systems, processes, and standards, and provide guidance and mentoring to document controllers, program analysts, and project teams.

Oversee document intake, processing, distribution, storage, and archival for design, construction, right-of-way, and environmental record sets across a rail capital program.

Review document submittals for completeness, accuracy, metadata, naming convention, version control, and classification compliance before acceptance into the document management system.

Perform system administration for the enterprise document control platform, including configuration, permissions, workflows, and troubleshooting.

Support deployment, configuration, and optimization of the enterprise document control system, and participate in defining system requirements, workflows, user roles, and reporting capabilities.

Evaluate system gaps, risks, and improvement opportunities, and recommend enhancements that improve efficiency and data integrity.

Develop and maintain process maps, standard operating procedures, desk manuals, and system user guides.

Maintain document control dashboards, trackers, risk logs, and issue logs, and monitor performance metrics, workload trends, and compliance indicators.

Support audit readiness by verifying that documentation is complete, traceable, and retained in line with contract and regulatory requirements.

Coordinate with project teams, IT, business analysts, procurement, and compliance staff, and serve as a point of contact for document control matters with staff, consultants, and contractors.

Provide training, onboarding, and ongoing user support, and support change management as new tools, workflows, and standards are adopted.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Composure to hold a documentation standard when the pressure is to move faster.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in business administration, information management, records management, or construction management, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

8+ years of document control experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Experience serving as a senior or lead document controller on a capital program, including submittal review, version control, and controlled record maintenance.

Experience developing standard operating procedures, workflows, process maps, and training materials for document control operations.

Working knowledge of document control standards, metadata and naming conventions, records retention requirements, and audit and compliance obligations.

Experience with enterprise electronic document management systems (e.g., SharePoint, Aconex, Unifier, ProjectWise, Adobe Acrobat, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in business administration, information management, records management, or construction management.

10+ years of document control experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Certified Records Manager (CRM) (Institute of Certified Records Managers), or Certified Document Imaging Architech+ (CDIA+) certification (CompTIA).

Experience serving as system administrator or subject matter expert for an enterprise-wide document control system rollout across multiple projects or business units.

Experience supporting document control on a rail or transit capital program exceeding $1B in construction value.

Experience supporting system implementation, change management, or process improvement initiatives affecting document control users across an organization.

Experience coordinating document control across multiple concurrent contracts or design packages on a single program.

Working knowledge of public agency records retention schedules, public records request handling, and audit response.

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Compensation Details

Expected Salary: $80k-$130k/year ($38-$63/hour). Document Control Specialist
Sacramento, California, United States · Posted: 2026-09-10T14:51:55-04:00
Comp: Salary: $68k-$117k/year ($33-$56/hour)
Job description
About the Position

We’re seeking a 
Document Control Specialist
 to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. This position supports the document control function on a major rail capital program, keeping the electronic document management system accurate, traceable, and audit-ready as submittals, drawings, and correspondence move through review. You’ll be the person who knows where a record lives, which revision governs, and whether the approval trail holds up under audit.

This is a long-term, full-time, hybrid (3-4 days per week on-site) position based in Sacramento, CA.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Maintain document control systems and workflows for document submissions, approvals, and distribution.

Support setup and configuration of the electronic document management system, including folder architecture, metadata schemas, naming conventions, automated workflows, and user roles and permissions.

Receive and log incoming submittals, drawings, and correspondence into the document control system, verifying that metadata including title, number, revision, discipline, and originator is accurate and complete.

Maintain master copies of controlled documents, track revisions, and verify that formatting and naming conventions conform to program standards.

Coordinate with contractors, consultants, and program staff so required documentation is submitted on schedule and retrievable when needed.

Verify compliance with document control standards, QA/QC protocols, and contractual, legal, and regulatory requirements, including ISO 9001:2015, FTA, and FRA.

Perform periodic audits for metadata accuracy, overdue reviews, unauthorized revisions, and approval gaps, and flag inconsistencies for corrective action.

Support development and upkeep of the document control management guide so it reflects current procedures, system changes, and compliance requirements.

Generate reports on document status, track submittal turnaround times, escalate review bottlenecks, and maintain the trackers and dashboards that keep program leadership informed.

Monitor document retention schedules, archive project records, and support legal holds, public records requests, and third-party audit responses.

Provide training and user support on document control processes and tools, and maintain training records and reference materials.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Willingness to hold a documentation standard when the person submitting outranks you.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in business administration, information management, construction management, or engineering, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

3+ years of document control experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Experience administering an electronic document management system as the system of record, including metadata, revision control, and controlled workflows.

Experience logging, tracking, and reporting on submittals, requests for information, and program correspondence through review and closure.

Working knowledge of records retention, document traceability, and audit readiness under a quality management system.

Experience with industry standard electronic document management platforms (e.g., Aconex, Unifier, Kahua, ProjectWise, SharePoint, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in business administration, information management, construction management, or engineering.

Certified Records Manager (CRM) certification (Institute of Certified Records Managers) or Information Governance Professional (IGP) certification (ARMA International).

Experience supporting document control on a capital program exceeding $1B in construction value.

Experience supporting document control from an owner’s representative, program management, or construction management position.

Experience supporting ISO 9001:2015 internal audits, external audits, or recertification, including evidence gathering and corrective action tracking.

Experience supporting public records requests, legal holds, or third-party audit responses on a publicly funded program.

Experience configuring or migrating an electronic document management system, including folder architecture, metadata schemas, and permission structures.

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Compensation Details

Expected Salary: $68k-$117k/year ($33-$56/hour). At Broadpin, we don’t just implement technology — we enable transformation.

Broadpin is seeking an experienced Oracle Primavera P6 EPPM and Oracle Primavera Cloud (OPC) Consultant for a remote position. The ideal candidate will have 8+ years of experience supporting clients through the entire implementation lifecycle, from concept through go-live and post-production support.
Responsibilities include analyzing business processes, recommending future-state workflows, defining solution requirements, ensuring alignment with client IT standards, and supporting deployed solutions.
Responsibilities

Manage the full implementation lifecycle from concept through program launch.
Analyze current (as-is) processes and recommend future-state business processes based on client requirements and best practices.
Collaborate with consultants to document solution requirements, including functional and technical specifications.
Work with clients to meet IT requirements that support solution deployment and align with organizational IT roadmaps.
Manage project deliverables, including project charters, risks, and issue resolution.
Build strong client relationships and quickly learn their processes, culture, and business objectives.
Provide Level 2 production support for deployed solutions.

Qualifications

8+ years of program management experience across multiple industries.
5+ years of experience with Oracle Primavera P6 EPPM (P6 Professional and P6 EPPM Web) and Oracle Primavera Cloud (OPC).
Strong understanding of project change management, risk management, and quality management.
Experience leading teams of functional and technical consultants.
Strong communication and client management skills.
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience.

Experience working with Primavera P6 integrations with Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems.
Experience with Oracle Primavera Unifier.

Why Join Us?

Collaborate with a team of industry experts and technology leaders.
Work on impactful projects across various industries.
Expand your expertise in Primavera P6, Oracle Primavera Cloud, and system integrations.
Competitive compensation, benefits, and professional growth opportunities.

Job description
About the Positions

We’re seeking 
Office Engineers
 of various skill levels to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. These positions run the construction office: submittals, RFIs, contract records, pay applications, and change documentation. You’ll keep that record complete and current so decisions on payment, time, and entitlement hold up months later under audit or claim review.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. 
We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Note: We are seeking candidates of various skill levels, and the following responsibilities represent the core of these roles. Scope and complexity increase with experience level.

May administer the program’s submittal and RFI process, logging, distributing, and tracking each item through technical review to a documented response within the contractual review period.

Maintain the construction record set, including contract documents, plans, specifications, addenda, and as-built markups, so the current approved version is the one in use.

Review pay applications and progress payment requests against verified quantities, the approved schedule of values, and contract terms, and route them for approval.

Compile and track change order documentation, including entitlement records, independent estimate backup, and negotiation history, so the program’s position is documented before anything is executed.

Monitor contract compliance items, including insurance certificates, bonds, certified payroll, DBE participation, and permit conditions, and escalate lapses before they affect payment.

Coordinate document flow across active work areas and the contract packages they support.

Reconcile field records, daily reports, and quantity documentation against contractor submissions so program records support payment decisions and claim review.

Coordinate with contractors, designers, and agency staff to keep responses moving, and document review cycle delays and their cause when they occur.

Prepare program progress reports, log summaries, and meeting minutes, and track open action items to closure.

Organize the project’s document control structure, including naming conventions, version control, and retention, so the record survives audit, claim review, and funding review.

Support schedule updates by reconciling schedule submissions against program records of submittals, RFIs, and change activity.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering, construction engineering, construction management, or engineering technology, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

5+ years of office engineering experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Experience administering submittal, RFI, and construction correspondence logs on an active construction program.

Working knowledge of contract documents, technical specifications, and construction drawings, and of how pay applications and change orders are documented against them.

Experience with industry standard document management and project / construction management software (e.g., Procore, e-Builder, Primavera P6, Unifier, Kahua, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in civil engineering, construction engineering, construction management, or engineering technology.

Active professional certifications such as CCM (CMAA), PMP (PMI), and/or CDT (CSI).

Experience running the owner’s construction office records on a package exceeding $100M in construction value.

Experience administering pay applications and progress payments on a program valued at $1B+.

Experience assembling change order and claim documentation that was later relied on in negotiation, dispute review board, or audit.

Understanding of public agency procedures and contract compliance requirements (e.g., FTA, FAA, state DOT, etc.).

Experience with industry standard labor compliance and document collaboration software (e.g., LCPtracker, B2GNow, Bluebeam Revu, SharePoint, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Compensation Details

Expected Salary: $90k-$150k/year ($43-$72/hour). Washington, District of Columbia, United States · Posted: 2026-10-15T21:24:46-04:00
Comp: pay applications and progress payments on a program valued at $1B+
Job description
About the Positions

We’re seeking 
Office Engineers
 to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. These positions run the construction office: submittals, RFIs, contract records, pay applications, and change documentation. You’ll keep that record complete and current so decisions on payment, time, and entitlement hold up months later under audit or claim review.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

May administer the program’s submittal and RFI process, logging, distributing, and tracking each item through technical review to a documented response within the contractual review period.

Maintain the construction record set, including contract documents, plans, specifications, addenda, and as-built markups, so the current approved version is the one in use.

Review pay applications and progress payment requests against verified quantities, the approved schedule of values, and contract terms, and route them for approval.

Compile and track change order documentation, including entitlement records, independent estimate backup, and negotiation history, so the program’s position is documented before anything is executed.

Monitor contract compliance items, including insurance certificates, bonds, certified payroll, DBE participation, and permit conditions, and escalate lapses before they affect payment.

Coordinate document flow across active work areas and the contract packages they support.

Reconcile field records, daily reports, and quantity documentation against contractor submissions so program records support payment decisions and claim review.

Coordinate with contractors, designers, and agency staff to keep responses moving, and document review cycle delays and their cause when they occur.

Prepare program progress reports, log summaries, and meeting minutes, and track open action items to closure.

Organize the project’s document control structure, including naming conventions, version control, and retention, so the record survives audit, claim review, and funding review.

Support schedule updates by reconciling schedule submissions against program records of submittals, RFIs, and change activity.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering, construction engineering, construction management, or engineering technology, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

5+ years of office engineering, quality control, and construction safety experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Experience supporting transportation projects delivered under a multiple task order contract, including task order records and status reporting.

Experience administering submittal, RFI, and construction correspondence logs on an active construction program.

Working knowledge of contract documents, technical specifications, and construction drawings, and of how pay applications and change orders are documented against them.

Experience with industry standard document management and project / construction management software (e.g., Procore, e-Builder, Primavera P6, Unifier, Kahua, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in civil engineering, construction engineering, construction management, or engineering technology.

Active professional certifications such as CCM (CMAA), PMP (PMI), and/or CDT (CSI).

Experience running the owner’s construction office records on a package exceeding $100M in construction value.

Experience administering pay applications and progress payments on a program valued at $1B+.

Experience assembling change order and claim documentation that was later relied on in negotiation, dispute review board, or audit.

Understanding of public agency procedures and contract compliance requirements (e.g., FTA, FAA, state DOT, etc.).

Experience with industry standard labor compliance and document collaboration software (e.g., LCPtracker, B2GNow, Bluebeam Revu, SharePoint, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Compensation Details

Expected Salary: $90k-$150k/year ($43-$72/hour). Luster provides the salary range that the company in good faith believes it might offer for this position based on the successful candidate’s level and years of experience, knowledge, skills, abilities, education, certifications, licenses, geographic location, etc. Luster reserves the right to ultimately pay more or less than the posted range depending on circumstances not related to any status protected by local, state, and/or federal law.

Project Overview:
 
Bechtel’s Manufacturing and Technology (M&T) is an exciting and growing business unit that serves customers in the semiconductor, electric vehicle, and datacenter markets. M&T strives to exceed our customer objectives through utilizing our agility, innovative technologies, and world class talent. Job Summary:
 
Provides engineering assistance to superintendents, directs assigned personnel in meeting cost and time schedules, verifies materials, equipment, and quality and assures results meet design requirements. We will be pouring a lot of concrete (a lot of elevated work) with heavy duty reinforcement, sometimes in cold weather, and we're looking for folks with that kind of experience. #LI-ME1
Major Responsibilities:
 
Responsible for the activities of assigned construction engineers, such as the application of drawings, specifications, and subcontracts.
Directs preparation of quantity listings of field purchased material and equipment and initiates requisitions for field purchases.
Supervises preparation of construction drawings and schedules, design of temporary construction facilities, and ensures preparation of “as built” drawings and other job plans Assists subordinate construction engineers and superintendents.
Interpreting design drawings.
Monitoring equipment installation and planning for delivery of construction materials and equipment.
Assuring that proper warehousing and storage exists to ensure environmental protection.
Reviews specifications, purchase orders, subcontracts, inspection reports, delivery schedules, instruction manuals, and technical data.
Administers assigned subcontracts to ensure contract remains up to date in areas such as drawings, specifications, cost, and schedule.
Coordinates with the Field Construction Manager on activities affecting the contract administration operation.
Coordinates with engineering design on constructability issues.
Supervises subcontractor work efforts and administers routine subcontract changes and interfaces with client personnel; may represent the company in contractual discussions and negotiations.
Performs personnel evaluation of assigned subordinate personnel and ensures they receive progressive training.
May direct minimal numbers of manual craft field forces during project closeout.
Works with various functions to ensure the project achieves corporate goals set for environmental, safety & health, quality, cost, and schedule
Education and Experience Requirements:
 
 Required bachelor's degree (or international equivalent) and 8-10  years of relevant experience or 12-14 years of relevant work experience
Required Knowledge and Skills:
 
An understanding of applicable Bechtel work processes, including Standard Work Process Procedures, is preferred. 
Experience in semiconductor fabrication facilities is preferred. 
Working knowledge of ACI 301, 318, 117-10, 305R, 306R, CRSI, AISC, RCSC 
Familiarity with Bechtel Standard Applications (BSAPs), including TEAMWorks, Aconex, DSCS, Unifier, Agile, Navisworks, and other automation tools used on Bechtel projects. 
Computer literate in word processing, spreadsheet, and database applications.  Excellent communication and problem-solving ability.

Project Overview:
 
Bechtel is building a semiconductor manufacturing plant in New Albany, Ohio. We are partnering with the North America Building Trades Unions and suppliers to create several thousand new jobs and work with local education organizations to implement new training programs that will support the future talent pipeline. Bechtel Manufacturing & Technology, Inc. offers engineering, procurement, and construction services for customers in the semiconductor manufacturing, electric vehicle, and data center markets. Headquartered in Reston, Virginia, the M&T global business unit also includes colleagues working in Arizona, Ohio, Texas, India, and additional project locations around the world.
Job Summary:
 
Civil-Structural Field Engineer will report directly to the Area  Field Engineer assist the construction team in the technical aspects of the civil, structural, and architectural scope. Individual will provide direct support to superintendents and craft professionals, including, but not limited to, work package creation and maintenance, quality control, quantity verifications, material take-offs, material verifications, design change coordination, and general problem solving – all in support of meeting project cost and time schedules.   
Project involves a significant civil/structural scope involving both structural concrete and structural steel. Candidate should be well versed in concrete operations and the American Concrete Institute (ACI) Codes and Standards. Candidate should be well versed in structural steel erection and the American Institute of Steel Construction manual and standards. Candidate should be able to proficiently work in high-paced environments and manage change while upholding Bechtel Safety and Quality standards.
#LI-CL1
Major Responsibilities:
 
Collaborate with engineering teams to address constructability and design challenges related to commodity installations and work sequencing 
Provide comprehensive field engineering support to superintendents and project personnel, ensuring adherence to cost and schedule objectives
Develop work plans, perform material take-offs, create material requisitions, perform and document quality control inspections, report installation progress, and resolve design and construction conflicts related to the installation and testing of civil/structural commodities 
Perform civil field engineering activities including inspections, audits, and planning to support the installation of formwork, rebar, concrete, structural steel, architectural commodities, and earthworks 
Assure procedural compliance for work being completed in the field
Review specifications, purchase orders, subcontracts, inspection reports, delivery schedules, instruction manuals, and technical data to assist and advise on site.
Oversee, interface, and coordinate with subcontractors and subcontractor work efforts. Assist in the management of subcontract changes.
Education and Experience Requirements:
 
 Required bachelor's degree (or international equivalent) and 5-8 years of relevant experience or 9-12 years of relevant work experience
Required Knowledge and Skills:
 
Must be physically able to conduct field inspections and participate in project walk-downs which may require the following activities: extensive walking in and around a construction site, climbing ladders, climbing scaffolding, using fall protection and other personal protective equipment (PPE), walking on elevated platforms, walking on uneven surfaces, and maneuvering around very small and/or confined spaces. 
Must be able to complete and pass a pre-employment drug screen 
Demonstrated commitment to Environment, Safety and Health (ES&H). Demonstrated commitment to a Zero Accident safety program.
An understanding of applicable Bechtel work processes, including Standard Work Process Procedures, is preferred. 
Experience in semiconductor fabrication facilities is preferred. 
Working knowledge of ACI 301, 318, 117-10, 305R, 306R, CRSI, AISC, RCSC 
Familiarity with Bechtel Standard Applications (BSAPs), including TEAMWorks, Aconex, DSCS, Unifier, Agile, Navisworks, and other automation tools used on Bechtel projects. 
Computer literate in word processing, spreadsheet, and database applications. 
Excellent communication and problem-solving ability.

Project Overview:
 
Louisiana LNG is located approximately 11 miles southwest of Lake Charles, Louisiana. The project includes a mid-scale, mixed-refrigerant Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) production and export facility on the west side of the Calcasieu River. There are five identical process plants. Each process plant consists of one gas pre-treatment unit, one condensate stabilization unit, and four Chart heavy hydrocarbon (HHC) removal and liquefaction groups. The facility will include associated utilities, refrigerant storage, three 235,000m3 full-containment LNG storage tanks, and three marine berths.
Job Summary:
 
In this role, you will provide project field engineering specialization and expertise with work planning and packaging, material management, quantity verification and validation, safety and quality control, technical inspection and testing knowledge, and subcontract coordination. Your recommendations will ensure field engineering activities operate safely, are complete, and conform to quality standards and project requirements. 
#LI-BH1
Major Responsibilities:
 
Work Planning & Packaging 
Prepares construction drawings and sketches. 
Facilitates planning construction methods and procedures.   
Material Management  
Initiates requisitions for field purchases                         
Prepares quantity takeoffs of field purchased material and equipment. 
Quantities 
Verifies commodities on quantity tracking systems or other computer database systems as required.  
Safety / Quality Control 
Ensures zero accident philosophy and requirements are implemented and adhered to by craft and others when in the operational area, and tools and equipment are in safe condition and operated safely. 
Technical  
Proactively considers continuous learning or show interest to pursue appropriate learning activities 
System Turnover Coordinator  
For Direct Hire:  
Develops firm understanding of system and area scoping and drawings required for package development. 
STR / Subcontract Coordinator 
Reviews and approves inspection test plans,  
Coordinates reviews of subcontractor submittals,  
Education and Experience Requirements:
 
 Required bachelor's degree (or international equivalent) and 5-8 years of relevant experience or 9-12 years of relevant work experience
Required Knowledge and Skills:
 
Experience in a field construction environment working with specifications, vendor procedures, instructions, & codes.
Heavy industrial direct hire construction experience commensurate with the type of work to be undertaken.
Demonstrated ability to motivate and lead team members effectively & positively in a collaborative team environment.
Demonstrated ability to problem-solve in high pressure situations.
Experience in oil, gas, refinery, petrochemical, minerals processing or power generating station construction.
Good knowledge in MS Word, Excel, Visio, PowerPoint, and other common applications used on the construction industry.
Working knowledge of applicable industry codes and standards.
Experience managing technical services subcontracts.
Experience on an LNG construction site
Understanding of applicable Bechtel work processes including Standard Work Process Procedures.
Advanced knowledge of Project Bechtel Standard Applications (BSAPs) including Setroute, Unifier, Aconex, DSCS, PTR, Agile, Navisworks, and other automation tools which are used on Bechtel projects.
 
Additional Information: Work requires the physical ability to conduct field inspections including but not limited to: extensive walking in and around a construction site often in high heat and high humidity conditions, climbing ladders, climbing scaffolding, working on elevated platforms, working on uneven surfaces, and working in small or confined spaces. Some lifting may be required. Must have the ability to walk into and out of the project (enter/egress). Must be able to use appropriate standard issued Personal Protection Equipment (PPE) required for each assigned task (i.e. harness, life vest, lift buckets, etc.).

Your oversight will ensure craft professionals have the tools required to be productive, comply with project policies, procedures, and job site work rules and procedures, and perform within specifications, schedules and budgets.

Demonstrated ability to motivate and lead team members effectively & positively in a collaborative team environment.
Demonstrated ability to problem-solve in high pressure situations.
Heavy industrial direct hire construction experience in a supervisory role commensurate with the type of work to be undertaken.

Job Summary:
 
LOTO Tagging Authority (TA) will report to the Lead LOTO Tagging Authority and is responsible for receiving and acting on requests to perform work on components or systems that are energized or have the potential to be energized. The TA will be responsible for energy isolation management in accordance with corporate and project specific procedures. Must be willing to work a flexible schedule if required.
Acting as the primary on-site LOTO Tagging Authority for commissioning, this position works closely with engineering, construction, operations, vendors, equipment suppliers, commissioning teams, and Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJs) to develop and execute comprehensive testing and validation programs. The role provides technical leadership throughout system turnover, integrated systems testing, regulatory inspections, and operational readiness activities to ensure all life safety systems are fully functional, code-compliant, documented, and ready for safe occupancy and operation.
•    Collaborate: Actively seeks out others’ opinions and input and is open-minded to their views. Challenges others appropriately and is also open to being challenged on their own views. 
•    Communicate: Is effective at adapting their communication style appropriately to their audience, providing context and using the right tone and level of information. 
•    Customer Focus: Prioritizes the customer needs and puts these at the forefront of all interactions. Ensures that others within their team maintain this same approach.
•    Deliver: Demonstrates making well thought out, timely decisions and prioritization that leads to successful outcomes. Includes the right people at the right time. 
•    Problem Solve: Accurately assesses a situation to find the best solution or way of working in order to resolve the issues. Is focused on creating a long term fix rather than a short-term solution.
•    Role Model: Contributes to the Bechtel culture by inspiring and motivating others through their positive approach and attitude. Comes to work determined to do a good job, for themselves and for their team. .

Major Responsibilities:
 
Manage the integrated LOTO program on the Project coordinating between subcontractors, JV partners, and all other affected entities to deliver a safe and uniform program for the control of work and isolation of hazardous sources of energy.
Ensure the energy isolation program complies with SWPP's, STCP's, and Q4Safety. Use Q4Safety for electronic Energy Isolation Permits (EIP's).
Provide input and support to the Construction, Operations, and Commissioning teams, in piping, mechanical, and electrical isolations.
Identify isolation boundaries based on work scope and develop and issue EIP's.
Administer and manage the energy isolation program with strict enforcement and record keeping.

Procure material required to support the energy isolation management program.
Monitors the activities of subcontractors to ensure compliance with energy isolation.

Monitor the installation of LOTO equipment such as Locks and Tags etc.
Work hours as required, including overtime, weekends, and holidays, as necessary to support the project.

Bechtel is partnering with NextDecade to support their vision to provide the world access to lower carbon intensive energy with their Rio Grande LNG (RGLNG) project in Brownsville, Texas. RGLNG is a natural gas liquefaction and export terminal situated on a 984-acre site on the banks of the Brownsville ship channel. At full capacity, the five-train facility will have a production capacity of 27 million tonnes per annum (MTPA). Brownsville, Texas is a city known for its diverse history, tradition, and rich culture. Project Overview:
 
Bechtel is building a semiconductor manufacturing plant in New Albany, Ohio. Bechtel will design and build Phase 1 of the Ohio One project, a total of 2.5 million square feet, including 600,000 square feet of cleanrooms. Construction will require as much steel as eight Eiffel Towers and as much concrete as the tallest skyscrapers. Bechtel will strengthen future economic development in the region by partnering with the North America Building Trades Unions and suppliers to create several thousand new jobs and work with local education organizations to implement new training programs that will support the future talent pipeline.
Job Summary:
 
Architectural Field Engineer will assist the construction team in the technical aspects of the civil and architectural scope. Individual will provide direct support to superintendents and craft professionals, including, but not limited to, work package creation and maintenance, quality control, quantity verifications, material take-offs, material verifications, design change coordination, and general problem solving – all in support of meeting project cost and time schedules. The project involves a significant concrete and architectural scope. Candidate should be well versed in concrete operations and American Concrete Institute (ACI) Codes and Standards, with emphasis on concrete finishing, curing, and patching. Candidate should understand architectural systems and be able to organize and coordinate between concrete operations and architectural installations. Candidate should have an understanding of building systems such as drywall, wall paneling, Ceiling systems, light metal framing, doors, gates, and enclosures. Candidate should be able to proficiently work in high-paced environments and manage change while upholding Bechtel Safety and Quality standards.  
Major Responsibilities:
 
Coordinates with engineering on constructability and design issues relating to commodity installations and work sequencing. Provides field engineering support and assistance to superintendents, supporting personnel in meeting cost and time schedules, verifies materials, equipment, and quality, and assures results meet design requirements. Develops work plans, coordinate material take-offs and requisitions, perform and document inspections, report progress, and resolve conflicts in design and construction related to the installation and testing of civil commodities, Assures procedural compliance, material control, and complete and thorough documentation of inspections for completed work. Directs or performs preparation of quantity listings of field purchased material and equipment and initiates requisitions for field material purchases. Supports planning and delivery of construction materials and equipment, assuring that proper warehousing and storage exists to ensure environmental protection.  Review’s specifications, purchase orders, subcontracts, inspection reports, delivery schedules, instruction manuals, and technical data to assist and advise on site. Oversees and coordinates subcontractor work efforts and subcontract changes and interfaces.
Education and Experience Requirements:
 
Required bachelor's degree (or international equivalent) and 5-8 years of relevant experience or 9-12 years of relevant work experience
Required Knowledge and Skills:
 
Experience working with or designing building systems such as drywall, wall paneling, ceiling systems, light metal framing, doors, gates, and enclosures
Working knowledge of ACI 301, 318, 117-10, 305R, 306R
Familiarity with Bechtel Standard Applications (BSAPs), including TEAMWorks, Infoworks or Aconex, BPS or DSCS, PTR or Unifier, Agile, Navisworks, and other automation tools used on Bechtel projects
Computer literate in word processing, spreadsheet, and database applications
Excellent communication and problem-solving ability. 
Understanding of applicable Bechtel work processes, including Standard Work Process Procedures, is preferred.
Experience in semiconductor fab facilities is preferred.
Experience in clean room construction

Job Summary:
 
The Fire Protection & Life Safety Systems Subcontract Technical Representative (STR) serves as the primary technical and field liaison between Bechtel and subcontractors responsible for the Fire Protection, Fire Alarm, Voice Evacuation, and Early Warning Smoke Detection (VESDA) systems across Project Cardinal. The STR is responsible for overseeing the safe execution, technical compliance, installation, integration, testing, commissioning, and turnover of all fire suppression and life safety systems, including wet-pipe, dry-pipe, deluge, water spray, sprinkler, fire alarm, voice evacuation, and smoke detection systems serving the Fab, support buildings, utility facilities, warehouses, and specialty hazard areas. The STR works closely with Engineering, Quality, ES&H, Procurement, Construction, Startup, AHJs, SIAs, Intel, and subcontractor teams to ensure all systems are delivered in accordance with contract requirements, IMCS specifications, applicable codes and standards, approved design documents, and project schedule objectives.
Major Responsibilities:
 
Provide day-to-day leadership, coordination, and technical oversight of Fire Protection and Fire Alarm subcontractors from engineering through final turnover.
Ensure all fire suppression and life safety systems are designed, fabricated, installed, tested, commissioned, and documented in accordance with Intel Master Construction Specifications (IMCS), approved drawings, AHJ requirements, FM approvals, and applicable fire and life safety codes.
Coordinate and manage engineering deliverables including LOD400 models, hydraulic calculations, VESDA calculations, BIM coordination, clash resolution, shop drawings, material take-offs, equipment layouts, and as-built documentation.
Oversee installation and integration of fire alarm panels, voice evacuation systems, VESDA smoke detection systems, notification appliances, interface modules, sprinkler systems, dry-pipe systems,
deluge systems, fire water distribution components, valves, suppression equipment, and associated field devices.
Coordinate system interfaces between Fire Alarm, Fire Protection, HVAC, Building Management Systems (BMS), Facility Management Systems (FMS), Access Control, Elevator Systems, Electrical Systems, and other building infrastructures.
Manage quality surveillance activities, ITP implementation, inspections, testing requirements, special inspections, hydrostatic testing, flushing, integrated systems testing, performance testing, reliability testing, commissioning activities, and final acceptance testing.
Monitor subcontractor safety performance, workforce planning, material management, procurement status, construction progress, schedule adherence, and execution risks while ensuring compliance with project ES&H requirements.
Coordinate RFIs, technical clarifications, design conflicts, field changes, nonconformance resolution, punch list closure, and turnover documentation requirements.
Interface with Intel representatives, Quality organizations, Startup teams, Special Inspection Agencies (SIA), Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJs), Fire Marshals, manufacturers, and commissioning personnel to achieve successful system acceptance and turnover.
Support startup activities, operator training, O&M documentation, spare parts turnover, and final closeout of all Fire Protection and Life Safety systems.
