Level I - Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Construction Management, or other relevant technical disciplines from an accredited University, plus 5-8 years of relevant work experience; or 9-12 years of relevant work experience in lieu of a degree.

Project Overview:
 
Bechtel is building a semiconductor manufacturing plant in New Albany, Ohio. Bechtel will design and build Phase 1 of the Ohio One project, a total of 2.5 million square feet, including 600,000 square feet of cleanrooms. Construction will require as much steel as eight Eiffel Towers and as much concrete as the tallest skyscrapers.
Bechtel will strengthen future economic development in the region by partnering with the North America Building Trades Unions and suppliers to create several thousand new jobs and work with local education organizations to implement new training programs that will support the future talent pipeline.
Job Summary:
 
The Cleanroom Subcontract Technical Representative (STR) is responsible for the technical oversight, field execution, and coordination of the cleanroom build-out subcontracts across Project Cardinal. Cleanroom build-out is a system-of-systems rather than a single trade package, spanning the architectural envelope, mechanical and air management systems, and specialty cleanroom components serving the Phase 1 Fab: raised metal floor (RMF), furred, framed, studless and softwall assemblies, ceiling grid and suspension, fan filter units (FFUs), ULPA and AMC filtration, plenum barrier, ionization, pressurization, cleanroom specialties, and material handling interfaces. The STR serves as the primary interface between Bechtel and the cleanroom subcontractors, ensuring all design, supply, installation, testing, commissioning, and turnover activities are executed safely, on schedule, and in compliance with project specifications, contamination control protocols, quality standards, and construction work processes. The individual will provide direct support to the subcontractor including, but not limited to, quality control, quantity verifications, material take-offs, material verifications, design change coordination, and general problem solving – all in support of meeting project cost and time schedule objectives.
Major Responsibilities:
 
Provide day-to-day leadership, coordination, and technical oversight of cleanroom build-out subcontractors from engineering through final turnover, serving as the focal point for coordination of work by assigned subcontracts.
Ensure cleanroom envelope, air management, and specialty systems are designed, fabricated, installed, tested, commissioned, and documented in accordance with Specifications approved drawings, applicable codes and standards, and project schedule objectives.
Oversee installation of the ceiling system (grid structure, suspension, seismic bracing, lighting, access systems), FFUs, ULPA and AMC filters, ionization systems, the plenum barrier system, raised metal floor components (panels, pedestals, stringers, bracing), and cleanroom wall systems including doors, glazing, fire-rated construction, and pass-throughs.
Enforce contamination control requirements through each cleanroom protocol level, from initial conversion of construction space and blowdown through gowning, wipe-down, HEPA vacuum use, approved-material restrictions, cleanroom badging, and the static particle count criteria required before and after filter installation.
Coordinate the cleanroom build sequence – high and tight MEP, mixed air return shaft (MARS), ceilings, lights and FFUs, raised metal floor, and cleanroom walls – with Lead Superintendents, Lead Field Engineers, the direct hire team, and adjacent subcontractors.
Coordinate system interfaces with MEP, I&C, and process systems, including HVAC and process ductwork, Building Management and Facility Management Systems, fire protection and life safety, electrical, AMHS and stockers, tool interface zones, and HiNA crane scope where applicable.
Coordinate and manage engineering deliverables including models, BIM coordination and clash resolution, shop drawings, material take-offs, equipment and panel layouts, and as-built documentation.
Monitor long lead material status, delivery sequencing, and the clean storage and handling requirements for cleanroom ceiling components, FFUs, light fixtures, and filters, including supplier-furnished material integration into the field installation plan.
Manage quality surveillance activities, ITP implementation, inspections, installation tolerance verification, pressure and leak integrity testing, rough and final air balance, particle count verification, integrated systems testing, commissioning, and final acceptance testing.
Monitor subcontractor safety performance, workforce planning, material management, construction progress, schedule adherence, and execution risks while ensuring compliance with project ES&H requirements and the principles of the Integrated Safety Management System.
Validate subcontractor installed quantities, monthly progress payments, invoices, and force account and time reports, and coordinate RFIs, technical clarifications, design conflicts, field changes, nonconformance resolution, punch list closure, and turnover documentation requirements.
Manage and coordinate Subcontractor Construction Work Packages (CWPs) and subcontract-specific Condition Reports, including creation of Corrective Action Plans and participation in causal (apparent and root) analysis.
Support startup activities, operator training, O&M documentation, spare parts turnover, and final closeout of all cleanroom systems, interfacing with client representatives, Quality organizations, Startup teams, and commissioning personnel to achieve system acceptance and turnover.
Education and Experience Requirements:
 
Level I 
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Construction Management, or other relevant technical disciplines from an accredited University, plus 5-8 years of relevant work experience; or 9-12 years of relevant work experience in lieu of a degree.
Level II
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Construction Management, or other relevant technical disciplines from an accredited University, plus 8-10 years of relevant work experience; or 12-14 years of relevant work experience in lieu of a degree.
Required Knowledge and Skills:
 
Basic Qualifications
Working knowledge of cleanroom construction standards, contamination control protocols, and cleanliness classification and certification practices applicable to semiconductor manufacturing facilities, including ISO 14644 and IEST recommended practices.
Working knowledge of cleanroom envelope and air management systems – raised metal floor, cleanroom wall assemblies, ceiling grid, FFUs, ULPA and AMC filtration, plenum barrier, ionization, and pressure cascade requirements – including installation tolerances, sequencing, and pressure integrity requirements.
Ability to read and understand isometrics, P&ID’s, orthographics, plans, and other design drawings.
Working knowledge of applicable industry codes and standards is required. Excellent communication and problem-solving ability.
Understanding of applicable Bechtel work processes including Standard Work Process Procedures is preferred.
Computer literate in word processing, spreadsheet and database applications.
Must be physically able to conduct field inspections and participate in project walk-downs which may require the following activities: extensive walking in and around a construction site, climbing ladders, climbing scaffolding, using fall protection and other personal protective equipment (PPE), walking on elevated platforms, walking on uneven surfaces, and maneuvering around very small and/or confined spaces. Must also be able to work in full cleanroom gowning for extended periods.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience in semiconductor fabrication facilities, including first-of-a-kind cleanroom build-out execution, is preferred.
Proficient level of understanding of ISO 14644 and IEST-RP-CC standards, SMACNA and MFMA guidelines, IBC, NFPA, Ohio Building Code, ASCE 7, AISC, and RCSC.
Familiarity with Bechtel Standard Applications (BSAPs), including TEAMWorks, Aconex, DSCS, Unifier, Agile, Navisworks, and other automation tools used on Bechtel projects.
Proficiency in Navisworks Simulate and 3D model navigation is preferred.
Previous experience as a Subcontract Technical Representative or Quality Control Representative, including experience managing construction subcontracts and field design changes.
Experience supporting cleanroom certification activities, air balance, and particle count testing through startup and turnover.
Computer literate in word processing, spreadsheet, and database applications. Excellent communication and problem-solving ability.

Job Summary:
 
The Life Safety Systems (LSS), Pfisterer Terminations, and Fiber Optic Subcontract Technical Representative (STR) is responsible for the technical oversight, field execution, and coordination of a combined portfolio of electrical, low-voltage, and life safety subcontracts across Project Cardinal. The assigned scopes include the Life Safety Systems packages – fire alarm with voice evacuation and Early Warning Smoke Detection (EWSD), gas detection panels, Hazardous Production Material (HPM) monitoring, and Toxic Alarm System (TAS) PLCs on a design-build basis, and the combined Distributed Antenna System (DAS) and LSS site radio scope – together with medium and high voltage Pfisterer cable termination work and fiber optic cable pulling performed by a certified installer. The STR serves as the primary interface between Bechtel and the assigned subcontractors, ensuring all design, supply, installation, termination, testing, commissioning, and turnover activities are executed safely, on schedule, and in compliance with project specifications, quality standards, and construction work processes. The individual will provide direct support to the subcontractors including, but not limited to, quality control, quantity verifications, material take-offs, material verifications, design change coordination, and general problem solving – all in support of meeting project cost and time schedule objectives.
Major Responsibilities:
 
Provide day-to-day leadership, coordination, and technical oversight of the assigned LSS, Pfisterer termination, and fiber optic subcontractors from engineering through final turnover, serving as the focal point for coordination of work by assigned subcontracts.
Ensure all life safety, termination, and fiber optic systems are designed, fabricated, installed, terminated, tested, commissioned, and documented in accordance with the specifications, approved drawings, AHJ requirements, applicable codes and standards, and project schedule objectives.
Oversee installation and integration of fire alarm control panels, voice evacuation systems, EWSD detection, notification appliances, and interface modules, coordinating acceptance testing with the Fire Marshal, Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJs), and Special Inspection Agencies.
Oversee the design-build execution of gas detection panels, HPM monitoring, and TAS PLC systems, including panel fabrication and factory acceptance testing, field installation, I/O checkout, sequence of operations verification, alarm response validation, and integration with the Facilities Management System and life safety interlocks.
Coordinate the combined DAS and LSS site radio scope, including antenna and head-end equipment installation, coverage verification, and emergency responder communication system testing and acceptance.
Provide technical oversight of medium and high voltage Pfisterer termination work, including certified installer qualification, manufacturer training and workmanship requirements, cable preparation, environmental and cleanliness controls during termination, torque and assembly verification, hi-pot and partial discharge testing, and witness and hold point documentation.
Oversee fiber optic cable pulling, routing, splicing, and termination by the certified installer, including pull tension and bend radius controls, pathway and raceway readiness, cable management, labeling schemes, OTDR and insertion loss testing, and acceptance documentation.
Major Responsibility (Cont.)
 
Coordinate and manage engineering deliverables including LOD 400 models, BIM coordination and clash resolution, shop drawings, panel and device layouts, cable and termination schedules, material take-offs, and as-built documentation.
Coordinate system interfaces between life safety, electrical, telecom, HVAC, Building Management and Facility Management Systems, access control, elevator systems, process systems, and other building infrastructures, including sequencing with cleanroom protocol levels and energized equipment access restrictions.
Manage quality surveillance activities, ITP implementation, inspections, special inspections, megger and continuity testing, integrated systems testing, performance and reliability testing, commissioning activities, and final acceptance testing.
Monitor subcontractor safety performance with particular attention to energized work, arc flash boundaries, lockout/tagout, and confined space and elevated work, along with workforce planning, material management, procurement status, construction progress, schedule adherence, and execution risks in compliance with project ES&H requirements.
Validate subcontractor installed quantities, monthly progress payments, invoices, and force account and time reports, and coordinate RFIs, technical clarifications, design conflicts, field changes, nonconformance resolution, punch list closure, and turnover documentation requirements.
Manage and coordinate Subcontractor Construction Work Packages (CWPs) and subcontract-specific Condition Reports, including creation of Corrective Action Plans and participation in causal (apparent and root) analysis.
Education and Experience Requirements:
 
Level I: Requires bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Construction Management, or other relevant technical disciplines from an accredited University, plus a minimum of 5 years of relevant work experience; or 9 years of relevant work experience in lieu of a degree.
Level II:  Requires bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Construction Management, or other relevant technical disciplines from an accredited University, plus a minimum of 8 years of relevant work experience; or 12 years of relevant work experience in lieu of a degree.
Required Knowledge and Skills:
 
Basic Qualifications
Working knowledge of NFPA 70 (National Electrical Code), NFPA 72, Ohio Building and Fire Codes, IBC, AHJ permitting requirements, and UL-listed life safety equipment requirements as applicable to semiconductor manufacturing facilities.
Working knowledge of medium and high voltage cable termination practices, including manufacturer-certified installer requirements, cable testing methods, and energized work safety requirements per NFPA 70E.
Working knowledge of fiber optic installation and testing practices, including pull tension and bend radius limits, splicing methods, connector types, labeling and administration standards, and OTDR and insertion loss acceptance testing.
Ability to read and understand single-line diagrams, cable and termination schedules, P&ID’s, orthographics, plans, and other design drawings.
Working knowledge of applicable industry codes and standards is required. Excellent communication and problem-solving ability.
Understanding of applicable Bechtel work processes including Standard Work Process Procedures is preferred.
Computer literate in word processing, spreadsheet, and database applications.
Must be physically able to conduct field inspections and participate in project walk-downs which may require the following activities: extensive walking in and around a construction site, climbing ladders, climbing scaffolding, using fall protection and other personal protective equipment (PPE), walking on elevated platforms, walking on uneven surfaces, and maneuvering around very small and/or confined spaces.
Required Knowledge and skills: (Cont.)
 
Preferred Qualifications
Experience in semiconductor fabrication facilities is preferred, including familiarity with toxic gas monitoring, HPM handling areas, and cleanroom protocol level work restrictions.
Proficient level of understanding of NFPA 70, NFPA 70E, NFPA 72, IEEE 400 and 404 cable testing and accessory standards, TIA-568 and TIA-569 telecommunications standards, IBC, and applicable Ohio codes.
Experience overseeing design-build subcontracts for PLC-based detection and alarm systems, including factory acceptance testing and sequence of operations validation.
Familiarity with Bechtel Standard Applications (BSAPs), including TEAMWorks, Aconex, DSCS, Unifier, Agile, Navisworks, and other automation tools used on Bechtel projects.
Proficiency in Navisworks Simulate and 3D model navigation is preferred.
Previous experience as a Subcontract Technical Representative or Quality Control Representative, including experience managing construction subcontracts and field design changes.

Project Overview:
 
Bechtel is building a semiconductor manufacturing plant in New Albany, Ohio. We are partnering with the North America Building Trades Unions and suppliers to create several thousand new jobs and work with local education organizations to implement new training programs that will support the future talent pipeline. Bechtel Manufacturing & Technology, Inc. offers engineering, procurement, and construction services for customers in the semiconductor manufacturing, electric vehicle, and data center markets. Headquartered in Reston, Virginia, the M&T global business unit also includes colleagues working in Arizona, Ohio, Texas, India, and additional project locations around the world. 
Job Summary:
 
In this position, you will be responsible for the organization and direction of piping field engineering personnel and activities across the project, providing technical leadership for all above and below ground piping work and serving as the engineering liaison to the design functional group. You will interpret design drawings and specifications, supervise field verification of materials, and provide technical direction to piping field engineers and superintendents. The Lead Piping Field Engineer provides project field engineering specialization and expertise with work planning and packaging, material management, quantity verification and validation, safety and quality control, technical inspection and testing, and subcontract coordination, ensuring field engineering activities operate safely, are complete, and conform to quality standards and project requirements.
The successful applicant will work closely with superintendents and direct hire craft to ensure full compliance of the assigned scope of work, and will coordinate with other discipline leads across the Fab, support buildings, utility facilities, and underground scopes.
Major Responsibilities:
 
Provide technical and administrative direction to assigned subordinate piping field engineers, and provide technical assistance to the piping superintendents and crafts.
Establish a Design/Field Engineering working relationship and lines of communication with the Project Engineer, including agreement on engineering deliverables, and coordinate with engineering on constructability and design issues.
Direct the implementation of the project ES&H program and quality control program within the piping discipline, and develop and implement Inspection and Test Plans for major piping activities.
Oversee inspection of field installations and completion of associated documentation on a continuing basis, and ensure final P&ID checks are completed prior to turnover.
Direct the development of pressure test packages and the witnessing, verification, and acceptance of hydrostatic and pneumatic testing, flushing, and cleanliness verification.
Responsible for quantity take-off, control, reporting, and forecasting for all piping quantities, and direct the preparation of cost estimates for piping construction activities.
Direct the development of piping work packages in conjunction with supervision, and assist supervision and project controls in the preparation of detailed work plans and short-term schedules.
Review and provide input to project controls documents on progress relating to cost and schedule, and coordinate the interfacing between the construction automation plan and the project controls program at the jobsite.
Interpret design drawings and interface with the engineering office to resolve design and constructability issues, and direct the preparation of field change documentation and as-built documentation as required.
Direct the preparation of requisitions for field procured materials, material substitution, services, and equipment, and approve requisitions as delegated by the Project Field Engineer.
Major Responsibilities(Contd.):
 
Work with suppliers to ensure compliance with project drawings and specifications, coordinate and review vendor drawings, and work with Procurement's expediting team to ensure delivery of vendor materials to support the project schedule.
Review material and receiving reports and warehousing to ensure delivery of correct materials, complete material receipt inspections as required, and ensure materials are stored properly to ensure environmental protection and preservation of piping components.
Work within TEAMWorks to verify accurate data from engineering and suppliers, and direct the maintenance of construction engineering records for job history, including the receiving, distribution, and filing of plans and specifications.
Develop and ensure implementation of the project construction procedures from the Standard Work Process Procedures (SWPPs), coordinate any deviations from SWPPs, and coordinate with superintendents and subcontractors to plan construction schedules.
Coordinate subcontract activities to ensure materials, equipment, and quality comply with design plans and specifications, and plan and recommend procedures to be implemented by superintendents to ensure construction operations are within the requirements of engineering design and specifications.
Work closely with other discipline field engineers and coordinate efforts and activities to meet project requirements, including coordination with cleanroom protocol level restrictions and turnover system boundaries.
Education and Experience Requirements:
 
Requires bachelor's degree (or international equivalent) and 8-10 years of relevant experience or 12-14 years of relevant work experience.
Required Knowledge and Skills:
 
Basic Qualifications
Proficient level of understanding of mechanical piping systems, connections, and components, including above and below ground installation methods.
Ability to read and understand isometrics, P&ID’s, orthographics, plans, and other design drawings.
Familiarity with ASME B31.3 and applicable welding, examination, and pressure testing requirements.
Technical knowledge of all phases of construction engineering relating to the piping discipline while interfacing with all areas of the project, and thorough knowledge of construction activities as they relate to engineering disciplines, cost and scheduling, and contract administration.
Knowledge of the use of subcontracts and of the contractor and subcontractor responsibilities contained in subcontract documents, with prior experience supervising and administering subcontractors.
Knowledge and understanding of the application and requirements of the Project Environmental, Safety, & Health (ES&H) Handbook, Bechtel Core Processes, project-specific environmental compliance requirements, and Bechtel’s “Zero Accidents” safety program. Familiarity with Bechtel’s Business Ethics handbook and policies.
Understanding of applicable Bechtel work processes including Standard Work Process Procedures is preferred.
Working knowledge of applicable industry codes and standards is required. Excellent communication and problem-solving ability.
Computer literate in word processing, spreadsheet, and database applications.
Work includes field inspections and the physical ability to conduct field inspections which require the following activities: extensive walking in and around a construction site, climbing ladders, climbing scaffolding, working on elevated platforms, working on uneven surfaces, and working in small or confined spaces.
Required Knowledge and Skills(Contd.):
 
Preferred Qualifications
Experience in semiconductor fabrication facilities, including process piping, high purity systems, and specialty gas and chemical distribution, is preferred.
Prior experience leading a discipline field engineering team on a large-scale direct hire and subcontracted construction project.
Familiarity with Bechtel Standard Applications (BSAPs), including TEAMWorks, Aconex, DSCS, Unifier, Agile, Navisworks, and other automation tools used on Bechtel projects.
Proficiency in Navisworks Simulate and 3D model navigation is preferred.
Experience with Advanced Work Packaging and construction work package development is preferred.

Project Overview:
 
Bechtel is partnering with NextDecade to support their vision to provide the world access to lower carbon intensive energy with their Rio Grande LNG (RGLNG) project in Brownsville, Texas. RGLNG is a natural gas liquefaction and export terminal situated on a 984-acre site on the banks of the Brownsville ship channel. The first phase of the RGLNG project consists of three liquefaction trains, two storage tanks and one marine berth. At full capacity, the five-train facility will have a production capacity of 27 million tonnes per annum (MTPA). 
Brownsville, Texas is a city known for its diverse history, tradition, and rich culture. Located in the southernmost region in the beautiful state of Texas, lays Brownsville a rich, tropical oasis bordering the Rio Grande River and near the shores of the Gulf of Mexico. Brownsville embraces innovation, looks forward to the future and beyond! 
Job Summary:
 
The LOTO Tagging Authority (TA) will report to the Lead LOTO Tagging Authority and is responsible for receiving and acting on requests to perform work on components or systems that are energized or have the potential to be energized. The TA will be responsible for energy isolation management in accordance with corporate and project specific procedures. Must be willing to work a flexible schedule if required, including, but not limited to nightshift, split shift, or day shift. 
 #LI-SP1
Major Responsibilities:
 
Manage the integrated LOTO program on the Project coordinating between subcontractors, JV partners, and all other affected entities to deliver a safe and uniform program for the control of work and isolation of hazardous sources of energy.
Ensure the energy isolation program complies with SWPP’s, STCP’s, and Q4Safety.
Use Q4Safety for electronic Energy Isolation Permits (EIP’s).
Provide input and support to the Construction, Operations, and Commissioning teams, in piping, mechanical, and electrical isolations.
Identify isolation boundaries based on work scope and develop and issue EIP’s.
Administer and manage the energy isolation program with strict enforcement and record keeping.
Perform other duties as directed in support of project activities.
Coordinate activities with other disciplines or areas and client representatives.
Maintain the training program and register on the project related to EIP’s.
Procure material required to support the energy isolation management program.
Monitors the activities of subcontractors to ensure compliance with energy isolation.
Problem resolution and inspection of EIP’s.
Monitor the installation of LOTO equipment such as Locks and Tags etc.
Work hours as required, including overtime, weekends, and holidays, as necessary to support the project.
Education and Experience Requirements:
 
Requires bachelor's degree (or international equivalent) and 5-8 years of relevant experience or 9-12 years of relevant work experience
Required Knowledge and Skills:
 
Construction experience assigned to a construction site.
Heavy industrial direct hire construction experience.
Experience in oil, gas, refinery, petrochemical, minerals processing, or power generating station construction.
Knowledge of engineering and construction methods and processes customarily acquired over time through specialized instruction or practical experience.
Demonstrated ability to motivate and lead team members effectively & positively in a collaborative team environment.
Demonstrated ability to problem-solve in high pressure situations.
Computer literate in word processing and spreadsheet and database applications.
Preferred: Experience on an LNG construction site especially along the U.S. Gulf Coast.
Preferred: Understanding of applicable Bechtel processes including Standard Work Process Procedures.
Preferred: Advanced knowledge of Project Bechtel Standard Applications (BSAPs) including Setroute, Unifier, Aconex, DSCS, PTR, Agile, Navisworks, and other automation tools which are used on Bechtel projects.
Experience managing technical services subcontracts.
Additional Information:
Work requires the physical ability to conduct field inspections including but not limited to: extensive walking in and around a construction site often in high heat and high humidity conditions, climbing ladders, climbing scaffolding, working on elevated platforms, working on uneven surfaces, and working in small or confined spaces. Some lifting may be required. 
Must have the ability to walk into and out of the project (enter/egress). 
Must be able to use appropriate standard issued Personal Protection Equipment (PPE) required for each assigned task (i.e. harness, life vest, lift buckets, etc.).

Project Overview:
 
The project is a 1.3 GW simple-cycle power generation facility located in Millersport, Ohio, being constructed adjacent to a hyperscale data center campus. The facility includes multiple power generation technologies consisting of Solar Titan 130 gas turbines, Siemens SGT800 gas turbines, reciprocating engines, battery energy storage systems (BESS), substations, and associated balance of plant infrastructure.
 
The scope includes major civil, mechanical, electrical, structural, underground utility, control systems, and commissioning works required to support phased energization and turnover of the facility. Construction will be executed through a combination of direct hire and subcontracted labor supported by modularization, pre-assembly, offsite warehousing, and advanced work packaging methodologies.
Job Summary:
 
In this role, you will lead, implement, and maintain global construction field welding programs and provide specialized welding engineering support. You will manage, inspect, and monitor the welding test lab, the rod room, the weld heat treatment program, and the laboratory quality plan. Your technical advice will help ensure defects, behaviors, and other issues are rectified prior to final inspection.
 #LI-BH1 
Major Responsibilities:
 
Coordinates work activities for Project Field Engineer and the Lead Field Welding Engineer in implementing the site welding program on medium sized projects.
Implements and maintains Bechtel Field Welding program or all welding operations.
Provides specialized welding engineering support for construction to ensure construction meets all code, client/engineering specifications and Bechtel procedures and standards.
Assists in the management of the pre- and post-weld heat treatment program.
Assists in the management of the rod room and rod room attendant to ensure all weld filler materials are controlled so to meet Bechtel, Code, and Client requirements.
Schedules and coordinates NDE with construction and subcontractors for the most efficient NDE schedule at the least cost and least impact to construction.
Works with the team to review and keep up to date with weld documents and ensures the credibility/accountability of the Welding Program.
Performs field inspections of welding work, and advises on rectification of quality behaviors and defects prior to final inspection
May be responsible for the implementation and leads the subcontractors and direct hire Pre/PWHT program.
May be responsible for the implementation and management of the Welder Performance Qualifcation program. 
Education and Experience Requirements:
 
Requires bachelor's degree (or international equivalent) and 5-8 years of relevant experience or 9-12 years of relevant work experience​
Required Knowledge and Skills:
 
NDE Certs including VT, PT, and MT.
Knowledge of AWS, API, NFPA, AWWA, ASTM and ASNT codes, specifications, and standards.
Heavy industrial direct hire construction experience commensurate with the type of work to be undertaken.
Advanced knowledge and/or certifications in SMAW / GTAW / GMAW / FCAW.
Intermediate understanding of Preheat/Post weld heat treatment of equipment and consumables.
Knowledge of engineering and construction methods and processes customarily acquired over time through specialized instruction or practical experience.
Demonstrated ability to problem-solve in high pressure situations.
Must be certifiable by written examination to Bechtel's nondestructive examination requirements as NDE Level II Visual Examination.
Knowledge and understanding of Bechtel's SWPP 4MP-T81-03701 Welding Program, 03708 Pre/Post Weld Heat Treatment and 03705 Welding & NDE Documentation.
Familiarity with Bechtel Standard Applications (BSAPs) including Unifier, Aconex, DSCS, PTR, Agile, Navisworks, WITs, Teamwork’s, Arc Stryker, Pipe Fighter, and other automation tools which are used on Bechtel projects.
 
Work includes field inspections and the physical ability to conduct field inspections which require the following activities: extensive walking in and around a construction site often in high heat and high humidity conditions, climbing ladders, climbing scaffolding, working on elevated platforms, working on uneven surfaces and working in small or confined spaces. Some lifting may be required. Must have the ability to walk into and out of the project (enter/egress). Must be able to use appropriate standard issued Personal Protection Equipment (PPE) required for each assigned task (i.e. harness, life vest, lift buckets, etc.).

Job Summary:
 
In this role, you will provide project field engineering support with work planning and packaging, material management, quantity verification and validation, safety and quality control, technical inspection and testing knowledge, and coordination of system turnover. #LI-BH1
Major Responsibilities:
 
Assist the PFE in the establishment, implementation and maintenance of various field engineering and construction programs
Maintain project document control and ensure all work activities are executed using the latest versions of relevant documents
Work with the area and discipline superintendents to develop detailed, integrated installation plans for complex, cross discipline installations
Ensure that work package generation by field engineers supports the construction schedule
Prioritize work for the multi-discipline team of field engineers within the assigned area (Civil/Structural, Mechanical, Piping, Electrical, Instrumentation and Marine) and provide day to day direction and supervision
Work with Area superintendent to ensure that quantities are reported, verified and submitted for all commodities each week Assist with the development and implementation of Inspection and Test Plans (ITP’s)
Perform quality control inspections of completed work and generate associated documentation
Ensure that all project quality requirements are understood and adhered to Liaise with the design engineering group and provide support to resolve design and constructability issues
Assist subordinate responsible field engineers within generation of Field Change Documentation Develop the technical sections of field subcontracts
Work with supervision to perform front-end work package scoping
Develop construction progress reports and quantity forecasts
Ensure that field engineers complete required material requisitions to ensure that material deliveries support scheduled activities and complete material receipt inspections
Monitor field costs and assist in cost forecasts
Assist in the preparation and updating of construction schedules Ensure correct preparation of applicable as-built documents and inspections required by the contract
Perform system/area turnovers Conduct annual goal setting/performance reviews and quarterly feedback discussion with assigned field engineers  
Education and Experience Requirements:

Project Overview:
 
Louisiana LNG is located approximately 11 miles southwest of Lake Charles, Louisiana. The project includes a mid-scale, mixed-refrigerant Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) production and export facility on the west side of the Calcasieu River. There are five identical process plants. Project Overview:
 
Bechtel is partnering with NextDecade to support their vision to provide the world access to lower carbon intensive energy with their Rio Grande LNG (RGLNG) project in Brownsville, Texas. RGLNG is a natural gas liquefaction and export terminal situated on a 984-acre site on the banks of the Brownsville ship channel. The first phase of the RGLNG project consists of three liquefaction trains, two storage tanks and one marine berth. At full capacity, the five-train facility will have a production capacity of 27 million tonnes per annum (MTPA). Brownsville, Texas is a city known for its diverse history, tradition, and rich culture. Located in the southernmost region in the beautiful state of Texas, lays Brownsville a rich, tropical oasis bordering the Rio Grande River and near the shores of the Gulf of Mexico. Brownsville embraces innovation, looks forward to the future and beyond!
Job Summary:
 
In this role, you will lead, implement, and maintain global construction field welding programs and provide specialized welding engineering support. You will manage, inspect, and monitor the welding test lab, the rod room, the weld heat treatment program, and the laboratory quality plan. Your technical advice will help ensure defects, behaviors, and other issues are rectified prior to final inspection. 
#LI-BH1
Major Responsibilities:
 
Coordinates work activities for Project Field Engineer and the Lead Field Welding engineer in implementing the site welding program on large projects. 
Implements and maintains Bechtel Field Welding program for all welding operations.
Provides technical assistance to field superintendents and crafts.
Ensures that all supervision and craft personnel involved in welding operations are educated and aware of applicable code and project requirements.
Provides welding engineering support to ensure construction meets all code and Bechtel procedures.
Provides technical expertise for ASME, API, and AWS or other code designed and fabricated items.
Coordinates pre- and post-weld heat treatment program whether self- performed by Bechtel or subcontracted.
Coordinates rod room and rod room attendant to ensure all weld filler materials are controlled and meet Bechtel and Code requirements.
Assists in the management of the NDE subcontract, including scheduling and coordination between construction and subcontractor.
Coordinates the welder qualification lab to ensure high quality welders are being employed.
Works with craft to maintain welding documentation and ensure the credibility/accountability of the Welding Program.
Supports the field inspections of welding work to ensure workmanship and materials are in conformance with project requirements.
Advises on recertification of quality behaviors and defects prior to final inspection.
Implements the project quality control program for welding.
Responsible for the requisitioning and set up of the welding consumables program.
Assists field procurement in inspection and receipt of welding materials.
Implements weld inspection tracking system using TEAMWorks/WITS applications. 
May be responsible for the implementation and coordination of subcontractors and direct hire Pre/PWHT program.  
Additional Responsibilities:
 
Working knowledge of mechanical/piping engineering principles in the design and installation of structures, systems, and components.
Strong ability to read, understand and interpret structural/mechanical/piping/electrical construction drawings.
Technical knowledge of a specialized engineering discipline, cost, scheduling and contracts administration relating to the construction of heavy industrial or commercial complexes.
Strong understanding of module assembly, completion walk-downs, testing, punch list management, turn over packages and routine interface with Start-Up.
Knowledge of requirements for Lock Out Tag Out for safety.
Education and Experience Requirements:
 
Requires bachelor's degree (or international equivalent) and 8-10 years of relevant experience or 12-14 years of relevant work experience​
 
Required Knowledge and Skills:
 
Candidates should be self-starters, highly motivated, requiring little supervision, and able to work well in a team environment.
Knowledge of current design Knowledge of current codes and standards such as AMSE, API, AWS, and NFPA.
Knowledge of welding technical and practical applications such as SMAW, GTAW, GMAW STT.
Knowledge of Preheat/Post Weld Heat Treatments, equipment, and consumables.
Excellent oral and written communication skills.
A sound knowledge base of environmental, safety and health compliance standards required on government projects.
Ability to provide clear and precise verbal and written communications with design engineers in order to assist with the project review.
Mechanical/Piping system construction installation and inspection experience.
Required Knowledge and Skills: (Cont)
 
Computer literate in word processing, spreadsheet, and database applications in accordance with current Bechtel standards.
Working knowledge of Bechtel Construction automation systems (e.g., TeamWorks, InfoWorks, WITS, etc).
Ability to interface with diverse construction disciplines as well as all levels of management.                                                                                                                                                                 
A basic knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite applications such as Word, Excel, Teams, etc.
Working knowledge of Bechtel standard programs used on Bechtel EPC projects is preferred (e.g., SmartPlant design tools, Digital Supply Chain, Synchro 4D, Navisworks, xFighters, PowerBI, BookBuilder, SetRoute, Construction Unifier, and EQMS).              
Recent Bechtel experience as a Welding/Mechanical/Piping Field Engineer or Lead Welding/Mechanical/Piping Field Engineer at a large EPC Project.
Working knowledge of the Bechtel Standard Work Processes Procedures (*SWPPs) and the related Bechtel Standard application Programs (BSAPs) utilized by Construction

Night Shift position but must be willing to work a flexible schedule as required that may include but not limited to split shift. Project Overview:
 
Port Arthur LNG, LLC (PALNG) is developing a Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) production and export facility on a site located on the western shoreline of the Port Arthur Canal in Jefferson County, Texas. The project base scope will include two (2) identical LNG trains, two (2) LNG Storage Tanks, one (1) LNG Carrier Berth, and associated utilities/facilities. The Project is to be constructed on a parcel of land located along State Highway 87 south of Port Arthur, Texas, between the inner coastal waterway bridge and Keith Lake. The Infrastructure Global Business Unit (GBU) is executing site civil and marine scopes of work associated with our scopes of work on the Energy GBU LNG projects. As the #1 LNG EPC contractor by installed capacity, Bechtel has the capability to successfully deliver a broad range of LNG projects through our integrated EPC self-perform model, strategic partnerships, and proven experience in LNG project delivery. Partnering with Bechtel means lower cost, shorter delivery schedules, and greater certainty of outcomes for our customers.

New York, New York, United States · Posted: 2026-10-16T17:32:38-04:00

Job description
About the Positions

We’re seeking 
Construction Managers
 to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. You’ll oversee an assigned construction package or group of contracts from preconstruction through closeout, hold the work to the contract documents, and keep cost, schedule, quality, and safety visible so field issues get resolved before they turn into claims.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. 
We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Note: We are seeking candidates of various skill levels, and the following responsibilities represent the core of these roles. Scope and complexity increase with experience level.

Oversee contractor performance across an assigned construction package or group of contracts from preconstruction through closeout, and hold the work to the plans, specifications, and contract requirements.

Administer the construction contract, including submittals, requests for information, notices, and correspondence, and keep the record complete enough to stand up under audit and claim review.

Evaluate change proposals and contractor pricing for entitlement, technical merit, cost impact, and schedule impact, and recommend a position the program can act on.

Review baseline and update schedules for critical path, logic, and sequencing, and quantify the effect of delays and changes on the contract completion date.

Coordinate the program’s inspection, materials testing, and quality assurance staff, and verify that installed work and submitted quantities match approved documents before payment.

Quality Manager
New York, New York, United States · Posted: 2026-09-10T11:05:53-04:00
Comp: Salary: $110k-$185k/year ($53-$89/hour)
Job description
About the Positions

We’re seeking 
Quality Managers
 to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. These positions run the quality assurance program. You’ll set the standard, audit whether committed quality control plans are actually being followed, and make sure nonconformances get closed instead of carried. Luster’s own quality management system is ISO 9001:2015 certified, so the framework you work inside is audited rather than sitting in a binder.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. 
We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Develop and maintain the quality management system for the program, including the quality manual, procedures, and forms, aligned to ISO 9001:2015 and the program’s contract requirements.

Review the quality control plans and inspection and test plans submitted by designers and contractors, and confirm they meet contract requirements before the work they cover begins.

Audit designer and quality control programs against their own approved plans, and report whether the program is being followed in practice rather than only documented.

Oversee nonconformance reporting from identification through disposition, corrective action, and verified closure, and keep the log current and visible to the program team.

Verify that materials testing, special inspection, and independent assurance testing are performed by qualified laboratories and personnel, and that results stay traceable to the work they cover.

Coordinate quality surveillance across every discipline on your assigned program so one standard applies to all of the work.

Evaluate design quality by reviewing the designer’s own checking and quality control records, and confirm submittals arrive for review with those checks complete.

May lead root cause analysis on recurring defects and rework, and drive corrective and preventive actions to closure so the same problem does not come back.

Analyze quality performance data and report audit status, trends, and open nonconformances to program leadership.

Deliver quality orientation and training to program staff, designers, and personnel so requirements are understood before the work is in place.

Coordinate quality requirements through procurement, construction, testing, commissioning, and turnover, and confirm the record documentation supports acceptance and closeout.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering, construction management, construction engineering, or quality management, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

10+ years of quality management experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Experience developing and administering quality management system documentation aligned to ISO 9001:2015, including quality plans, procedures, and audit programs.

Experience leading quality assurance audits and driving nonconformances and corrective actions to documented closure.

Experience reading construction drawings, specifications, and industry codes such as ASTM, ACI, and AWS.

Experience with industry standard quality and project management information software (e.g., Kahua, Unifier, e-Builder, Primavera P6, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in civil engineering, construction management, construction engineering, or quality management.

Active professional certifications such as ISO 9001:2015 Lead Auditor, CQA or CQE (ASQ), and/or Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt.

Experience leading the owner’s quality assurance function on a program exceeding $1B in construction value.

Experience standing up a program quality management system in a new program office, including the quality manual, the procedure set, and the audit schedule.

Experience auditing a contractor’s or designer’s quality control program and holding that organization to its own approved plan.

Experience overseeing quality across more than one sector on the same program, such as roadway, structures, trackwork, airfield, or water and wastewater facilities.

Experience overseeing materials testing and special inspection programs, including laboratory qualification and independent assurance testing.

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Compensation Details

Expected Salary: $110k-$185k/year ($53-$89/hour). Luster provides the salary range that the company in good faith believes it might offer for this position based on the successful candidate’s level and years of experience, knowledge, skills, abilities, education, certifications, licenses, geographic location, etc. Luster reserves the right to ultimately pay more or less than the posted range depending on circumstances not related to any status protected by local, state, and/or federal law.

Job description
About the Positions

We’re seeking 
Quality Managers
 to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. These positions run the quality assurance program. You’ll set the standard, audit whether committed quality control plans are actually being followed, and make sure nonconformances get closed instead of carried. Luster’s own quality management system is ISO 9001:2015 certified, so the framework you work inside is audited rather than sitting in a binder.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. 
We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Develop and maintain the quality management system for the program, including the quality manual, procedures, and forms, aligned to ISO 9001:2015 and the program’s contract requirements.

Review the quality control plans and inspection and test plans submitted by designers and contractors, and confirm they meet contract requirements before the work they cover begins.

Audit designer and quality control programs against their own approved plans, and report whether the program is being followed in practice rather than only documented.

Oversee nonconformance reporting from identification through disposition, corrective action, and verified closure, and keep the log current and visible to the program team.

Verify that materials testing, special inspection, and independent assurance testing are performed by qualified laboratories and personnel, and that results stay traceable to the work they cover.

Coordinate quality surveillance across every discipline on your assigned program so one standard applies to all of the work.

Evaluate design quality by reviewing the designer’s own checking and quality control records, and confirm submittals arrive for review with those checks complete.

May lead root cause analysis on recurring defects and rework, and drive corrective and preventive actions to closure so the same problem does not come back.

Analyze quality performance data and report audit status, trends, and open nonconformances to program leadership.

Deliver quality orientation and training to program staff, designers, and personnel so requirements are understood before the work is in place.

Coordinate quality requirements through procurement, construction, testing, commissioning, and turnover, and confirm the record documentation supports acceptance and closeout.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering, construction management, construction engineering, or quality management, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

Active OSHA-10 certification.

5+ years of quality management experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Experience developing and administering quality management system documentation aligned to ISO 9001:2015, including quality plans, procedures, and audit programs.

Experience leading quality assurance audits and driving nonconformances and corrective actions to documented closure.

Experience reading construction drawings, specifications, and industry codes such as ASTM, ACI, and AWS.

Experience with industry standard quality and project management information software (e.g., Kahua, Unifier, e-Builder, Primavera P6, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in civil engineering, construction management, construction engineering, or quality management.

Active professional certifications such as ISO 9001:2015 Lead Auditor, CQA or CQE (ASQ), and/or Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt.

Experience leading the owner’s quality assurance function on a program exceeding $1B in construction value.

Experience standing up a program quality management system in a new program office, including the quality manual, the procedure set, and the audit schedule.

Experience auditing a contractor’s or designer’s quality control program and holding that organization to its own approved plan.

Experience overseeing quality across more than one sector on the same program, such as roadway, structures, trackwork, airfield, or water and wastewater facilities.

Experience overseeing materials testing and special inspection programs, including laboratory qualification and independent assurance testing.

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Job description
About the Positions

We’re seeking 
Resident Engineers
 of various skill levels to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. These positions run the field office on an assigned construction contract, administering the contract, overseeing inspection staff, and enforcing what the plans and specifications require. The record you build behind every determination is what holds up when a change or a claim surfaces months later.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. 
We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Note: We are seeking candidates of various skill levels, and the following responsibilities represent the core of these roles. Scope and complexity increase with experience level.

Administer construction contracts in the field, holding the contractor to the plans, specifications, and contract requirements across assigned work areas.

Oversee inspection staff and daily field coverage, and hold inspection assignments and daily documentation to the program’s standards.

Serve as the program’s focal point for correspondence with the contractor, and coordinate formal responses with agency staff and the designer of record.

Review and process submittals, requests for information, and shop drawings, and coordinate technical responses with the design team.

Evaluate progress against the schedule, verify installed quantities against approved documents, and recommend progress payments.

Analyze change requests, potential change orders, and claims, and develop independent cost and schedule positions that support the program’s determination.

Oversee quality assurance activities and materials testing coordination, and track nonconformances through documented resolution.

Monitor contractor compliance with site safety requirements and permit conditions, and support incident reporting and corrective action.

Coordinate with designers, utility owners, railroads, airport and transit operations groups, and adjacent contracts to resolve field conflicts before they reach the schedule.

Maintain complete construction records, daily reports, correspondence, and as-built documentation in the program’s project management information system so the program’s position holds up under audit and claim review.

May lead progress meetings, and coordinate punch list development, testing and commissioning oversight, substantial completion, and closeout documentation.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering, construction management, construction engineering, or engineering technology, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

5+ years of construction management, resident engineering, or construction engineering and inspection experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Experience administering construction contracts in the field, including submittals, requests for information, change management, and progress payments.

Experience overseeing inspection staff and field documentation on an active construction site.

Working knowledge of construction means and methods, contract administration practices, quality assurance, and field documentation standards.

Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and construction schedules.

Experience with industry standard project / construction management software (e.g., Primavera P6, Unifier, Kahua, e-Builder, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in civil engineering, construction management, construction engineering, or engineering technology.

Active professional certifications and licenses such as PE, CCM (CMAA), and/or OSHA 30-Hour Construction (OSHA).

Experience serving as the owner’s resident engineer on a construction contract exceeding $100M in construction value.

Experience supporting programs valued at $1B+, or transportation megaprograms exceeding $10B.

Experience overseeing construction across more than one sector, such as transit guideway, station, and trackwork; airfield runway, taxiway, or terminal work; bridge and structures work; water and wastewater facilities; or highway and roadway work.

Experience with federally funded construction and the associated documentation and reporting requirements.

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Job description
About the Positions

We’re seeking 
Construction Inspectors
 of various skill levels to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. We hire across civil and structural, mechanical and plumbing, and electrical inspection, so we are looking for real depth in one of them rather than all of them. Your focus is field verification. You’ll confirm that installed work matches the approved plans and specifications, document what happens on site every day, and catch problems while they are still cheap to fix.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. 
We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Note: We are seeking candidates of various skill levels, and the following responsibilities represent the core of these roles. Scope and complexity increase with experience level.

Inspect installed work for conformance with approved plans, specifications, permits, codes, and contract quality requirements.

Document daily construction activity, including labor, equipment, materials, quantities, weather, and progress photographs.

Verify materials on delivery against approved submittals, certifications, and product data, and reject nonconforming material.

Coordinate and witness field and laboratory testing, and track results, deficiencies, and corrective actions to closure.

Identify and report nonconforming work, safety concerns, and design conflicts to the resident engineer promptly, and confirm correction.

Measure and record pay quantities so payment covers only work actually installed and accepted.

Verify survey layout checks and as-built documentation against approved plans.

Monitor traffic control, work zone, and site safety requirements within the assigned work area, and report deviations.

Coordinate inspection coverage with contractors, utility owners, agency staff, and third parties during active construction operations.

Inspect work staged around live operations so verification happens without interrupting service.

Support punch list development, testing and startup verification, and closeout documentation.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in construction management, engineering technology, civil engineering, or construction engineering, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

5+ years of construction inspection experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Experience inspecting one or more of the following: civil and structural construction (earthwork, grading, drainage, utilities, foundations, concrete, and structures); mechanical and plumbing systems (HVAC, piping, pumps, and plumbing rough-in and finish); or electrical construction (conduit, cable, terminations, grounding, lighting, panels, and power distribution).

Working knowledge of construction means and methods, applicable codes and standards, and materials testing and acceptance practices.

Experience preparing daily inspection reports, quantity records, and nonconformance documentation.

Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, specifications, submittals, and shop drawings.

Experience with industry standard field reporting and document management software (e.g., Kahua, Unifier, e-Builder, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in construction management, engineering technology, civil engineering, or construction engineering.

Active professional certifications such as OSHA 30-Hour Construction (OSHA), ICC certifications, NICET Level III or IV, ACI Concrete Field Testing Technician Grade I (ACI), and/or CWI (AWS).

Experience serving as lead inspector on a construction package exceeding $100M in construction value.

Experience inspecting work on a capital program exceeding $1B in total value where coverage spanned multiple active contracts.

Experience inspecting multiple disciplines or systems on the same program, such as building, electrical, mechanical, or utility work.

Experience inspecting construction on transit corridors, airport airside or terminal areas, or water and wastewater treatment facilities kept in service during the work.

Experience with industry standard inspection management software (e.g., Procore, Autodesk Construction Cloud, SharePoint-based systems, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Expected Salary: $85k-$150k/year ($41-$72/hour). About the Positions

We’re seeking 
Construction Inspectors
 of various skill levels to support large, complex transit capital programs, including light rail and bus corridors, stations, tunnels, elevated guideway, trackwork, and rail systems, delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. These roles verify that installed work conforms to the contract documents, submittals, requests for information, and applicable codes and design standards, and produce the daily field record that the project relies on when quantities, changes, and claims are settled. We hire across the core inspection disciplines, including civil and structural, building, electrical, mechanical, utility, and roofing inspection, as well as safety and security representatives.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Inspect construction activities for conformance with the contract documents, submittals, requests for information, approved shop drawings, and applicable codes and design standards.

Prepare accurate and legible daily inspection reports covering contractor labor, equipment, materials, quantities installed, weather, delays, safety observations, and work locations.

Identify nonconforming work and report it to the resident engineer and the inspection quality assurance lead at the moment it is observed, and document it in the daily report.

Verify materials on delivery against submittals, certifications, mix designs, and delivery tickets, and confirm proper storage and handling.

Witness and document field sampling and materials testing, and track results, deficiencies, and retests through closure.

Measure and record pay quantities supporting progress payments, and photograph and log field conditions to support quantity verification and change review.

Monitor contractor compliance with approved traffic control, work zone safety, environmental, and erosion and sediment control requirements.

Coordinate daily inspection coverage with the resident engineer and the owner’s construction management staff against the approved staffing plan.

Support survey verification, punch list development, substantial completion walkthroughs, and closeout documentation.

Coordinate with contractor personnel, design teams, utility owners, and third-party stakeholders during active construction operations.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in construction management, engineering technology, civil engineering, or construction engineering, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

Active OSHA-30 certification.

5+ years of construction inspection experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Inspection experience in at least one core discipline: civil and structural, building, electrical, mechanical, utility, or roofing inspection, or documented service as a safety and security representative.

Inspection experience on light rail, commuter rail, or bus rapid transit capital programs.

Experience inspecting multiple disciplines on the same program.

Experience inspecting within an active rail or transit operating environment.

Document Control Manager

Job description
About the Positions

We’re seeking 
Document Control Managers
 to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. These positions own the program record: the systems, procedures, and controls that keep every drawing, submittal, RFI, and piece of correspondence current, traceable, and defensible. When an audit, a claim, or a funding review lands two years after the fact, what you built is what the program stands on.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. 
We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Note: We are seeking candidates of various skill levels, and the following responsibilities represent the core of these roles. Scope and complexity increase with experience level.

May lead the document control function across the program, including direction of assigned document control staff and allocation of that workload across contracts, phases, and field offices.

Develop and maintain the program’s document control procedures, numbering and naming conventions, revision control, and retention schedules, and hold contractors, designers, and internal teams to them.

Administer the enterprise document management system, including permissions, workflow configuration, metadata structure, and issue resolution, so the system stays the single authoritative record.

Oversee the intake, logging, distribution, and closeout of submittals, RFIs, correspondence, and design deliverables in the system of record.

Keep the register accurate enough that turnaround can be measured and defended.

Verify that the current approved revision of drawings, specifications, and other controlled documents is the version in use across the program team, the field offices, and any shared platform.

Coordinate document flow across active work areas and the contract packages they support.

Monitor and report document control metrics, including submittal turnaround, RFI aging, overdue reviews, and open action items, and escalate what is at risk before it affects schedule or payment.

Prepare program records for internal and external audits, respond to findings from quality audits, agency reviews, and funding reviews, and drive corrective actions to closure.

Train program personnel and onboard incoming contractor and consultant staff on the program’s document control procedures and system use.

Coordinate with project management, design, construction, contracts, legal, and quality teams so document workflows support contract administration, entitlement, and public records obligations.

Oversee turnover and closeout documentation, including record drawing sets, warranties, permits, and archives, and confirm the record transfers complete and indexed.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in construction management, engineering, information management, or project management, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

10+ years of document control experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Experience leading a document control function or team on an active design or construction program, including procedure development and direction of staff.

Working knowledge of construction and program documents, including drawings, specifications, submittals, RFIs, correspondence, and record documents.

Working knowledge of ISO 9001-based document control requirements, including revision control, retention, traceability, and audit readiness.

Experience with industry standard document management and project / construction management software (e.g., SharePoint, e-Builder, Aconex, Primavera P6, Unifier, Kahua, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in construction management, engineering, information management, or project management.

Active professional certifications such as CRM or CRA (ICRM), ISO 9001:2015 internal auditor or lead auditor training, and/or PMP (PMI).

Experience leading the owner’s document control function on a program valued at $1B+.

Experience standing up document control at the start of a program, including system selection, configuration, and migration of legacy records.

Experience producing document records for public records requests, claims, disputes, or litigation holds.

Experience supervising and developing document control staff across multiple contracts or field offices.

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Compensation Details

Expected Salary: $110k-$175k/year ($53-$84/hour).
