Construction Cost Manager, NA Design & Construction Governance, Global Engineering Services, GEMS D&C, Cost Management
US, WA, Bellevue · Posted: June 2, 2026 — no longer listed as of 2026-10-28
Comp: Not listed
Job description
The NA Design & Construction (D&C) Cost Management team within Global Engineering Services (GES) is seeking a passionate and motivated Construction Cost Manager to manage and support a portfolio of industrial construction projects in North America. In this role, you will drive cost certainty across multiple projects, reporting on overall financial health to organizational leaders and cross-functional stakeholders. Working independently and with cross-functional teams, you will execute cost management frameworks, validate project financials, and contribute to cost management best practices across the program.
This is an individual contributor role that operates with moderate autonomy on defined workstreams, seeking guidance from the Cost Management Manager on strategic direction while independently managing day-to-day cost functions across assigned projects. 
This role requires approximately 25% regional travel within North America, with potential travel to all North America locations based on business needs.
Key job responsibilities
Cost Management & Governance
•	Execute end-to-end cost management functions aligned, including cost planning, cost control, cost forecasting, and cost reporting across multiple assigned projects.
•	Maintain compliance with Amazon's internal cost management governance standards, including cost authority thresholds, approval workflows, and financial delegation of authority.
Budget Management & Cost Controls
•	Track and report cost performance metrics 
•	Implement and maintain cost control processes including cost baselines, work breakdown structures, and cost breakdown structures.
•	Create and maintain processes for timely cost variance identification and escalation per established thresholds.
•	Review, analyze, and challenge cost and time change requests from external partners 
•	Contingency  management and monthly cost reporting leveraging internal data and tools with a bias toward automation.
Change Management 
•	Strong fundamental understanding of end-to-end change control process management (receipt, evaluation, negotiation, disposition) with the ability to drive a standardized process leveraging AACE standards.
•	Ability to develop and review change order logs, commitment registers, and produce audit-trail documentation
•	Working with construction managers, support in the action of reviewing and validating change orders including proposed costs, scope of work, and comparison with contractual terms.
External Partner & Stakeholder Management
•	Develop strong partnerships with Construction Managers, Preconstruction Managers, Design, Procurement, Finance, and Operations teams.
•	Align cost reporting and estimating deliverables with external project managers, architects, general contractors, and consultants.
•	Independently identify project risks including financial cost impacts and communicate to the Cost Management Manager and cross-functional partners.
Communication & Reporting
•	Contribute to daily, weekly, and monthly cost reports with a bias toward automation.
•	Communicate cost metrics, trends, and recommendations effectively (verbal and written) to cross-functional teams and senior stakeholders.
Data Analytics & Technology
•	Explore and implement generative AI and automation tools to accelerate cost estimating, change order analysis, variance reporting, and lessons-learned extraction.
•	Strong fundamentals on cost management platforms (e.g., Procore, Ecosys, Oracle Unifier, or equivalent) and advanced Excel capabilities (Power Query, pivot tables, array formulas, macros) for cost tracking and analysis.
A day in the life
As a Construction Cost Manager, you will primarily work with Construction Managers and act as a strategic advisor on all cost functions across multiple projects. You will independently manage cost tracking, change order validation, and financial reporting for your assigned portfolio while collaborating with Finance, Planning, and Design teams to predict project costs at a network level. With an attention to diving deep, you will support financial white papers with data and analysis, identify cost savings opportunities, and drive process improvements within your workstream. You will make trade-offs between time, quality, and resources on your assigned projects, escalating strategic decisions to your manager as appropriate.

- Proficiency with cost management software, scheduling tools (Primavera P6, MS Project, or similar), and advanced Excel
- Experience using data analytics to identify trends, drive and support process improvements, and inform strategic decisions through metrics and KPIs.

- Master's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Quantity Surveying, Business, or related field
- Experience across multiple construction disciplines (civil, structural, mechanical, electrical)
- Professional certifications: CCP (Certified Cost Professional), CCE (Certified Cost Engineer), PMP (Project Management Professional), MRICS/FRICS, EVP (Earned Value Professional), or equivalent

Job Summary:
 
The Construction Automation Specialist supports the day-to-day operation, setup, and maintenance of Construction Automation systems on an assigned construction project. This role provides hands-on support for digital tools, workflows, and field-related technology used by construction, project controls, ES&H, commissioning, and other project teams. Working under the direction of the Construction Automation Lead, the Construction Automation Specialist focuses on system setup, user support, troubleshooting, and maintaining reliable Construction Automation operations in an active construction environment.
 #LI-SM2
Major Responsibilities:
 
Configure, administer, and support TEAMWorks and related project applications. 
Coordinate the collection, validation, maintenance, and reporting of construction and engineering data. 
Support systemization, work packaging, turnover management, commissioning, and project progress reporting activities. 
Monitor data quality and collaborate with stakeholders to resolve discrepancies and improve data integrity. 
Develop and distribute reports, dashboards, and progress tracking tools to support project execution and management decision-making. 
Support integrations and interfaces between TEAMWorks  and other project systems as required. 
Provide day-to-day user support, troubleshooting, onboarding, and training for project personnel and contractors. 
Work directly with field personnel, supervisors, engineers, and CSU teams to ensure successful adoption and effective use of TEAMWorks application. 
Document business processes, procedures, lessons learned, and best practices. 
Participate in testing and validation of application updates, enhancements, and new functionality. Identify opportunities to improve workflows, reporting, data quality, and overall project efficiency. 
Support project turnover and system handover activities through accurate tracking, reporting, and completion management. 
Education and Experience Requirements:
 
Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Engineering Technology, Information Systems, Business, or a related field. Equivalent experience will be considered. 
Five or more years of experience supporting construction, commissioning, startup, turnover, quality, project controls, or related project execution activities. 
Experience administering SetRoute  , construction processes, commissioning, construction management, or project information management systems. Understanding construction, system turnover, CSU processes, work packaging, turnover planning, and project reporting. 
Experience working with project data, reporting tools, dashboards, analytics, and business applications.
Required Knowledge and Skills:
 
Experience supporting major capital EPC projects in the semiconductor, pharmaceutical, battery, data center, or other industrial sectors. 
Experience supporting commissioning, startup, turnover, and system handover activities. 
Familiarity with construction and project delivery platforms such as TEAMWorks, SetRoute, Unifier, Procore, or similar systems. 
Experience with SQL, SSRS, Databricks, data validation, dashboard development, data integration, and project analytics. 
Prior experience supporting field-based construction technology or digital project execution systems. 
Strong organizational, communication, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills. 
Ability to build relationships and work effectively with construction, commissioning, engineering, quality, project controls, and contractor personnel. 
Ability to support and train users while collaborating effectively with multidisciplinary project teams. 
Strong attention to detail with a focus on data accuracy and quality. 
Self-motivated and adaptable in a fast-paced project environment. 
Full-time assignment at an active construction project site in New Albany, Ohio. 
Requires daily on-site presence and direct support of project teams in both office and field environments. 
Significant time may be spent walking around the project site and supporting construction and commissioning activities in the field. 
Requires the ability to work in outdoor conditions and active construction environments. 
This position is not eligible for telework, remote work, or visa sponsorship.

Job description
About the Position

We’re seeking a 
Construction Manager
 to support a large, complex, heavy-civil rail infrastructure program. This role will be responsible for strategically directing and overseeing construction-related activities, ensuring alignment from pre-construction through delivery.

This is a long-term, full-time, on-site position located in the greater San Francisco Bay Area, CA.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Own the constructability strategy, identifying construction-related challenges and resolutions early in the process and continually throughout all phases.

Serve as the accountable lead for construction input to design activities and milestones.

Lead construction oversight across multiple contracts using a mix of delivery methods, spanning early works, specialty and heavy civil construction, systems installation, and facility fit-out phases.

Lead, oversee, and coordinate construction management services.

Ensure the people, processes, and verification protocols are in place so that the built project is consistent with contractual requirements.

Lead and develop direct reports across construction contract management teams, setting expectations, allocating resources, and building bench strength as the program scales.

Coordinate with engineering, project controls, procurement, right of way, safety, and quality teams to align construction sequencing with program schedule, budget, and risk priorities.

Support federal, state, regional, and local oversight requirements, including third-party project management oversight reviews and reporting.

Elevate construction risks, trends, and mitigation strategies to program leadership, and support the resolution of changes, claims, and disputes.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Ability to manage multiple contracts and scopes simultaneously.

Ability to engage and coordinate effectively across integrated delivery teams and with various stakeholders.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering, construction management, or architecture, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

10+ years' experience in successfully managing and overseeing large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil rail infrastructure projects.

Demonstrated experience leading construction management on transit, rail, or comparable heavy-civil programs, including tunneling, track and systems, and station or facility construction.

Demonstrated experience working within alternative delivery models.

Experience managing multiple concurrent construction contracts and scopes across design, procurement, and construction phases.

In-depth understanding of constructability principles, construction risk mitigation, and the verification protocols that confirm built work meets contractual requirements.

Experience providing construction input to design activities and milestones during pre-construction.

Experience leading and developing construction management staff, including direct reports across multi-disciplinary teams.

Experience with industry standard project / construction management software (e.g., Primavera P6, MS Project, Unifier, Kahua, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in civil engineering, construction management, or architecture.

Professional Engineer (PE) license or equivalent.

Certified Construction Manager (CCM), Project Management Professional (PMP), or Architect Registration (AIA).

Experience on federally funded transportation projects, including FTA Project Management Oversight (PMO/PMOC) requirements.

Experience delivering construction in dense urban environments with active rail, utility, and public right-of-way constraints.

Experience working within integrated delivery teams.

Experience with tunneling, deep excavation, or underground rail construction.

Experience leading or supporting various phases of the construction lifecycle, including utility relocation, site clearing, and demolition.

Familiarity or proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Expected Salary: $160k-$200k/year ($77-$96/hour). Job description
Requisition ID: 299159

Extraordinary teams building inspiring projects:
 
Since 1898, we have helped customers complete more than 25,000 projects in 160 countries on all seven continents that have created jobs, grown economies, improved the resiliency of the world's infrastructure, increased access to energy, resources, and vital services, and made the world a safer, cleaner place. 
 
Differentiated by the quality of our people and our relentless drive to deliver the most successful outcomes, we align our capabilities to our customers' objectives to create a lasting positive impact. We serve the Infrastructure; Nuclear, Security & Environmental; Energy; Mining & Metals, and the Manufacturing and Technology markets. Our services span from initial planning and investment, through start-up and operations. 
Core to Bechtel is our 
Vision, Values and Commitments
. They are what we believe, what customers can expect, and how we deliver. Learn more about our 
extraordinary teams building inspiring projects
 in our 
Impact Report
. 
Project Overview:
 
Louisiana LNG is located approximately 11 miles southwest of Lake Charles, Louisiana. The project includes a mid-scale, mixed-refrigerant Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) production and export facility on the west side of the Calcasieu River. There are five identical process plants. Each process plant consists of one gas pre-treatment unit, one condensate stabilization unit, and four Chart heavy hydrocarbon (HHC) removal and liquefaction groups. The facility will include associated utilities, refrigerant storage, three 235,000m3 full-containment LNG storage tanks, and three marine berths.
Job Summary:
 
In this role, you will lead construction automation efforts for complex projects, using database management, programming skills, and 3D tools. You will establish and administer the portfolio of construction automation applications on the jobsite and data requirements. You will review performance and recommend adjustments to tailor solutions to support strategy and compliance. 
#LI-BH1
Major Responsibilities:
 
The Construction Automation Engineer is responsible for establishing and administering the suite of Construction Automation applications. This includes, but is not limited to, the following applications: Unifier, PowerApps, AI – enabled solutions, TEAMWorks, SetRoute, WITS (Weld and Welder tracking system), Smart Completions, SSRS, Bechtel Productivity Services (BPS) (Xfighters), AWP Tools and DCS/ MAP.
Maintain existing and create new Unifier and Power Apps Workflows.
Work with the Project Team to establish the requirements for Construction Automation Systems to support construction work processes.
Coordinate with design engineering, supply chain, project controls, and other departments to establish automated data transfer between applications.
Configure BSAPs and other applications to meet project requirements.
Understand reporting requirements for each application and configure reports accordingly. Ensure reports are accurate and functioning as intended.
Review/trouble-shoot data for accuracy and completeness. Identify and address anomalies.
Provide ongoing administration to each BSAP.
Provide training and technical support to end users, including field engineering, supervision, administration, project controls, and other site personnel.
Interface with corporate BSAP administrators to change functionality or configuration of applications to meet project specific requirements.
Education and Experience Requirements:
 
Requires bachelor's degree (or international equivalent) and 5-8 years of relevant experience or 9-12 years of relevant work experience
Required Knowledge and Skills:
 
Knowledge of engineering and construction methods and processes customarily acquired over time through specialized instruction and practical experience is required.
Extensive knowledge of Unifier and linking Unifier to Bechtel BSAPs and other applications is required.
Extensive knowledge of Power Apps and linking Power Apps to Bechtel BSAPs and other applications is required.
Extensive knowledge of TEAMWorks and associated applications used for data integrity and reporting is required.
Experience with other Bechtel Standard applications, including but not limited to SETROUTE and DSCS/EBS required.
A good understanding of Bechtel standard construction work processes and procedures required.
Advanced level capability of databases is required.
Bechtel Direct Hire Construction experience is preferred.
Excellent communication and problem-solving ability.
Additional Information: 
Work requires the physical ability to conduct field inspections including but not limited to: extensive walking in and around a construction site often in high heat and high humidity conditions, climbing ladders, climbing scaffolding, working on elevated platforms, working on uneven surfaces, and working in small or confined spaces. Some lifting may be required. Must have the ability to walk into and out of the project (enter/egress). Must be able to use appropriate standard issued Personal Protection Equipment (PPE) required for each assigned task (i.e. harness, life vest, lift buckets, etc.).

PMIS Configuration Consultant
Phoenix, Arizona, United States · Posted: 2026-09-22T15:33:35-04:00 — no longer listed as of 2026-10-28
Comp: Salary: $130k-$160k/year ($63-$77/hour)
Job description
About the Positions

We’re seeking 
PMIS Configuration Consultants
 to configure, implement, and support project management information systems on large-scale, heavy-civil infrastructure programs across highways, roads and bridges, transit (rail and bus), aviation, and water sectors. You’ll build out PMIS modules for budget, cost, schedule, risk, and reporting, and partner with project controls teams to keep program data structured, accurate, and audit ready.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. 
We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.
 While we are currently targeting the Phoenix area, we welcome and will consider qualified candidates from anywhere in the continental United States. These positions require up to 50% travel.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Note: We are seeking candidates of various skill levels, and the following responsibilities represent the core of these roles. Scope and complexity increase with experience level.

Configure PMIS processes for budget, cost, change orders, payments, risk, issues, cash flow, and earned value to support project controls, project management, and program management functions.

Configure security roles, user access, and integrations between PMIS platforms, scheduling systems, document management systems, and ERP systems.

Configure cash flow, earned value, and other modules within the PMIS solution.

Identify and correct inconsistencies in data structures, coding, and hierarchy across project controls systems.

Develop and maintain data models that support integrated reporting across cost, schedule, and performance metrics, and drive continuous improvement of data structures, reporting processes, and data quality across the program.

Develop project reports and dashboards aligned with client and program reporting requirements.

Automate data extraction, transformation, and reconciliation across PMIS and integrated systems using SQL and/or Python.

Reconcile and validate data across multiple reporting systems to maintain accuracy and consistency.

Collaborate with project controls managers, cost engineers, and schedulers to ensure data structures support program controls requirements.

Support end-user training and knowledge transfer on deployed PMIS configurations, workflows, and reporting tools.

Attributes

Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical project data into clear reporting for program leadership and stakeholders.

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret complex datasets and identify meaningful insights.

High attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy.

Ability to manage multiple data sources and competing reporting deadlines across large, complex programs.

Collaborative mindset that supports project controls managers, cost engineers, and schedulers in achieving shared reporting goals.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, computer science, construction management, business administration (management information systems), data analytics, statistics, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

3+ years’ experience implementing, integrating, and configuring software systems, preferably Unifier, P6, Kahua, or Procore.

Experience configuring business processes, workflows, security roles, and user access within an enterprise software platform.

Experience building and maintaining integrations between enterprise systems, including work with APIs, authentication, and structured data formats such as JSON, XML, and CSV.

Proficiency with SQL and Python, including the use of Python to automate data extraction, transformation, reconciliation, and system-to-system integration.

Experience performing advanced data manipulation, transformation, and structuring of large datasets, beyond basic reporting or dashboarding.

Experience working with hierarchical data structures such as work breakdown structures (WBS), cost breakdown structures (CBS), chart of accounts, or similar multi-level coding frameworks.

Experience integrating, reconciling, and normalizing data across multiple systems, such as scheduling, cost, and financial systems.

Experience improving data quality, hierarchy, and alignment across systems when working with incomplete, inconsistent, or poorly structured datasets.

Experience developing reports and dashboards aligned with stakeholder and organizational reporting requirements.

Proficiency with Microsoft Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in engineering, computer science, construction management, business administration (management information systems), data analytics, or statistics.

PMP (PMI), CCM (CMAA), MRICS/FRICS (RICS), or CCA (AACE).

Experience supporting project controls, data, or reporting functions on large, complex infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (rail or bus), aviation, or water/wastewater projects, typically involving multi-contract delivery and integrated reporting requirements.

Understanding of project controls processes and their relationships to budget, schedule, risk, and governance on large capital programs.

Experience integrating PMIS or enterprise platforms via API with analytics platforms or AI-assisted reporting tools, including familiarity with applicable cybersecurity governance requirements.

Experience developing Python-based integrations in a production environment, including scheduled execution, error handling, logging, and documentation.

Experience operating within a Center of Excellence model, including development of templates, processes, and governance that support efficient configuration and delivery.

Experience supporting integrated cost and schedule reporting, including earned value or similar performance frameworks.

Experience supporting project controls or program management on infrastructure programs exceeding $500M in value.

Familiarity or proficiency with Microsoft Power BI.

Compensation Details

Expected Salary: $130k-$160k/year ($63-$77/hour). Utility Coordinator
San Francisco, California, United States · Posted: 2026-09-23T11:52:40-04:00 — no longer listed as of 2026-10-28
Comp: Salary: $115k-$165k/year ($55-$79/hour)
Job description
About the Position

We’re seeking a 
Utility Coordinator
 to support a large, complex, heavy-civil rail infrastructure program. This role will be responsible for identifying utility conflicts within the project corridor and coordinating with public and private utility owners to resolve them before they affect design or construction, keeping utility clearance aligned with the program’s overall schedule.

This is a long-term, full-time, onsite position located in the greater San Francisco Bay Area, CA.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Identify existing utilities and coordinate new installations, developing strategies to resolve conflicts before they affect design or construction.

Coordinate with public and private utility owners to confirm ownership, records, and relocation requirements, and negotiate utility agreements, cost responsibility, and reimbursement terms with project leadership and legal counsel.

Maintain the utility conflict matrix, driving each conflict to a documented clearance decision, and track relocation schedules against committed dates, escalating slippage before it reaches the critical path.

Prepare utility permit applications and confirm that utility coordination and design conform to accommodation policies, right of way requirements, and environmental regulations.

Review design plans, construction documents, and record drawings to identify conflicts and route them for resolution, and support construction teams during field investigations and relocations.

Coordinate subsurface utility engineering work and utility activities in dense urban corridors, including closure and outage windows.

Maintain detailed coordination records, correspondence, and approvals to support payment, audit, and claim review.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Communicate verbally and formally the status of coordination activities to keep the project delivery team and external stakeholders informed regarding utilities.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering, construction management, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

6+ years of experience in utility coordination, preferably on transportation infrastructure projects, including coordinating with public and private utility owners to resolve conflicts and tracking them through documented clearance.

Knowledge of utility systems (water, sewer, gas, electric, and telecommunications), utility accommodation policies, right of way requirements, easements, property rights, and environmental regulations as they apply to utility coordination and design.

Ability to read and interpret plans, profiles, construction documents, and utility record drawings well enough to identify conflicts and route them for resolution.

Proficiency with utility mapping and plan review tools (e.g., Esri ArcGIS, Autodesk AutoCAD Civil 3D, Bluebeam Revu).

Proficiency with industry standard project/construction management software (e.g., Primavera P6, MS Project, Unifier, Kahua).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in civil engineering or construction management.

Active professional certifications such as Certified Utility Coordination Professional (CUCP) and/or Project Management Professional (PMP).

8+ years of experience in utility coordination on transportation infrastructure projects.

Experience with large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects that include highways, roads, bridges, transit (including rail and bus), and/or airport projects.

Experience coordinating utility relocations in a dense urban corridor with overlapping municipal, transit, and private utility ownership.

Experience negotiating utility agreements, betterment splits, and reimbursement schedules directly with investor-owned utilities and municipal utility departments.

Experience coordinating utility work on design-build, CM/GC, progressive design-build, or other alternative delivery programs exceeding $100M in construction value.

Familiarity with owner’s representative, program management, or construction management utility coordination practices.

Working knowledge of subsurface utility engineering quality levels under ASCE 38 and how to scope a subsurface utility engineering investigation.

Experience with industry standard utility conflict tracking and program management software (e.g., Kahua, Unifier, Primavera P6, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Senior Principal Consultant/Consulting Technical Manager
United States · Posted: 2026-10-02 — no longer listed as of 2026-10-28
Comp: Not listed
Job description
U.S. Citizenship Required:
 This position supports projects with specific access and/or contractual requirements. As a result, U.S. citizenship is required for consideration for this role.

Job Description

Oracle’s Construction and Engineering Global Business Unit (CEGBU) focuses on project-intensive industries such as engineering and construction, aerospace and defense, utilities, oil and gas, chemicals, industrial manufacturing, automotive, financial services, communications, travel and transportation, healthcare; state, local and federal government.

The CEGBU has numerous products that support Enterprise Project Portfolio Management software such as Unifier, P6, Aconex, OPPM and Oracle Primavera Cloud (formerly Prime) that encompasses resource allocation, cost reduction, supply-chain efficiency, and decision-making―using real-time data, for the enterprise market.

 

The Technical Architect will be involved in solution design, implementation, deployment, maintenance and documentation of Project Integrated Framework (PIF) interfaces. PIF is an integration framework used to integrate CEGBU products with external applications like SAP, EBS etc. PIF interfaces can also be used for P6/Unifier data consolidation and data migrations. 

This responsibility includes interacting with clients/internal stake holders at all levels to understand the business requirements to conclude the blueprint, configuration, testing, migration, support and continuous enhancements of the integration framework.

The position operating independently with some assistance and guidance to provide quality work products to a project team or customer that comply with Oracle methodologies and practices. Performs standard duties and tasks with some variation to implement Oracle products and technology to meet customer specifications.
Standard assignments are accomplished without assistance by exercising independent judgment, within defined policies and processes, to deliver functional and technical solutions on moderately complex customer engagements.

 

Education:

Bachelor of Science Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field

 

Experience:

12+ years of customer facing or consulting experience in Primavera domain.

10+ years of overall experience in architecting integrations using PIF or 
any one of the integrations middleware like MuleSoft, Dell Boomi, OIC and etc

Hands on experience in Primavera product suits like Unifier, P6 EPPM, Oracle Primavera Cloud and Aconex.

Ability to communicate effectively and build rapport with team members and clients. 

Enterprise Software implementation experience working for a software company.

Thorough knowledge of the software development life cycle

Previous systems (integration) experience with Oracle Products and other systems.

Excellent communication & coaching skills.

Luster NationalTier C controls mentions Unifier
Change Manager
Los Angeles, California, United States · Posted: 2026-10-16T17:15:42-04:00 — no longer listed as of 2026-10-28
Comp: Salary: $125k-$200k/year ($60-$96/hour)
Job description
About the Positions

We’re seeking 
Change Managers
 to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. You’ll support the change control process, develop the independent analysis that tests submitted entitlement, cost, and time, keep the scope, cost, schedule, and technical baselines accurate and traceable, and give program leadership a defensible position before money moves, on assignments ranging from a single contract package to a program-level change function.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. 
We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Note: We are seeking candidates of various skill levels, and the following responsibilities represent the core of these roles. Scope and complexity increase with experience level.

Support the program’s change control process from early identification through entitlement determination, pricing, negotiation, and executed change order.

Track every change notice and open change item in the log to a documented decision within the timeframes the contract allows.

Evaluate change proposals, requests for equitable adjustment, and claims for contractual entitlement, and recommend a position supported by the contract language and the factual record.

Develop and review independent cost estimates and time impact analyses that test contractor-submitted pricing and delay claims rather than accepting the submitted numbers.

Coordinate with the estimators, schedulers, and analysts supporting change evaluation, and apply a consistent approach to how changes are analyzed, priced, and documented.

Prepare change board packages that carry the recommendation, the independent analysis, the funding source, and the consequence of not acting, and present them to program decision-makers.

Support negotiation of change order value and time extensions alongside the contracting officer or contract administrator, and document what was agreed and what was released.

Process approved change orders through the contract, and confirm each one is reflected in the contract value, the baseline schedule, the budget, and the affected drawings and specifications.

Coordinate change evaluation with the program’s engineering, inspection, right of way, and operations groups.

Evaluate impacts to active operations and existing facilities before a change is approved.

Analyze differing site conditions, design changes, and third-party-driven changes on bridges, underground work, and systems, and separate what the contract already covers from what it does not.

Report change trends, open change exposure, and pending time extensions to executive program leadership so cost and schedule risk is visible before it lands.

Maintain configuration control of the change record and the affected technical documentation, including version control, revision history, and audit trails.

Keep entitlement decisions, pricing basis, and correspondence retrievable for internal and external audit, funding review, and dispute resolution.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in construction management, civil engineering, construction engineering, or business administration, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

10+ years of construction change control, change order, or claims experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Experience leading the change control process on a construction contract package, including change identification, entitlement determination, pricing, executed change order, and coordination of the estimators, schedulers, and analysts who support change evaluation.

Experience evaluating change proposals, requests for equitable adjustment, or claims for entitlement, cost, and schedule impact, and recommending a position to the owner.

Experience developing or reviewing independent cost estimates and time impact analyses that test contractor-submitted pricing and delay claims.

Experience preparing change board or governance packages and presenting recommendations to owner decision-makers.

Working knowledge of public works contract provisions governing changes, differing site conditions, delays, and notice and claim requirements.

Experience with industry standard PMIS, document management, and CPM scheduling software (e.g., MS Project, Unifier, Kahua, e-Builder, Primavera P6, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in construction management, civil engineering, construction engineering, or business administration.

Active professional certifications such as CCM (CMAA), PMP (PMI), and/or CCP or CFCC (AACE).

Experience managing a program-level change control function across multiple contract packages, including supervising change analysts and standardizing how packages are evaluated.

Experience negotiating individual change orders exceeding $10M in value.

Experience leading the owner’s position on a claim through a dispute resolution board, mediation, or a formal claims process.

Experience analyzing delay and schedule impact on a CPM schedule, including concurrency and the difference between excusable and compensable delay.

Experience with industry standard estimating, cost analysis, and document markup software (e.g., HCSS HeavyBid, RSMeans, Bluebeam Revu, ProjectWise, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Compensation Details

Expected Salary: $125k-$200k/year ($60-$96/hour). Luster provides the salary range that the company in good faith believes it might offer for this position based on the successful candidate’s level and years of experience, knowledge, skills, abilities, education, certifications, licenses, geographic location, etc. Luster reserves the right to ultimately pay more or less than the posted range depending on circumstances not related to any status protected by local, state, and/or federal law.

Just LOOK at the Benefits We Offer!

Unlimited flexible time off

Paid holidays

Paid parental leave

Health, dental, and vision insurance

Flexible spending accounts (healthcare and dependent or elder care)

Long-term disability insurance

Short-term disability insurance

Life insurance and accidental death and dismemberment

401(k) plan with guaranteed employer contribution

Formal career planning and development program

$2,500 annually toward professional development

Wellness program with monthly wellness stipend

Company cell phone or cell phone plan reimbursement

Free personalized meal planning and nutrition support with a registered dietitian

Free personal financial planning services

Employee assistance program

Employee discounts

Employee referral bonus

Keep entitlement decisions, pricing basis, and correspondence retrievable for internal and external audit, funding review, and dispute resolution.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in construction management, civil engineering, construction engineering, or business administration, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

10+ years of construction change control, change order, or claims experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Experience leading the change control process on a construction contract package, including change identification, entitlement determination, pricing, executed change order, and coordination of the estimators, schedulers, and analysts who support change evaluation.

Experience evaluating change proposals, requests for equitable adjustment, or claims for entitlement, cost, and schedule impact, and recommending a position to the owner.

Experience developing or reviewing independent cost estimates and time impact analyses that test contractor-submitted pricing and delay claims.

Experience preparing change board or governance packages and presenting recommendations to owner decision-makers.

Working knowledge of public works contract provisions governing changes, differing site conditions, delays, and notice and claim requirements.

Experience with industry standard PMIS, document management, and CPM scheduling software (e.g., MS Project, Unifier, Kahua, e-Builder, Primavera P6, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in construction management, civil engineering, construction engineering, or business administration.

Active professional certifications such as CCM (CMAA), PMP (PMI), and/or CCP or CFCC (AACE).

Experience managing a program-level change control function across multiple contract packages, including supervising change analysts and standardizing how packages are evaluated.

Experience negotiating individual change orders exceeding $10M in value.

Experience leading the owner’s position on a claim through a dispute resolution board, mediation, or a formal claims process.

Experience analyzing delay and schedule impact on a CPM schedule, including concurrency and the difference between excusable and compensable delay.

Experience with industry standard estimating, cost analysis, and document markup software (e.g., HCSS HeavyBid, RSMeans, Bluebeam Revu, ProjectWise, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Construction Managers
 to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. You’ll oversee an assigned construction package or group of contracts from preconstruction through closeout, hold the work to the contract documents, and keep cost, schedule, quality, and safety visible so field issues get resolved before they turn into claims.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. 
We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Note: We are seeking candidates of various skill levels, and the following responsibilities represent the core of these roles. Scope and complexity increase with experience level.

Oversee contractor performance across an assigned construction package or group of contracts from preconstruction through closeout, and hold the work to the plans, specifications, and contract requirements.

Administer the construction contract, including submittals, requests for information, notices, and correspondence, and keep the record complete enough to stand up under audit and claim review.

Evaluate change proposals and contractor pricing for entitlement, technical merit, cost impact, and schedule impact, and recommend a position the program can act on.

Review baseline and update schedules for critical path, logic, and sequencing, and quantify the effect of delays and changes on the contract completion date.

Coordinate interfaces with utility owners, railroads, adjacent contracts, and airport or transit operations groups so construction phasing keeps facilities in service.

Document field conditions, directives, and determinations, and support the program’s response to notices of potential claim and dispute resolution.

Oversee closeout, including punch list resolution, record document and as-built turnover, warranty documentation, and support for commissioning and transition to operations and maintenance.

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Bachelor’s degree in construction management, civil engineering, construction engineering, or engineering technology, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

Experience administering construction contracts, including submittals, requests for information, change orders, and payment applications on publicly funded work.

Experience evaluating change proposals and contractor pricing for entitlement, cost impact, and schedule impact.

Ability to review CPM schedules for critical path, logic, and sequencing, and to assess the schedule effect of changes and delays.

Working knowledge of construction safety and quality assurance requirements on public infrastructure projects, including OSHA construction standards.

Experience with industry standard construction management and scheduling software (e.g., Primavera P6, MS Project, Unifier, Kahua, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in construction management, civil engineering, construction engineering, or engineering technology.

Active professional certifications and licenses such as CCM (CMAA), PMP (PMI), PE, and/or OSHA 30-Hour Construction (OSHA).

Experience serving as the owner’s lead construction manager on a package exceeding $100M in construction value.

Experience overseeing construction across multiple concurrent contracts or task orders on a program exceeding $1B in construction value.

Experience overseeing a highway, roadway, or bridge package, including structural work such as deep foundations, falsework, and girder erection.

Experience overseeing construction in an active rail transit corridor, on an operating airport, or at a water or wastewater treatment or conveyance facility.

Experience leading construction management and inspection staff on an owner’s program team, including inspector assignment and performance feedback.

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Contracts and Claims Specialist
Fresno, California, United States · Posted: 2026-10-16T17:36:26-04:00 — no longer listed as of 2026-10-28
Comp: Salary: $90k-$155k/year ($43-$75/hour)
Job description
About the Positions

We’re seeking 
Contracts and Claims Specialists
 of various skill levels to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. These are construction claims and disputes roles, meaning contract claims rather than insurance adjusting. You’ll evaluate claims and requests for equitable adjustment for entitlement and quantum, test claimed cost and time against the contract and the contemporaneous record, and develop a position that holds up in negotiation, in front of a dispute review board, and in whatever comes after that. Contract administration is part of the job, but the center of it is what happens when the parties stop agreeing.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. 
We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Note: We are seeking candidates of various skill levels, and the following responsibilities represent the core of these roles. Scope and complexity increase with experience level.

Analyze claims and notices of potential claim and lost productivity, and evaluate entitlement against the contract provisions that govern each one.

Evaluate requests for equitable adjustment and disputed change proposals for entitlement, merit, and cost reasonableness, and recommend a position supported by the record.

Review claimed costs, including labor, equipment, materials, extended field and home office overhead, and markup, against contract provisions, force account records, and submitted cost backup.

Identify unsupported, duplicated, or misclassified amounts.

Coordinate with scheduling staff to evaluate time impact analyses and time extension requests against the accepted baseline and the contemporaneous progress schedules.

Assemble the contemporaneous record behind each claim, pulling daily reports, correspondence, requests for information, submittals, inspection records, and meeting minutes into a package that supports the program’s position.

Verify that notices meet the timing and content requirements of the contract, and track responses so contractual response periods are met and the program’s defenses stay intact.

Develop independent cost estimates and quantity checks on roadway, structures, and utility work to test contractor pricing on disputed changes and claims.

Prepare claim position papers, findings of fact, and recommendations for program decision-makers, dispute review boards, and mediation or arbitration panels.

Support negotiation and settlement of disputed changes and claims by developing entitlement and quantum summaries, cost comparisons, and a documented basis of settlement.

Evaluate claims arising in active operating environments, including restricted service windows, access limits, and facility shutdowns.

Coordinate with counsel, claims consultants, project controls, and finance staff on claim strategy, document production, and responses to formal demands.

Track open claims and disputed exposure by contract for program leadership.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in construction management, civil engineering, quantity surveying, or finance, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

5+ years of contract administration and construction claims experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Experience analyzing or supporting claims, requests for equitable adjustment, or disputed change proposals for entitlement, cost, and schedule impact.

Working knowledge of standard construction contract terms and public agency contracting requirements, including notice, changes, differing site conditions, delay, and disputes provisions.

Ability to interpret construction contract documents, plans, specifications, and cost and schedule records, and to build an entitlement narrative from the contemporaneous record.

Experience with industry standard contract administration, document management, and CPM scheduling software (e.g., Unifier, Aconex, e-Builder, Primavera P6, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in construction management, civil engineering, quantity surveying, or finance.

Active professional certifications such as CPCM (NCMA), CCM (CMAA), and/or CCP or CFCC (AACE).

Experience serving as the owner’s lead analyst on a claim exceeding $10M in disputed value.

Experience supporting contract administration and claims on a package exceeding $100M in construction value.

Experience carrying a claim beyond the project level through a dispute review board, mediation, arbitration, or litigation, including document production and support to counsel.

Experience preparing or reviewing time impact analyses, as-planned versus as-built comparisons, or windows analyses supporting delay claims, including the treatment of concurrent delay.

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Compensation Details

Expected Salary: $90k-$155k/year ($43-$75/hour). Job description
About the Positions

We’re seeking 
Contracts and Claims Specialists
 of various skill levels to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. These are construction claims and disputes roles, meaning contract claims rather than insurance adjusting. You’ll evaluate claims and requests for equitable adjustment for entitlement and quantum, test claimed cost and time against the contract and the contemporaneous record, and develop a position that holds up in negotiation, in front of a dispute review board, and in whatever comes after that. Contract administration is part of the job, but the center of it is what happens when the parties stop agreeing.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. 
We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Note: We are seeking candidates of various skill levels, and the following responsibilities represent the core of these roles. Scope and complexity increase with experience level.

Analyze claims and notices of potential claim and lost productivity, and evaluate entitlement against the contract provisions that govern each one.

Evaluate requests for equitable adjustment and disputed change proposals for entitlement, merit, and cost reasonableness, and recommend a position supported by the record.

Review claimed costs, including labor, equipment, materials, extended field and home office overhead, and markup, against contract provisions, force account records, and submitted cost backup.

Identify unsupported, duplicated, or misclassified amounts.

Coordinate with scheduling staff to evaluate time impact analyses and time extension requests against the accepted baseline and the contemporaneous progress schedules.

Assemble the contemporaneous record behind each claim, pulling daily reports, correspondence, requests for information, submittals, inspection records, and meeting minutes into a package that supports the program’s position.

Verify that notices meet the timing and content requirements of the contract, and track responses so contractual response periods are met and the program’s defenses stay intact.

Develop independent cost estimates and quantity checks on roadway, structures, and utility work to test contractor pricing on disputed changes and claims.

Prepare claim position papers, findings of fact, and recommendations for program decision-makers, dispute review boards, and mediation or arbitration panels.

Support negotiation and settlement of disputed changes and claims by developing entitlement and quantum summaries, cost comparisons, and a documented basis of settlement.

Evaluate claims arising in active operating environments, including restricted service windows, access limits, and facility shutdowns.

Coordinate with counsel, claims consultants, project controls, and finance staff on claim strategy, document production, and responses to formal demands.

Track open claims and disputed exposure by contract for program leadership.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in construction management, civil engineering, quantity surveying, or finance, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

5+ years of contract administration and construction claims experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Experience analyzing or supporting claims, requests for equitable adjustment, or disputed change proposals for entitlement, cost, and schedule impact.

Working knowledge of standard construction contract terms and public agency contracting requirements, including notice, changes, differing site conditions, delay, and disputes provisions.

Ability to interpret construction contract documents, plans, specifications, and cost and schedule records, and to build an entitlement narrative from the contemporaneous record.

Experience with industry standard contract administration, document management, and CPM scheduling software (e.g., Unifier, Aconex, e-Builder, Primavera P6, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in construction management, civil engineering, quantity surveying, or finance.

Active professional certifications such as CPCM (NCMA), CCM (CMAA), and/or CCP or CFCC (AACE).

Experience serving as the owner’s lead analyst on a claim exceeding $10M in disputed value.

Experience supporting contract administration and claims on a package exceeding $100M in construction value.

Experience carrying a claim beyond the project level through a dispute review board, mediation, arbitration, or litigation, including document production and support to counsel.

Experience preparing or reviewing time impact analyses, as-planned versus as-built comparisons, or windows analyses supporting delay claims, including the treatment of concurrent delay.

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Compensation Details

Expected Salary: $90k-$155k/year ($43-$75/hour). Document Control Manager
San Francisco, California, United States · Posted: 2026-10-16T17:42:30-04:00 — no longer listed as of 2026-10-28
Comp: Salary: $110k-$175k/year ($53-$84/hour)
Job description
About the Positions

We’re seeking 
Document Control Managers
 to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. These positions own the program record: the systems, procedures, and controls that keep every drawing, submittal, RFI, and piece of correspondence current, traceable, and defensible. When an audit, a claim, or a funding review lands two years after the fact, what you built is what the program stands on.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. 
We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities
 
may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Note: We are seeking candidates of various skill levels, and the following responsibilities represent the core of these roles. Scope and complexity increase with experience level.

May lead the document control function across the program, including direction of assigned document control staff and allocation of that workload across contracts, phases, and field offices.

Develop and maintain the program’s document control procedures, numbering and naming conventions, revision control, and retention schedules, and hold contractors, designers, and internal teams to them.

Administer the enterprise document management system, including permissions, workflow configuration, metadata structure, and issue resolution, so the system stays the single authoritative record.

Oversee the intake, logging, distribution, and closeout of submittals, RFIs, correspondence, and design deliverables in the system of record.

Keep the register accurate enough that turnaround can be measured and defended.

Verify that the current approved revision of drawings, specifications, and other controlled documents is the version in use across the program team, the field offices, and any shared platform.

Coordinate document flow across active work areas and the contract packages they support.

Monitor and report document control metrics, including submittal turnaround, RFI aging, overdue reviews, and open action items, and escalate what is at risk before it affects schedule or payment.

Prepare program records for internal and external audits, respond to findings from quality audits, agency reviews, and funding reviews, and drive corrective actions to closure.

Train program personnel and onboard incoming contractor and consultant staff on the program’s document control procedures and system use.

Coordinate with project management, design, construction, contracts, legal, and quality teams so document workflows support contract administration, entitlement, and public records obligations.

Oversee turnover and closeout documentation, including record drawing sets, warranties, permits, and archives, and confirm the record transfers complete and indexed.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in construction management, engineering, information management, or project management, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

10+ years of document control experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Experience leading a document control function or team on an active design or construction program, including procedure development and direction of staff.

Working knowledge of construction and program documents, including drawings, specifications, submittals, RFIs, correspondence, and record documents.

Working knowledge of ISO 9001-based document control requirements, including revision control, retention, traceability, and audit readiness.

Experience with industry standard document management and project / construction management software (e.g., SharePoint, e-Builder, Aconex, Primavera P6, Unifier, Kahua, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in construction management, engineering, information management, or project management.

Active professional certifications such as CRM or CRA (ICRM), ISO 9001:2015 internal auditor or lead auditor training, and/or PMP (PMI).

Experience leading the owner’s document control function on a program valued at $1B+.

Experience standing up document control at the start of a program, including system selection, configuration, and migration of legacy records.

Experience producing document records for public records requests, claims, disputes, or litigation holds.

Experience supervising and developing document control staff across multiple contracts or field offices.

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Compensation Details

Expected Salary: $110k-$175k/year ($53-$84/hour). Luster provides the salary range that the company in good faith believes it might offer for this position based on the successful candidate’s level and years of experience, knowledge, skills, abilities, education, certifications, licenses, geographic location, etc. Luster reserves the right to ultimately pay more or less than the posted range depending on circumstances not related to any status protected by local, state, and/or federal law.

Develop and maintain the program’s document control procedures, numbering and naming conventions, revision control, and retention schedules, and hold contractors, designers, and internal teams to them.

Administer the enterprise document management system, including permissions, workflow configuration, metadata structure, and issue resolution, so the system stays the single authoritative record.

Oversee the intake, logging, distribution, and closeout of submittals, RFIs, correspondence, and design deliverables in the system of record.

Keep the register accurate enough that turnaround can be measured and defended.

Verify that the current approved revision of drawings, specifications, and other controlled documents is the version in use across the program team, the field offices, and any shared platform.

Coordinate document flow across active work areas and the contract packages they support.

Monitor and report document control metrics, including submittal turnaround, RFI aging, overdue reviews, and open action items, and escalate what is at risk before it affects schedule or payment.

Prepare program records for internal and external audits, respond to findings from quality audits, agency reviews, and funding reviews, and drive corrective actions to closure.

Train program personnel and onboard incoming contractor and consultant staff on the program’s document control procedures and system use.

Coordinate with project management, design, construction, contracts, legal, and quality teams so document workflows support contract administration, entitlement, and public records obligations.

Oversee turnover and closeout documentation, including record drawing sets, warranties, permits, and archives, and confirm the record transfers complete and indexed.

Attributes

Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in construction management, engineering, information management, or project management, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

10+ years of document control experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

Experience leading a document control function or team on an active design or construction program, including procedure development and direction of staff.

Working knowledge of construction and program documents, including drawings, specifications, submittals, RFIs, correspondence, and record documents.

Working knowledge of ISO 9001-based document control requirements, including revision control, retention, traceability, and audit readiness.

Experience with industry standard document management and project / construction management software (e.g., SharePoint, e-Builder, Aconex, Primavera P6, Unifier, Kahua, etc.).

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in construction management, engineering, information management, or project management.

Active professional certifications such as CRM or CRA (ICRM), ISO 9001:2015 internal auditor or lead auditor training, and/or PMP (PMI).

Experience leading the owner’s document control function on a program valued at $1B+.

Experience standing up document control at the start of a program, including system selection, configuration, and migration of legacy records.

Experience producing document records for public records requests, claims, disputes, or litigation holds.

Experience supervising and developing document control staff across multiple contracts or field offices.

Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

Compensation Details

Expected Salary: $110k-$175k/year ($53-$84/hour).
